Endowed with the fourteenth vowel and adorned with a bindu at its head—this single-syllable great vidyā has been taught by Padmayogin. (99)
All his worship and other rites are like those of Mahāgaṇapati;
however, the ritual placement on the hands and limbs is performed with one's own seed-syllable conjoined with the six long vowels.
Another variety of this [mantra] is as follows:
the wise man should constantly recite it beginning with Lakṣmī, or beginning with Kūrca, or beginning with Māyā;
or he should always recite it beginning with Kāma, or beginning with Vadhū-bīja, or beginning with Vāk.
Oṃ, likewise, [one should recite] the great vidyā beginning with Kara and so forth, preceded by its own seed-syllable. || 1 ||
And so it is said:
"O Dear One, the Great Vidyā consists of two syllables, and that of three syllables is joined with the Weapon;
the Vidyā consisting of four phonemes extends up to the Wife of Fire (Svāhā)."
This knowledge is a great knowledge, very difficult to obtain in the three worlds;
it directly bestows the four aims of human life and destroys even the greatest sins.
The worship and other rites for these [mantras] are to be performed like those for the Mahāgaṇapati mantra. (3)
Now, the mantras of Lakṣmī:
Next, I shall declare the mantras for the sake of Śrī, which bestow the fruits of fortune and prosperity, by whose mere sidelong glance even the three worlds flourish. (4)
The letter *va* mounted upon fire (*ra*), conjoined with the moon of the left eye (*i*)—this is the seed-syllable of the Goddess Śrī, which bestows the fruit of all desires. (5)

The procedure for its worship is as follows: having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties and ending with the *pīṭhanyāsa*, as described in the general manual of worship (*sāmānyapūjāpaddhati*), one should perform the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*.
One should place *namaḥ* to the sage Bhṛgu on the head, *namaḥ* to the Nivṛt-Gāyatrī metre on the mouth,
and *namaḥ* to the deity Śrī on the heart. Then, one should install the throne-powers (*pīṭhaśakti*) and the throne-mantra (*pīṭhamantra*) upon the filaments and in the center.
For example: Oṃ, obeisance to Vibhūti.
Likewise, [obeisance] to Unnati, Kānti, Sṛṣṭi, Kīrti, Sannati, Vyuṣṭi, and Utkṛṣṭi.
For the sake of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*);
and likewise in the *Nibandha*:
"Vibhūti, unnati, kānti, for the sake of splendor (*kānti*), sṛṣṭi, kīrti, and sannati."
Vyuṣṭi, utkṛṣṭi, and ṛddhi are declared to be the nine powers (navaśaktayaḥ). || 6 ||
Then, one should assign the seat with: *śrīṃ kamalāsanāya namaḥ*.
Then, the assignments for the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *śrāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*.
Śrīṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers; Śrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers;
Śraiṃ, huṃ to the two ring fingers.
*Śrauṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*;
*śraḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*. In this manner, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) with *śrāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*, and so forth.
And likewise in the Nibandha:
"One should fashion the limbs with the seed-syllable of Ramā joined with the long [vowel]. (7)
Then comes the meditation:
[one should visualize the goddess] resembling gold in her radiance,
[seated upon] four elephants like the Himalayan mountains, who have lifted with their trunks golden jars of nectar.

I bow to her who stands upon a lotus, being sprinkled by the goddess Śrī; she who bears a boon-granting gesture and a pair of fear-dispelling lotuses in her hands; who is radiant with a crown, and who is beautiful with the curve of her hips bound in silken garments.
Having meditated thus and performed worship with mental offerings, one should perform the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*).

Then, having performed the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*), and having worshipped the pedestal-mantras beginning with *vibhūti* and ending with the *mantra* in the filaments and in the center, one should fashion the form (*mūrti*) by means of the root mantra.

Having meditated again and performed the rites beginning with the invocation and ending with the offering of five handfuls of flowers, one should commence the worship of the deities of the enclosure (*āvaraṇapūjā*).
Namely:
having worshipped with "OṂ HRĪḤ, obeisance to the Heart," and so forth, in the filaments starting from the fire [direction], in the center, and in the cardinal directions;
then, in the petals of the directions starting from the east, [one worships] "OṂ VĀSUDEVĀYA NAMAH," and likewise—
To Saṅkarṣaṇa, to Pradyumna, and to Aniruddha. In the petals at the intermediate directions, starting from the southeast (Agni), [one offers] *oṃ* to Damaka, to Salila, to Guggulu, and to Kuruṇṭaka.
Then, to the right of the Goddess: *oṃ śaṅkhanidhaye namaḥ*, and likewise to Vasudhā; to the left: *oṃ padmanidhaye namaḥ*, and likewise to Vasumatī.
On the tips of the petals, starting from the east: *oṃ balākyai namaḥ*, and likewise to Vimalā and Kamalā.
One should worship Vanamālikā, Vibhīṣikā, Mālikā, Śāṅkarī, and Vasumālikā; outside of that, one should worship Indra and the other deities, as well as the Vajra and the other implements.
Then, one should complete the ritual actions from the offering of incense up to the final dismissal. || 9 ||
The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) for this consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations.
And so it is said:
"The initiated one, having conquered his senses, should recite the mantra one million times."
One should offer a thousand oblations with lotuses smeared with honey;
at the end of the recitation, the practitioner should offer oblations with sesame seeds soaked in honey,
or with bilva fruits, or with all three, O best of practitioners.
Following the mantras is the Vāgbhava [seed-syllable], then the Māyā of Viṣṇu, and the Makaraketana;
this four-syllabled mantra bestows the fruits of the four aims of human life. || 11 ||
His worship and so forth are to be understood as before. || 12 ||
And likewise: One should worship on a pedestal fashioned for Ramā according to its prescribed rite;
there, the best of practitioners should perform the ritual applications with the mantra.
He is constantly attended by personified treasures standing before him;
yet in his meditative absorption, there is a distinction: his radiance is like that of a ruby.
She who is constantly being sprinkled by four lofty elephants, white as snow, with water from jeweled jars held in their trunks;
she who, with her lotus-hands, bestows boons and displays the *abhaya* and *varada* gestures; the beloved of Hari—[I bow to her].
I bow to the one seated upon the lotus, who is the wish-fulfilling *parijāta* creeper.
The preliminary practice (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations (japa).
And so it is said:
"One who eats sacrificial food (haviṣya) should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times for each sun (bhānu), and at the conclusion, [offer worship] with lotuses."
One who has conquered the senses should offer a thousand oblations with blossoming reddish flowers.
Another mantra:
"Obeisance to the Dweller in the Lotus," followed by two *ṭha*s; thus it is declared to consist of ten syllables.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:

The ten-syllable mantra is said to begin with *dīrgha* (the letter *da*) and end with *visarga*, consisting of Brahmā, Bhānu, Vasundharā, and the beloved of Vāyu (the letter *ya*), followed by the beloved of Agni (*ra*). || 15 ||
Its worship:
having performed the placement [of mantras] up to the seat (pīṭha) as before, one should perform the placement of the seer (ṛṣi) and so forth.
For example:
Salutation to the sage Dakṣa on the head;
salutation to the Virāṭ meter in the mouth;
salutation to the goddess Śrī in the heart.
And so it is stated in the Śāradā-tilaka:
"The seer is Dakṣa, the metre is Virāj, and the deity is declared to be Śrī. (16)
Then, the ritual assignments of the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *Oṃ*, salutation to the Goddess, *namaḥ* to the two thumbs;
*Oṃ*, salutation to Padminī, *svāhā* to the two index fingers.

Oṃ, obeisance to the consort of Viṣṇu; vaṣaṭ to the middle fingers. Oṃ, obeisance to the bestower of boons; huṃ to the ring fingers. Oṃ, obeisance to her whose form is the lotus; phaṭ to the little fingers.
Thus: *Oṃ devyai namaḥ* [is for] the heart, *namaḥ* [is for] the head, and so forth. And likewise in the Nibandha: "The heart is declared for Devī; the head is said to be for Padminī."
The *śikhā* is declared for Viṣṇupatnī, and the *tanucchada* for Varadā;
the *astra* is for Kamalarūpā—these [mantras] begin with the *praṇava* and end with *namaḥ*. || 17 ||
Then comes the meditation:
Seated upon a lotus, her face smiling, holding with her lotus-like hands the gestures of generosity, the pair of lotuses, and fearlessness; her body resembling a flash of lightning.
May Kamalā protect you— she who shines with broad, lofty breasts adorned with radiant pearl necklaces, and who gladdens Hari with the splendor of her sidelong glances.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, having performed the installation of the conch,

and having conducted the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) ending with the mantra of the pedestal together with the previously mentioned pedestal-energies (pīṭhaśakti), one should meditate again, [performing the rites] from the invocation (āvāhana) up to the offering of the five handfuls of flowers (pañcapuṣpāñjali).
Having performed the worship of the enclosures, one should proceed. || 18 ||
In the center of the four corners beginning with the fire-quarter (southeast), and in the cardinal directions: *Oṃ devyai namaḥ* to the heart, *namaḥ*;
*Oṃ padminyai namaḥ* to the head, *svāhā*;
*Oṃ viṣṇupatnyai namaḥ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
Oṃ, obeisance to Varadā; for the armor, huṃ. Oṃ, obeisance to Kamalarūpā; for the weapon, phaṭ.
Then, one should worship Balākī and the others on the petals starting from the east, as before.
Outside of that, one should worship Indra and the other deities, as well as the vajra and the other implements.
Then, one should complete the ritual procedure from the offering of incense up to the final dismissal. || 19 ||
The preliminary recitation (*puraścaraṇa*) for this mantra consists of ten lakhs of repetitions.
And so it is said:
"One who knows the mantra and has conquered his senses should recite the mantra ten lakh times."
The mantra-practitioner should offer oblations ten times the number [of recitations] using lotuses smeared with honey.
Now, the mantras of Mahālakṣmī: Tāra (Oṃ), Vāgbhava (Aiṃ), Māyā (Hrīṃ), Ramā (Śrīṃ), Kāma (Klīṃ); [the mantra is] "Obeisance to He, the progenitor of the universe. And likewise:
Vāgbhava, Śambhuvanitā, Ramā, Makaraketana,
the third [seed-syllable], Jagatpārśva, blazing with the fire-seed (vahni-bīja),
and Bhṛgu enriched by Arghīśa— this twelve-syllabled mantra is Hṛt.
This [mantra] beginning with "Tārā" is declared for Mahālakṣmī; it bestows all perfections.
Its worship:

having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties up to the placement of the sacred seat (pīṭhanyāsa) as described for the Śrībīja, one should perform the placement of the seer and the other [limbs] (ṛṣyādinyāsa).
Salutation to the sage Brahmā on the head; salutation to the meter Gāyatrī in the mouth; salutation to the deity Mahālakṣmī in the heart. || 22 ||

Then, having purified both hands with the root mantra, one should place the five seed-syllables— beginning with *Tāra* (Oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*— on each finger in the sequence starting from the thumb:
*oṃ aiṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ klīṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ heso*.

*Namaḥ*, *oṃ jagatprasūtyai namaḥ*. Thus, [one should place it] on the palm of the hand. Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) from the head down to the feet with the root mantra.
Then, one should place the five seed-syllables on the head, face, heart, private parts, and feet;
the remaining syllables [should be placed] on the heart and the seven constituent elements (dhātus).
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:

Having purified both hands with the root mantra, the practitioner should place the five seed-syllables, beginning with *tāra* (oṃ) and ending with the heart-mantra, upon the fingers in their proper order;
he should then place the remainder of the mantra upon both palms.
One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-nyāsa) with the root mantra from the head down to the feet.
One should place the five seed-syllables on the head, face, chest, genitals, and feet.
The remaining seven syllables one should place in the heart upon the seven constituent elements (dhātus).
Then, the placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *Aiṃ*, salutation to Knowledge with the two thumbs;
*Hrīṃ*, *svāhā* to Sovereignty with the two index fingers.
Śrīṃ, to Śakti, for the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ; Klīṃ, to Bala, for the two ring fingers, huṃ;
He Soḥ, to Vīrya, for the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ.
"Obeisance to the splendor that brings forth the universe; *phaṭ* to the palms and backs of the hands.
Thus [it is applied] to the heart and other [limbs].
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
The limbs [of the mantra] are formed from the five seed-syllables, and the weapon-mantra (astra) from the remaining syllables.
These are joined with the qualities beginning with knowledge and sovereignty (jñāna, aiśvarya, etc.), ending in the dative case, and accompanied by their respective gender-terminations:
knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, heroism, and splendor.
Knowledge, sovereignty, and the others are declared to be the deities of the limbs in a sequence of six. || 24 ||
Then the meditation:

[one should visualize] the goddess Śālī, who possesses the luster of the rising sun, radiant with a crown and necklace shimmering with crescent moons, adorned with jewel ornaments, her breasts bent down, holding a cluster of blossoms in her hands.

One should meditate upon the supreme Mother (Ambikā), who is smiling, who incessantly bears the lotus and the Kaustubha gem, and who possesses three eyes like full-blown lotuses. For a detailed meditation,
one should consult the Śāradā-tilaka.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*). Then,
having performed the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) as described for the *Śrībīja*, and having meditated again,
[one should perform the rites] from the invocation (*āvāhana*) up to the offering of the five handfuls of flowers (*pañcapuṣpāñjali*).
Having performed the worship of the enclosure (āvaraṇapūjā), one should begin as follows:
"Salutation to Śaṅkaranandana on the right of the Goddess; likewise, salutation to Puṣpadhanvan on the left."
One should worship with "Aiṃ, salutation to the Heart for Knowledge," and so forth, in the intermediate corners beginning with the southeast, in the center, and in the cardinal directions.
And likewise, in the *Śāradā*:
One should worship the Son of Śaṅkara on the right side of the Goddess;
on the other side, one should worship the Flower-Bowed One (Kāmadeva) with his hands joined in a handful of flowers.
One should worship the limbs according to the prescribed rule in the locations previously mentioned.
On the leaves, starting from the east and so forth: *oṃ umāyai namaḥ*; likewise [to] Śrī, Sarasvatī, Durgā, Dharaṇī, Gāyatrī, Devī, and Uṣā.
On the south, [to] Jahnu’s daughter; on the left, [to] Sūrya’s daughter; again on the south, *oṃ*.
To the conch-treasure (śaṅkhanidhi), and again on the left, *oṃ* to the lotus-treasure (padmanidhi); in the west, one should worship Varuṇa holding a parasol (*dhṛtātapatram*).
As follows:
One should worship the eight Śaktis, beginning with Umā, situated in the middle of the petals in due order:
namely, Umā, Śrī, Sarasvatī, Durgā, and Dharaṇī.
The goddess Gāyatrī and Uṣas, holding lotuses in their hands and exceedingly beautiful;
outside of that, one should worship each of the twelve zodiac signs and the nine planets;
and outside of that, the eight elephants beginning with Airāvata.
One should worship Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, Añjana, Puṣpadanta, Sārvabhauma, and Supratīka.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
The two daughters of Jahnu and Sūrya, worthy of worship, are intent on washing [his] feet;
the two treasures, Śaṅkha and Padma, holding chowries, are to be worshipped at his sides.
Then one should worship Varuṇa, who is supported by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, in the west.
Having worshipped him, one should then worship the zodiac signs all around and the nine planets.
One should worship the elephants of the quarters, adorned with four tusks, in their respective directions.
Airāvata, Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, and Añjana.
Puṣpadanta, Sārvabhauma, and Supratīka—these are to be worshipped in sequence.
Then one should worship Indra and the other [deities], as well as the thunderbolt and the other [weapons].
Thereafter, one should complete the ritual from the offering of incense (dhūpa) until the final dismissal (visarjana). || 26 ||
The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations.
And so it is said:
"One should recite the mantra one million times and perform oblations with ghee ten thousand times."
One should offer two tens of thousands of bilva fruits and lotuses for each [deity].
One should satiate them with pure, fragrant waters twenty thousand times;
the phrase "twenty thousand times" is a formal injunction.
Another mantra: Śambhūpatnī, Śriyāruddhā, Kama, Bhagavatī,
Mahī, Brahmādityau, Dharā, Dīrghā, Lakṣmyādi, and Bhagavān Marut.
The pair *pra-sī-da*, followed by *bhūyaḥ* (bhū-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ), then *śrīruddhā bhuvaneśvarī*, and ending with *mahālakṣmi namaḥ*—this mantra begins with the *praṇava* (*oṃ*).
*Mahī* is the letter *la*; *Bhagavatī* is the letter *e*; *Brahmā* is the letter *ka*; and *Āditya* is the letter *ma*.
The letter *la* is *dharā*; the long [vowel] is joined with *ā*; the letter *la* is the beginning of *lakṣmī* and so forth; the wind is the letter *ya* joined with *e*. || 20 ||

The worship of this [deity] is as follows: having performed the previously mentioned rites beginning with the morning duties and ending with the nyāsa of the seers (ṛṣi) and so forth, one should perform the nyāsa on the hands and limbs.
*Śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kamale śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Likewise, *śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kamalālaye śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ*.
Svāhā!
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, be gracious! Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers!
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Prasīda Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the two ring fingers, Huṃ!
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Mahālakṣmī Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the two little fingers,
Vauṣaṭ!
*Śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*.
In this manner, [the mantra is applied] to the heart and the other limbs.
And so it is stated in the *Nibandha*:
The heart is said to be "kamale," and the head should be "kamalālaye. The crest-mantra (śikhā) is "prasīda" with that same [seed-syllable], and the armor (kavaca) consists of four syllables.
One should perform the weapon-mantra (astra) with these words, each separately encased by the three seed-syllables.

Then the meditation: [He meditates on her] whose splendor is as red as vermilion, whose abode is the lotus, who is a treasure-trove of the waters of beauty, and who is adorned with a crown, armlets, necklaces, earrings, a waist-string, and other ornaments.

One should constantly meditate upon the supreme beloved of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, who carries a vessel of eight jewels, a pair of lotuses, and a mirror in her lotus-hands, and who is surrounded by female attendants.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should prepare the place for the conch.
Having performed the worship of the pedestal as before, and having meditated once more,
one should perform the rites from the invocation up to the offering of the five handfuls of flowers, and then begin the worship of the surrounding deities (āvaraṇapūjā).

One should worship with "Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kamale Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ" and so forth, in the filaments at the corners starting from the southeast (Agni), in the center, and in the cardinal directions.
At the base of the petals, starting from the east, one should worship "Oṃ Śrīdharāya Namaḥ," and likewise "Hṛṣīkeśāya."
To Vaikuṇṭha, to Viśvarūpa, to Vāsudeva, to Saṅkarṣaṇa, to Pradyumna, and to Aniruddha;
in the middle of the petals, to Bhāratī, to Pārvatī, to Cāndrī, to Śacī, to Damaka, and to Salila.
To Guggulu and Kuruṇṭaka.
On the tips of the petals:
Anurāga, Visaṃvāda, Vijaya, Vallabha, and Mada.

One should worship the arrows of Mahālakṣmī as "Joy," "Strength," and "Splendor. With the mantra: "Obeisance to the arrow of Mahālakṣmī for the sake of devotion," one should worship them in this sequence. || 31 ||
And likewise, in the Nibandha:
"One should worship these arrows of Mahālakṣmī on the tips of the petals in their proper order;
outside of that, one should worship Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and the other weapons."
Then, one should complete the ritual actions ending with the dismissal of the incense and other offerings. || 31ka ||
The preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of one hundred thousand recitations (lakṣajapa).
And likewise:

One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times and perform oblations with bilva fruits smeared with honey, ten parts of which should be offered into the consecrated fire according to the very path previously described.
Now, the mantras of the Sun:
Tāra (Om), followed by Ghṛṇi, Bhṛgu, adorned with the left ear (U), seated on fire (Ra), the remainder of Marut (Sa), with the eye (I), and finally Adri (Ma). Thus: Om Ghṛṇi Bhṛgūṃ.
The eight-syllable mantra of the Sun is proclaimed to bestow all desired objects. || 33 ||

The procedure for its worship is as follows: having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties and ending with breath control (prāṇāyāma) as described in the General Manual of Worship (Sāmānyapūjāpaddhati), one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the seat (pīṭha).
In this regard, the specific detail is as follows:

having placed in the eastern and other directions of one's own heart, as well as in the center, the abundant, pure, essential, worshipful, and supreme bliss, [one should place] the Foundation Power (ādhāraśakti) and so forth, beginning with the letter *aṃ*.
One should perform the placement [of mantras] ending with: "Obeisance to the solar orb, whose self consists of twelve digits.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"Once the pedestal has been prepared, one should first worship [the deities] in the cardinal directions and in the center."

One should arrange the seat (*pīṭha*) consisting of the abundant, stainless, and essential [syllables], which is to be propitiated immediately and is the supreme primordial bliss, ending with one's own *vidyā*.
Then, in the filaments and in the center, [one should place]: *rāṃ dīptāyai namaḥ*, *rīṃ sūkṣmāyai*.
Namaḥ; to Jayā, Rūpa; to Bhadrā, Reṃ; to Vibhūti, Raiṃ; to Vimalā, Roṃ; to Amoghā, Rauṃ; to Vidyutā, Raṃ; to Sarvatomukhī, Raḥ—namas. As it is stated in the Nibandha:
Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā, Amoghā, Vidyutā, and Sarvatomukhī are the Pīṭha-śaktis;
one should know their seed-syllables (bījas) in sequence, having the form of the flame of a blazing lamp.

[One should write] the three short vowels, excluding the neuter (a), conjoined with the bindu and the fire (the letter *r*). Above that, [one writes]: *oṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakāya saurāya yogapīṭhāya namaḥ*.
And likewise in the Śāradā:
One should utter the word ending in the dative case, consisting of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;
immediately thereafter, the word "namaḥ" for the solar seat of yoga (saurāya yogapīṭhāya).
This is declared to be the seat-mantra (pīṭhamantra) of the Sun, the Lord of the World. || 34 ||

Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seers and so forth: "Salutation to the seer Devabhāga on the head; salutation to the metre Gāyatrī on the mouth; salutation to the deity Āditya on the heart."
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"The sage is declared to be Devabhaga; Gāyatrī is said to be the meter;
Āditya is declared to be the deity, bestowing both seen and unseen fruits. (35)
In the *Rāmārcanacandrikā*: "The seed-syllable is declared to be *tāra* (Om), and *yaḥ* is proclaimed as the *śakti*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of this mantra is Bhārgava."
This has been stated in the *Rāmārcanacandrikā*:
"The sage of this mantra is said to be Bhārgava, and its deity is Gāyatrī," and so forth.
Then follows the ritual assignment of the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*):
To Satya, the Jewel of Blazing Radiance, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, homage to both thumbs (*aṃguṣṭhābhyām*).
To Brahmā, the Jewel of Blazing Radiance, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, *svāhā* to both index fingers (*tarjanībhyām*).
*Viṣṇave tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—to the middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*.
*Rudrāya tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—to the ring fingers, *huṃ*.
*Agnaye tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—to the little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*.
*Sarvāya tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—*phaṭ* with both palms and backs of the hands; likewise for the heart and other [limbs]. || 36 ||
And so it is stated in the Śāradā-tilaka:
"The Heart is declared for Satya; the Head is said to be for Brahmā;
the Crest (Śikhā) should belong to Viṣṇu; and the Armor (Varman) is proclaimed for Rudra."
The eye of Agni has been declared; that of Sarvāyudha is proclaimed as *tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ*, ending with two *ṭh*s, each uttered separately. || 37 ||
Then follows the ritual placement of the forms (*mūrtinyāsa*), as follows:
on the head, *oṃ ādityāya namaḥ*; likewise, on the face, *eṃ ravaye*; on the heart, *uṃ bhānave*.
Iṃ to Bhāskara in the secret place; Aṃ to Sūrya in the two feet. || 38 ||
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"One should place Āditya on the head, and one should place Ravi on the face;
one should place the one named Bhānu on the heart, and Bhāskara on the private parts."
One should place the Sun on the two feet with the five short vowels beginning with *a* (the *satya* group).
Then follows the mantra-deposition (*mantranyāsa*).
In the heart: oṃ oṃ namaḥ; in the mouth: oṃ ghṛ namaḥ;
in the throat: oṃ ṇi namaḥ; in the heart: oṃ sū namaḥ; in the belly: oṃ ryya namaḥ; in the navel: oṃ ā namaḥ.
Oṃ di namaḥ on the *liṅga*; oṃ tya namaḥ on the two feet.
And likewise, in the *Nibandha*:
"On the head, mouth, throat, heart, belly, navel, penis, and feet..."
One should assign the eight mantra-syllables individually, each preceded by the Praṇava (Oṃ). || 39 ||
Then comes the meditation:
I praise the Lord of Day, who has hands granting boons and holding a pair of red lotuses, adorned with armlets, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings;
who wears a ruby crown, possesses the luster of the bandhūka flower, and has three shining eyes. (40)
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the ritual placement of the *arghya* water.
Then, having performed the worship of the lineage of gurus (gurupaṃkti), one should perform the worship of the seats (pīṭhapūjā).
Having conceptualized the form with "Oṃ Khaṃ, obeisance to Khakholka," and having meditated once more,
one should carry out the rites from the invocation (āvāhana) up to the offering of the fivefold handfuls of flowers (pañcapuṣpa-añjali-dāna).
One should begin the worship of the obstructions (āvaraṇapūjā).
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"The visualization of the form [of the deity] is performed with the mantra beginning with 'Tārā' and ending with 'khaṃ khakholkāya'."
Having invoked the witness of all the worlds into that [image], one should worship it.
In the filaments, in the corners beginning with the southeast, in the center, and in the cardinal directions: *oṃ satyāya tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, [this is] for the heart, *namaḥ*.
Likewise: *oṃ brahmaṇe tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, [this is] for the heart, *namaḥ*.
Thus: *Oṃ brahmaṇe tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—*svāhā* to the head (*śiras*).
*Oṃ viṣṇave tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—*vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *Oṃ rudrāya tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—*huṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*).
Oṃ agnaye tejojvālāmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Oṃ sarvāya tejojvālāmaṇe huṃ phaṭ svāhā, phaṭ to the weapon (*astra*).
On the petals of the directions, starting from the east: Oṃ ādityāya namaḥ; likewise, eṃ to Ravi, uṃ to Bhānu.
*Im* to Bhāskara. On the petals in the intermediate directions: *Ūm* to Ūṣā, *Paṃ* to Prajñā, *Paṃ* to Prabhā, and *Saṃ* to Sandhyā.
And likewise, in the Nibandha:
"One should first worship the limbs; on the petals of the directions are the forms of the Sun (Āditya), and the four Śaktis beginning with Ādityā are to be worshipped on the petals of the corners."
The seed-syllables (bījas) of these [goddesses] are, in sequence, the initial letters of their respective names.
They are proclaimed as the powers (śaktis): Ūṣā, Prajñā, Prabhā, and Sandhyā.
Then, having worshipped Brāhmī and the others on the tips of the petals, one should worship Aruṇa in front;
and so it is said in the Śāradā:
"One should worship Brāhmī and the others situated on the tips of the petals, and Aruṇa in front."
Outside of that, one should worship the Moon and the others in the east and so forth:
*oṃ candrāya namaḥ*; likewise for Maṅgala, Budha, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, and Ketu.
And so it is stated in the *Śāradā*:
"Thereafter, one should worship the eight planets, beginning with the Moon, outside of that;
then, having worshipped Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and the other [emblems], one performs the ritual from the offering of incense until the final dismissal."
One should bring it to completion. || 42 ||
The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) for this consists of reciting the mantra eight hundred thousand times.
And so it is said:
"One should recite the mantra eight hundred thousand times with the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) of trees that bear milky sap."
One who has conquered the senses should offer that thousand-fold oblation with [fuel sticks] smeared with milk.
In this case as well, the oblation of eight thousand [times] is indeed based on explicit scriptural injunction. || 43 ||
The other mantra is Bhuvaneśvarī, joined with Ākāśa (ha), Agni (ra), Dīrgha-indu (ī), and Sarga (ḥ);
this three-syllabled mantra of the Sun is thus proclaimed, followed by Bhṛgu (sa). || 44 ||
The worship of this [deity] is as follows:

having first performed the rites of the morning duties and so forth, one should perform the placement of the seat (pīṭhanyāsa) as stated in the preceding mantra, and then perform the placement of the seers (ṛṣyādinyāsa) and other such placements as stated in the preceding mantra. || 45 ||
Then follows the ritual placement of the mantras (*mantranyāsa*):
*hrāṃ namaḥ* from the *ādhāra* to the feet;
*hrīṃ namaḥ* from the throat to the *ādhāra*.
From the crown of the head down to the throat, he says "Namaḥ.
In the *Śāradā*:
"From the base of the support (*ādhāra*) up to the tip of the feet, and from the throat down to the base of the support."
One should sequentially place the three seed-syllables from the crown of the head down to the throat. || 46 ||
Then, the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *hrāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*;
*hrīṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā*.
Hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers; hraiṃ, huṃ to the two ring fingers;
hrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers.
HRAḤ PHAṬ with the palms and backs of the hands.
Likewise for the heart and other [limbs].
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
The visualization of the limbs and other parts is performed by means of the seed-syllable situated in the center, which is conjoined with the six long vowels.
Then comes the meditation:
I worship the Sun, seated upon a red lotus, the sole ocean of all virtues, the sovereign lord of the entire world.
Holding two lotuses, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons with his lotus-like hands, he wears a crown of rubies, possesses a reddish bodily luster, and has three eyes.
Having meditated thus and performed worship with mental offerings, one should perform the installation of the *arghya* water.

Then, having performed the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha-pūjā*) according to the previously mentioned sequence and having conceptualized the form (*mūrti*) with the root mantra, one should meditate once more.
Having performed the rites from the invocation (āvāhana) up to the offering of the five handfuls of flowers (pañcapuṣpāñjali),

one should perform the worship of the enclosures (āvaraṇapūjā). In the corners of Agni, Nirṛti, Vāyu, and Īśāna, as well as in the center and the cardinal directions, [one should worship] with "hrāṃ hṛdayāya" [and so forth].
One should worship with "namaḥ" and so forth;
one should worship the moon and the others upon the petals as before.
Then one should worship Indra and the other deities, as well as the vajra and the other weapons.
Thereafter, one should complete the ritual from the offering of incense up to the final dismissal. || 49 ||
The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) for this consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations.
And so it is said:
"One should recite the mantra one million times, and perform oblations with clarified butter in a tenth part thereof."
Or one who has conquered the senses should offer oblations with sesame seeds sprinkled with honey.
This seed-syllable, ending with the mantra [HŪM],
followed by ĀKĀŚA (L), VAHNI (R), PAVANA (Y), SATYA (Ū), ANTARGHĪŚA (AU), and the bindu (M)—
is declared to be named Mārttaṇḍabhairava.
Enclosed by the seed-syllable of the Bimba fruit, it bestows the fruits of all desires. || 51 ||
The seed-syllable of the *vimbā* is stated in the Tantra:
"That which ends with the letter *ṭ*, joined with fire (*ra*), the eye (*i*), and the moon (*u*), is thus declared. (52)
The procedure for its worship is as follows:

having first performed the rites beginning with the morning duties up to the placement on the seat (pīṭhanyāsa) as previously stated in the mantra, one should perform the placement of the seers (ṛṣyādinyāsa) as before. || 53 ||
Then follows the ritual placement of the forms (mūrtinyāsa):
*ṭhraṃ* to Sūrya, salutation on the two thumbs;
*ṭhriṃ* to Bhāskara, salutation on the two index fingers.
Ṭhruṃ, salutation to Bhānu on the middle fingers; Ṭhreṃ, salutation to Ravi on the ring fingers;
Ṭhroṃ, salutation to Divākara on the little fingers.
Then, one should place those [mantras] preceded by their respective seed-syllables on the head, face, heart, and feet.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"One should duly install the five forms with the seed-syllables augmented by the five short vowels."
These [syllables] are to be placed in order upon the fingers, beginning with the thumb and ending with the little finger.
Sūrya, Bhāskara, Bhānu, Ravi, and Divākara—
these [names] are again [assigned] to the regions of the head, face, heart, private parts, and feet respectively.
Then follows the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*):
*ṭhrāṃ* to both thumbs, *namaḥ*;
*ṭhrīṃ* to both index fingers, *svāhā*.
Ṭhrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers;
ṭhraiṃ, huṃ to the two ring fingers;
ṭhrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers.
Ṭhraḥ, with the palms and backs of the hands, phaṭ! Likewise: Ṭhrāṃ, to the heart, namaḥ, and so forth.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"Thereafter, one should perform the pervasion with the root seed-syllable. (54)

Then the visualization: [He holds] a beautiful khaṭvāṅga, a bow, a discus, a spear, a noose, a goad, a most beautiful rosary, and a skull-cup, which possess a luster like that of gold, a lotus, coral, and pure crystal.

We worship the Sun-god, who holds lotuses in his hands, who is beautiful with four faces adorned by three sparkling eyes, who bears the beloved Goddess as half of his body, and who shines with a jeweled crown and a radiant necklace.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the ritual placement of the *arghya*.
Then, having worshipped up to the *pīṭha-mantra* according to the previously stated sequence, one should worship in the east and other directions,
as well as on the pericarp (*karṇikā*), with "Oṃ, obeisance to Ūṣā," and likewise to Prajñā, Prabhā, and Sandhyā; then [worship] the form (*mūrti*) with the root mantra (*mūla*).
One should perform [the visualization].
Then, having meditated once more and performed the rites from the invocation up to the offering of five handfuls of flowers, one should begin the worship of the enclosures (*āvaraṇapūjā*).
And likewise, in the *Nibandha*:
"When the pedestal is joined with the [planets] beginning with the Sun (Dīpta),
one should worship the [deities] beginning with Uṣā in the pericarp and in the directions starting from the East, and then fashion the form by means of the root mantra."
Then, one should worship Sūrya, Bhāskara, Bhānu, and Ravi in the directions starting from the east;
and Divākara in the corners.
Then, in the corners of Agni, Nirṛti, Vāyu, and Īśāna, [one should worship] with "Ṭhrāṃ, obeisance to the heart," and so forth.
In the northeast: *Ṭhrauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*.
In the *Śāradā*:
one should worship the four [deities] beginning with Sūrya in the cardinal directions and the other in the intermediate directions.
The limb-worship (*aṅgapūjā*) is as before: "the eye [is worshipped] in the directions starting from the northeast (*īśāna*)," and so forth.
Then, having worshipped the eight planets beginning with the Moon as previously described, one should worship the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) within the enclosures of the earth.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"Likewise, one should worship the eight planets and then the guardians of the world (lokapālas);
thereafter, one should complete the ritual from the offering of incense (dhūpa) until its conclusion. (56)
The preliminary recitation (*puraścaraṇa*) for this [mantra] consists of three hundred thousand repetitions.
The fire-oblation (*homa*) should consist of ten parts (*daśāṃśa*) performed with lotuses mixed with the "three sweets" (*trimadhura*).
And so it is said:

One should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times, encased within the seed-syllables of the *bimba* flower; one should then perform oblations with a sixth part of that number using full-blown lotuses sprinkled with honey.
A mortal who recites this mantra shall achieve splendor, sons, wealth, and luster;
he shall also accomplish incomparable perfection of speech, fortune, and good luck. (58)
Now, the Ajapā mantra:
Viyat (the letter *ha*), adorned with an Arddhendu (the crescent moon), followed by the first [vowel] and joined with Sarga (the visarga);
this two-syllabled mantra known as Ajapā is declared to be the celestial wish-fulfilling tree. (59)
The worship of this [deity] is as follows:

having completed the morning rites and so forth, up to the previously mentioned seat-mantra (pīṭhamantra), one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seer (ṛṣi) and the other [components].
Salutation to the sage Brahmā on the head;
salutation to the meter Gāyatrī on the mouth;
salutation to the deity Śrī Girijāpati on the heart.
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"O Goddess, the seer is remembered as Brahmā; Gāyatrī is declared to be the meter;
and the deity is proclaimed to be Girijāpati, the primordial source of the worlds. (60)
Then, for the limbs of the hands, [he recites]: *hsāṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*, and so forth.
Likewise for the heart and other [limbs].
And likewise, in the Nibandha: "One should perform the ritual of the limbs (aṅgakriyā) for the mantra using *hsāṃ* joined with the six long vowels. (61)
Then the meditation:

[one should visualize] the Lord of the Half-Mother (Ardhāmbikeśa), whose form is like the flash of lightning from the rising sun, holding in his lotus-hands the noose, the gesture of fearlessness, the boon-granting gesture, and the axe.
May the moon-crested, three-eyed one protect you— He who is the root of the universe, adorned with divine ornaments made of fresh jewels, and whose form embodies both the gentle and the fiery.

Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, having performed the installation of the conch (*śaṅkha-sthāpana*) and carried out the previously mentioned worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha-pūjā*), one should meditate again [on the deity] up to the offering of the five handfuls of flowers (*pañca-puṣpāñjali*) beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*).
Having performed the worship of the enclosure (āvaraṇapūjā), one should begin [the main rite].
One should worship in the corners of Agni, Nirṛti, Vāyu, and Īśāna, as well as in the center and the cardinal directions, with "Hsāṃ, obeisance to the heart," and so forth.
One should worship Ṛta, Vara, Vasu, and Nara in the cardinal directions; and Ṛtajā, Gojā, Abja, and Drijā in the intermediate directions.
Thus it is stated in the *Nibandha*:
One should worship the two supreme men, Ṛta and Vasu, on the petals of the directions and then in the intermediate directions;
furthermore, one should worship Ṛtajā, Gojā, the one named Abjā, and Adrijā.
Outside of that, one should worship Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and the other weapons.
Then, one should complete the ritual actions ending with the dismissal of the incense and other offerings. || 62 ||
The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of twelve lakhs of recitations.
The fire-oblation (homa) should be performed with milk-rice mixed with ghee, numbering one-tenth of that amount.
And so it is said:

One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times and then the practitioner of mantra should offer oblations ten times that amount with milk-rice mixed with ghee; thereafter, that person becomes accomplished.
Now, the Viṣṇu-mantras:
Next, I shall declare the great mantras of Viṣṇu, which bestow all prosperity;
by the mere remembrance of which the virtuous have reached the further shore of the ocean of worldly existence. (64)
One should utter the syllable *tāram*, the word *namaḥ*, and the two long vowels (*nārau*).
This supreme mantra, consisting of eight syllables, is proclaimed by the name *Pāvana*. (65)
The procedure for its worship is as follows:
having performed the rites beginning with the morning duties and ending with the bath, one should enter the pavilion of worship and perform the Vaiṣṇava ācamana (sipping of water). || 66 ||
As it is said in the Gautamīya:
"Having sipped water with three [verses] beginning with 'Keśava,' one should wash both hands with two;
having wiped the lips with two, one should then wipe the mouth with two."
Having washed one hand, and likewise the feet with the other [hand],
he should sprinkle his head with one [hand]; then, with the [mantras] beginning with Saṅkarṣaṇa,
he should successively touch the mouth, nose, eyes, ears, navel, chest, and arms.
One should touch [the water] in this manner; such indeed is the *ācamana* in the Vaiṣṇava lineage.
Having performed the *ācamana* in this way, one becomes Nārāyaṇa himself. Keśava and the others—Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu, Madhusūdana...
Trivikrama, Vāmana, Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, Dāmodara, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Puruṣottama, Adhokṣaja, Nṛsiṃha, Acyuta, Janārdana, Upendra, Hari, and Viṣṇu.
The mantra is *oṃ keśavāya namaḥ*, and so forth. And likewise:
"The wise one should perform the placement [of the syllables] with the names ending in the dative case followed by *namaḥ*. (68)
Then, having performed the rites beginning with the general *arghya* offering and ending with the *mātṛkā-nyāsa*, one should perform the *nyāsa* of Keśava, Kīrti, and the others.
The *nyāsa* of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth for this [mantra] is as follows:
Salutation to Prajāpati, the seer (ṛṣi), on the head;
salutation to the Gāyatrī metre (chandas) on the mouth;
salutation to the deity Arddhalakṣmīhari on the heart. || 69 ||
Then follow the nyāsa of the hands and limbs: *śrīṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*, and so forth;
likewise for the heart and other parts.
And likewise in the Gautamiya:
"The seer is Prajāpati, the metre is Gāyatrī, and the deity is proclaimed to be Hari-Ardhalakṣmī; the six limbs [of the ritual] are performed with the Śrī-bīja. (70)
Then comes the meditation:
[He] possesses the brilliance of a hundred rising suns, shines with the luster of molten gold, and is attended on both sides by the Daughter of the Ocean and the Mother of the Universe.
I bow to Viṣṇu, who wears various ornaments shining with diverse jewels and yellow garments,
and who holds the lotus, the Kaumodakī mace, and the discus in his hands.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*).
And so it is stated in the *Kramadīpikā*:
"Having uttered the phonemes together with the half-moon in front," and so forth; this is seen to apply everywhere.
It is accompanied by an anusvāra. || 71 ||
Aṃ, salutation to Keśava and Kīrti on the forehead; Āṃ, salutation to Nārāyaṇa and Kānti on the face;
Iṃ, salutation to Mādhava and Tuṣṭi on the right eye.
*Īṃ*, salutation to Govinda for nourishment (*puṣṭi*) on the left eye;
everywhere thus, *Uṃ*, salutation to Viṣṇu for steadfastness (*dhṛti*) on the right ear;
*Ūṃ*, salutation to Madhusūdana for peace (*śānti*) on the left ear.
Ṛṃ to Trivikrama and Kriyā at the right nostril; Ṝṃ to Vāmana and Dayā at the left nostril; Ḷṃ to Śrīdhara and Medhā at the right cheek.
Ḷṃ to Hṛṣīkeśa and Harṣā on the left cheek;
Eṃ to Padmanābha and Śraddhā on the upper lip; Eṃ to Dāmodara and Lajjā on the lower lip.
Oṃ vāsudevāya lakṣmyai on the upper row of teeth;
oṃ saṃkarṣaṇāya sarasvatyai on the lower row of teeth;
aṃ pradyumnāya prītyai on the head.
Aḥ to Aniruddha and Rati at the mouth; Kaṃ to the wielder of the discus (Cakrin) and Jayā;
Khaṃ to the wielder of the mace (Gadin) and Durgā; Gaṃ to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow (Śārṅgin) and Prabhā; Ghaṃ to the wielder of the sword (Khaḍgin).
To Satyā, Ṅaṃ Śaṅkhinī, and Caṇḍā— at the root-joint, middle, and tip of the right hand respectively;
Caṃ Halinī, Bāṇā, Chaṃ Muṣalinī, Vilāsinī, Jaṃ Śūlinī, Vijayā, Jhaṃ Pāśinī, Virajā, Ñaṃ Aṅkuśinī, Viśvā— at these [joints].
In the root-joint, middle-joint, and tip of the left hand:
*ṭaṃ* to Mukunda and Vinadā; *ṭhaṃ* to Nandaja and Sunadā; *ḍaṃ* to Nandin and Smṛti; *ḍhaṃ* to Nara and Ṛddhi; *ṇaṃ* to Narakajit and Samṛddhi. Thus.
In the joints and tips of the toes of the right foot:
*taṃ* to Hari for purity (*śuddhi*), *thaṃ* to Kṛṣṇa for intellect (*buddhi*), *daṃ* to Satya for devotion (*bhakti*),
*dhaṃ* to Sāttvata for intelligence (*mati*), and *naṃ* to Śauri for forbearance (*kṣamā*).
At the joints and tips of the toes of the left foot:
*paṃ* to Śūra and Ramā on the right side;
*phaṃ* to Janārdana and Umā on the left side.
Baṃ to Bhudhara and Kledinī at the back; Bhaṃ to Viśvamūrti and Klinnā at the navel;
Maṃ to Vaikuṇṭha and Vasudā at the belly.

To the Skin-Self, Puruṣottama, [one should offer] in the heart; to the Blood-Self, Bala, in the right shoulder; to the Flesh-Self, Anujabala, on the hump. To Vasudhā, Parā; to Parāyaṇā. To Laṃ. To the Bone-Self, Vīrabhadra, in the left shoulder; to Aparājitā, Parā. To Vaṃ. To the Marrow-Self, Śrīkaṇṭha, in the navel; to Māyā, Parā. To Śaṃ. To the Semen-Self, Sadāśiva, in the secret place; to Śakti, Parā. To Ṣaṃ. To the Vitality-Self, Maheśvara, in the anus; to Gaurī, Parā. To Saṃ. To the Mind-Self, Īśvara, in the mouth; to Umā, Parā. To Haṃ. To the Intellect-Self, Śambhu, in the forehead; to Ambikā, Parā. To L̥aṃ. To the Ego-Self, Rudra, in the crown of the head; to Kālī, Parā. To Kṣaṃ. To the Sound-Self, Viṣṇu, in the right ear; to Lakṣmī, Parā. To Khaṃ. To the Touch-Self, Brahmā, in the left ear; to Sarasvatī, Parā. To Gaṃ. To the Form-Self, Indra, in the right eye; to Indrāṇī, Parā. To Ghaṃ. To the Taste-Self, Yama, in the left eye; to Yamī, Parā. To Ṅaṃ. To the Smell-Self, Soma, in the right nostril; to Somā, Parā. To Caṃ. To the Speech-Self, Agni, in the left nostril; to Agnī, Parā. To Chaṃ. To the Hand-Self, Kubera, in the right hand; to Dhanadā, Parā. To Jaṃ. To the Grasping-Self, Varuṇa, in the left hand; to Varuṇā, Parā. To Jhaṃ. To the Locomotion-Self, Vāyu, in the right foot; to Vāyavī, Parā. To Ñaṃ. To the Excretion-Self, Nirṛti, in the left foot; to Nirṛtī, Parā. To Taṃ. To the Procreation-Self, Āpaḥ, in the private parts; to Apavatsā, Parā. To Thaṃ. To the Earth-Self, Pṛthivī, in the right thigh; to Pṛthvī, Parā. To Daṃ. To the Water-Self, Āpaḥ, in the left thigh; to Apavatsā, Parā. To Dhaṃ. To the Fire-Self, Tejaḥ, in the right shank; to Tejovatī, Parā. To Naṃ. To the Wind-Self, Vāyu, in the left shank; to Vāyuvatyā, Parā. To Paṃ. To the Ether-Self, Vyoma, in the right knee; to Vyomā, Parā. To Phaṃ. To the Moon-Self, Candra, in the left knee; to Candrikā, Parā. To Baṃ. To the Sun-Self, Sūrya, in the right ankle; to Sūryā, Parā. To Bhaṃ. To the Nakṣatra-Self, Nakṣatra, in the left ankle; to Nakṣatrā, Parā. To Maṃ. To the Constellation-Self, Nakṣatra, in the right toe; to Nakṣatrā, Parā. To Yaṃ. To the Planets-Self, Graha, in the left toe; to Grahiṇī, Parā. To Raṃ. To the Directions-Self, Diś, in the right palm; to Diśā, Parā. To Laṃ. To the Intermediate Directions-Self, Vidig, in the left palm; to Vidigā, Parā. To Vaṃ. To the Time-Self, Kāla, in the right side; to Kālī, Parā. To Śaṃ. To the Intermediate Time-Self, Antarakāla, in the left side; to Antarakālī, Parā. To Ṣaṃ. To the Moment-Self, Kṣaṇa, in the right shoulder-blade; to Kṣaṇā, Parā. To Saṃ. To the Muhūrta-Self, Muhūrta, in the left shoulder-blade; to Muhūrtā, Parā. To Haṃ. To the Year-Self, Saṃvatsara, in the right elbow; to Saṃvatsarī, Parā. To L̥aṃ. To the Half-Year-Self, Ayana, in the left elbow; to Ayanā, Parā. To Kṣaṃ. To the Season-Self, Ṛtu, in the right wrist; to Ṛtumatī, Parā. To Khaṃ. To the Month-Self, Māsa, in the left wrist; to Māsī, Parā. To Gaṃ. To the Fortnight-Self, Pakṣa, in the right forearm; to Pakṣī, Parā. To Ghaṃ. To the Day-Self, Ahaḥ, in the left forearm; to Ahnī, Parā. To Ṅaṃ. To the Night-Self, Rātri, in the right hand; to Rātrī, Parā. To Caṃ. To the Sandhyā-Self, Sandhyā, in the left hand; to Sandhyā, Parā. To Chaṃ. To the Twilight-Self, Sandhyā, in the right hip; to Sandhyā, Parā. To Jaṃ. To the Dawn-Self, Uṣas, in the left hip; to Uṣā, Parā. To Jhaṃ. To the Evening-Self, Pradoṣa, in the right buttock; to Pradoṣā, Parā. To Ñaṃ. To the Midnight-Self, Ardharātra, in the left buttock; to Ardharātrī, Parā. To Taṃ. To the Forenoon-Self, Pūrvāhṇa, in the right thigh; to Pūrvāhṇā, Parā. To Thaṃ. To the Afternoon-Self, Aparāhṇa, in the left thigh; to Aparāhṇā, Parā. To Daṃ. To the Evening-Self, Sāyam, in the right shank; to Sāyā, Parā. To Dhaṃ. To the Night-Self, Niśā, in the left shank; to Niśā, Parā. To Naṃ. To the Sleep-Self, Svapna, in the right knee; to Svapnā, Parā. To Paṃ. To the Waking-Self, Jagrat, in the left knee; to Jagradā, Parā. To Phaṃ. To the Dream-Self, Svapna, in the right ankle; to Svapnā, Parā. To Baṃ. To the Deep-Sleep-Self, Suṣupti, in the left ankle; to Suṣuptī, Parā. To Bhaṃ. To the Fourth-Self, Turya, in the right toe; to Turyā, Parā. To Maṃ. To the Fourth-Beyond-Self, Turyātīta, in the left toe; to Turyātītā, Parā. To Yaṃ. To the Unmanifest-Self, Avyakta, in the right palm; to Avyaktā, Parā. To Raṃ. To the Manifest-Self, Vyakta, in the left palm; to Vyaktā, Parā. To Laṃ. To the Individual-Self, Jīva, in the right side; to Jīvā, Parā. To Vaṃ. To the Supreme-Self, Paramātman, in the left side; to Paramātmanī, Parā. To Śaṃ. To the All-Self, Sarva
Vaṃ, to the Self of Intellect, the Youthful, the Subtle, on the left shoulder.
*Śaṃ* to the self of bone (*asthyātman*), to Vṛṣaghna, to Sandhyā, from the heart to the right hand;
*Ṣaṃ* to the self of marrow (*majjātman*), to Vṛṣa, to Prajñā, from the heart to the left hand; *Saṃ* to the self of semen (*śukrātman*), to Haṃsa, to Prabhā, from the heart to the right foot.
*Haṃ*, to the *prāṇātman* Varāha, to Niśā—from the heart to the left foot;
*laṃ*, to the *jīvātman* Vimala, to Amoghā—from the heart to the stomach;
*kṣaṃ*, to the *krodhātman* Nṛsiṃha, to Vidyutā—from the heart to the mouth. Thus.
Homage everywhere. || 72 ||
Śāradā says regarding Keśava and the others:
"Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, and Viṣṇu;
another is named Madhusūdana; then Trivikrama and Vāmana."
Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, and thereafter Padmanābha;
Dāmodara, Vāsudeva, and he who is called Saṃkarṣaṇa;
Pradyumna and Aniruddha—these are remembered as the forms of the vowels.
Afterwards, he is the wielder of the discus (Cakrī), the mace (Gadī), the bow Śārṅga (Śārṅgī), the sword (Khaḍgī), the conch (Śaṅkhī), and again the plow (Halī);
then the one known as the club-bearer (Muṣalī), another called the trident-bearer (Śūlī), the noose-bearer (Pāśī), and again the goad-bearer (Aṅkuśī);
[then] Mukunda, Nandaja, Nanda, Nara, the conqueror of Naraka (Narakajit), and Hari.
Kṛṣṇa, Satya, Sāttvata, Śauri, Śūra, Janārdana, Bhūdhara, Viśvamūrti, Vaikuṇṭha,
Puruṣottama, Balin, Balānuja, Bāla, Vṛṣaghn, and again Vṛṣa.
The Swan, the Boar, the Immaculate One, and the Man-Lion—these are my forms, O Halāyudha.
These, Keśava and the others, are dark-complexioned, with hands resplendent with the conch and discus;
they are Kīrti, Kānti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Dhṛti, Śānti, Kriyā, and Dayā.
Medhā, Saharṣā, Śraddhā, Lajjā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī,
Prīti, and Rati— these are declared to be the powers of the vowels in their respective order.
Jayā, Durgā, Prabhā, Satyā, Caṇḍā, Vāṇī, Vilāsinī, Vijayā,
Virajā, Viśvā, Vinadā, Sunadā,
Smṛti, Ṛṣi, Samṛddhi, Śuddhi, Bhukti, Buddhi, Mati, and Kṣamā.
Rama, Kledini, Klinna, Vasuda, Vasudha, and Para.
Likewise, Parāyaṇā, Sūkṣmā, Sandhyā, Prajñā, Prabhā, Niśā,
Amoghā, Vidyutā, and Kīrtti— these and others grant all desires.

These [goddesses], with smiling faces, should have the luster of streaks of lightning; they are immersed in the limbs of their beloved ones, holding lotuses and gestures of fearlessness in their hands. (73)
In the Gautamīya:
"This placement [of mantras] beginning with Keśava, by the mere act of placement, bestows the state of being Acyuta upon embodied beings; this is the truth, the truth—there is no doubt."
Having uttered the syllables of the Mātṛkā, one should recollect "to Keśava";
then one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa), beginning with "and for Kīrti, joined with *namaḥ*," and so forth.
In the *Āgamanakalpadruma*:
"One should know the letters of the Mātṛkā from 'A' to 'Kṣa' joined with the vowels in their proper order;
then the sequence is: the Deity in the dative case (ending in -ṅe), likewise the Śakti, and finally 'Namaḥ'."
Then [salutations] to Keśava, to Kīrti, to Kānti, and to Nārāyaṇa.
This sequence is established by such statements from the Agastyasaṃhitā;
it is not, however, "Obeisance to Keśava and Kīrti," and so forth.
Likewise, this placement (nyāsa) beginning with the Śrī-bīja should be performed by one desiring worldly enjoyment (bhukti).
For example: *Oṃ śrīṃ aṃ keśavāya kīrttyai namaḥ*, and so forth. || 75 ||
And likewise in the Gautamiya:
"Having first uttered the *praṇava*, immediately thereafter the *śrībīja*;
then one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the letters of the *mātṛkā*. I shall explain that method [beginning] with the *vāgbhava*."
Or else, by performing this placement (nyāsa), one shall attain the status of Vāgīśvara.
Whatever initial placement one performs, the arrangement of the limbs (aṅgakalpanā) should be done with its seed-syllable.
In this manner, one should perform the placement preceded by the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī.
Having attained mindfulness, fortitude, and great fortune, one shall go to the state of Hari at the end.

Then follows the Nyāsa of the Principles (tattva): one should utter the letters beginning with *ma* and ending with *kha*, as well as the seed-syllables (*bīja*), one by one; having pronounced "Salutation to the Supreme" (*namaḥ parāya*), one should then say "Salutation to the Self of the Principle" (*tattvātmane namaḥ*).
Thus, according to the view of Gautama, the term *tattva* is employed everywhere;
for example:
"Oṃ, salutation to the supreme soul of the principle of life (*jīvatattva*); salutation!"
*Bhaṃ*, salutation to the supreme Prāṇa-tattva; salutation to the self.
These two [syllables] are for all the limbs.
*Baṃ*, salutation to the supreme Mati-tattva; salutation to the self.

Phaṃ, salutation to the supreme self whose essence is the principle of ego (ahaṃkāra-tattva); Paṃ, salutation to the supreme self whose essence is the principle of mind (manas-tattva). These three [syllables] are placed in the heart.

Naṃ, obeisance to the supreme one whose essence is the principle of sound; obeisance to the head. Dhaṃ, obeisance to the supreme one whose essence is the principle of touch; obeisance to the mouth. Daṃ, obeisance to the supreme one whose essence is the principle of form; obeisance to the heart.

*Thaṃ*—salutation to the Supreme, to the Self whose essence is taste; salutation to the secret place. *Taṃ*—salutation to the Supreme, to the Self whose essence is smell; salutation to the two feet. *Ṇaṃ*—salutation to the Supreme, to the Self whose essence is hearing; salutation to the two ears.

Ḍhaṃ, salutation to the supreme self whose essence is the principle of skin; salutation to the skin. Ḍaṃ, salutation to the supreme self whose essence is the principle of the eyes; salutation to the two eyes.
Ṭhaṃ, salutation to the supreme one, the essence of the tongue; salutation to the tongue. Ṭaṃ, salutation to the supreme one, the essence of the nose; salutation to the two nostrils.
Ñaṃ, obeisance to the supreme essence of speech; obeisance to the speech-faculty. Jhaṃ, obeisance to the supreme essence of the hand; obeisance to the two hands.
Jaṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the essence of the feet; salutation to the feet. Chaṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the essence of wind; salutation to the secret organ.
Caṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the essence of the generative organ; salutation to the penis.

Ṅaṃ, obeisance to the supreme one, the self of the element of space; obeisance to the head. Ghaṃ, obeisance to the supreme one, the self of the element of air; obeisance to the mouth. Gaṃ, obeisance to the supreme one, the self of the element of fire; obeisance to the heart.
*Khaṃ*, salutation to the supreme one, the self of the water-element; salutation at the base of the *liṅga*.
*Kaṃ*, salutation to the supreme one, the self of the earth-element; salutation at the feet. (77)
And so it is said in the Dīpikā:
"Having thus made the body [of mantras] manifest, one should perform the deposition of the principles (tattvanyāsa),
preceded by the syllable *ma* and accompanied by the obeisance (*namas*) at the end of each supreme syllable."
Furthermore, for the sake of others and for yourself, do not abandon that truth, but extract it in its proper sequence.

The practitioner of mantra, having joined the individual soul (jīva) and the vital breath (prāṇa) within the entire body, should place the intellect (mati), ego (ahaṃkāra), and mind (manas) in the center;
then, in the mouth, heart, secret parts, and feet, he should likewise place the group of qualities (guṇagaṇa) preceded by sound (śabda).
That which resides in the ears and so forth, beginning with the ear.

One should withdraw the group of senses, beginning with speech and the rest, into the self; the group beginning with space [the elements] into the head, mouth, heart, crown, and feet; and the lotus of the heart into the heart.
"Śaṃ, obeisance to the supreme one, the essence of the heart-lotus; obeisance to the self in the heart."
Haṃ, salutation to the Supreme, whose essence is the solar orb pervaded by twelve digits; salutation to the heart.
Saṃ, salutation to the Supreme, whose essence is the lunar orb pervaded by sixteen digits; salutation.
In the heart: *Raṃ*, salutation to the heart, which is the essence of the fire-maṇḍala pervaded by ten digits; salutation to the heart.
Yaṃ, obeisance to the Supreme, the Self of the Puruṣatattva, to Vāsudeva; obeisance to the head.
Yaṃ, obeisance to the Supreme, the Self of the Puruṣatattva, to Saṅkarṣaṇa; obeisance to the mouth.
Laṃ, obeisance to the Supreme, the Self of the Viśvatattva, to Pradyumna; obeisance to the heart.
*Vaṃ*, obeisance to Aniruddha, the supreme refuge, whose essence is the principle of cessation; obeisance to his *liṅga*.
*Laṃ*, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, the supreme, whose essence is all principles; obeisance to his feet.
*Kṣrauṃ*, obeisance to Nṛsiṃha, the supreme, whose essence is the principle of wrath; obeisance to all his limbs.
And likewise in the Gautamiya:
"One should place the seed-syllable *śaṃ*, the reality of the heart-lotus, within the heart;
one should place the seed-syllable *haṃ*, the reality of the solar disc, within the heart."
One should place the seed-syllable *saṃ*, the principle of the lunar disc, in the heart;
one should place the seed-syllable *raṃ*, the principle of the fiery disc, there;
and the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, the principle of Parameṣṭhin, as well as Vāsudeva, upon the head.
One should place the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, the principle of the individual soul (*puruṣatattva*), and Saṅkarṣaṇa in the mouth;
and the seed-syllable *laṃ*, the principle of the universe (*viśvatattva*), and Pradyumna in the heart.

One should place the seed-syllable *vaṃ* and the principle of Nivṛtti, along with Aniruddha, upon the anus; the seed-syllable *laṃ* and the principle of Sarvatattva, along with Nārāyaṇa, upon the feet;
and the seed-syllable *kṣrauṃ* and the principle of Kopa, along with Nṛsiṃha, upon all the limbs.
Having thus assigned the principles (tattvas), one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma).
The result is stated in that very [text]:
"Then the practitioner, for the sake of attaining perfection, should perform the deposition of the principles (tattvanyāsa);
by doing so, he attains the very form of the God."

Then, having performed *prāṇāyāma* according to the rules and having performed the *pīṭhanyāsa*, one should place [the mantras] upon the filaments— starting from the east and proceeding clockwise, including the center— with "Oṃ, obeisance to Vimalā," and likewise to Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, Yogā, Prahvī, Satyā, and Īśānā.
For the sake of bestowing grace:
upon that, [one should offer] "Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the Blessed One, the Self of all beings, Vāsudeva;
salutation to the one whose self is the lotus-throne of the yoga of union with the Self of all. (80)
And so it is stated in the Nibandha:
"The powers are Vimalā, Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, and Yogā; Prahvī, Satyā, and Īśānā, while Anugrahā is remembered as the ninth. (81)
He states the recitation of the seat-mantra (pīṭhamantra): One should say "namo bhagavate," then utter the word "viṣṇave," and thereafter say "sarvabhūtātmane vāsudevāya."
Then follows the word *sarvātmasaṃyoga*, followed by the word *yogapadma*;
ending with "to the seat-self" (*pīṭhātmane*) and preceded by the *tāra* (the syllable *oṃ*), this is the mantra of Hari. (82)
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seer and so forth.
It is as follows:
on the head, "Salutation to the Seer Sādhyanārāyaṇa."
In the mouth: salutation to the Gāyatrī metre of the Goddess.
In the heart: salutation to the deity, the illustrious Viṣṇu.
And likewise:
Sādhyanārāyaṇa is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi), and the meter (chandas) has been proclaimed;
for this mantra, the goddess Gāyatrī is the meter and the imperishable Viṣṇu is the deity.
Then, the placement of mantras on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*):
*namaḥ* to Kruddholka with both thumbs;
*svāhā* to Maholka with both index fingers.
Vaṣaṭ to Vīrolka with the two middle fingers;
Huṃ to Atyulka with the two ring fingers;
Phaṭ to Sahasrolka with the two little fingers.
The same applies to the heart and the other [limbs].
And so it is stated in the *Prapañcasāra*:
"Kruddholkā is declared to be the heart; Maholkā is remembered as the head."
The *śikhā* is declared for Vīrolka, the *kavaca* is remembered for Atyulka, and the *astra* is said to belong to Sahasrolka; this is considered the arrangement of the limbs (*aṅgakalpti*).
Then, one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantra:
*oṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *naṃ śirase svāhā*, *moṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *nāṃ kavacāya hūṃ*, *rāṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*, *yaṃ astrāya phaṭ*.
Nāṃ, obeisance on the right side; yaṃ, obeisance on the left side. || 85 ||
And so it is said:
"One should perform the six ancillaries (ṣaḍaṅga) with the first six syllables of the mantra;
then, with the remaining syllables, one should place them on the belly and the two sides."
Then, having performed the binding of the directions with the mantra "Oṃ namaḥ sudarśanāya astrāya phaṭ," one should perform the ritual placement of the mantra (mantranyāsa).
And so it is said:
Then one should perform the placement of mantras (mantranyāsa), which bestows the fruit of all desires;
without which that [rite], being demonic, would not be perfect and would become fruitless. 86.
Namely: Oṃ namaḥ at the base; Naṃ mamaḥ at the heart; Moṃ namaḥ at the mouth;
Nāṃ namaḥ and Rāṃ namaḥ at the roots of the arms; Yaṃ namaḥ and Ṇāṃ namaḥ at the feet; and Yaṃ at the navel.
*Namaḥ*.
Thus [one should place the syllables] on the throat, the navel, the heart, the two breasts, the two sides, and the back;
and on the head, the mouth, the two eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils, and the two hands.
In the joints and fingers; likewise in the feet, in the joints and fingers;
in the heart, in the seven constituents, and in the vital breaths.
The constituents (*dhātu*): skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and semen are the constituents.
[They are located] in the head, the eyes, the mouth, the heart, the abdomen, and the thighs.
One should assign [the mantras] to the two calves, the two feet, the two cheeks, the two shoulders, the two thighs, and the two feet, as well as to the discus, the conch, the mace, and the lotus.
And so it is stated in the *Nibandha*:
"One should place the letters of the mantra upon the body using the mantra of the bound *dikcakra* [diagram]:
at the foundation (*ādhāra*), the heart, the mouth, the roots of the arms and thighs, and the navel."
Next, [one should place them] on the throat, the navel, the heart, the breasts, and the sides;
thereafter, on the head, mouth, eyes, ears, and nose;
then on the joints of the arms and feet, the fingers, the bodily constituents (dhātus), the vital breaths (prāṇas), and the region of the heart.

One should place the syllables one by one on the head, the right eye, the face, the heart, the belly, the thighs, the shanks, and the two feet; likewise on the cheeks, the shoulders, the thighs, and the feet.
Being composed, one should also place them upon the conch, the discus, the mace, the lotus, and the feet.
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the cage of forms (mūrtipañjara):
on the forehead, *oṃ aṃ* to Keśava and Dhātṛ, obeisance; in the belly, *naṃ āṃ* to Nārāyaṇa and Aryaman, obeisance.
Having placed *ṣoṃ iṃ* in the heart, [one says] "Salutation to Mitra.
In the pit of the throat, *bhaṃ īṃ*, "Salutation to Govinda Varuṇa.
On the right side, *gaṃ uṃ*, "Salutation to Viṣṇu Aṃśu."
On the right shoulder: *vaṃ ūṃ*, salutation to Madhusūdana, the Lord Bhaga.
On the right side of the neck: *teṃ eṃ*, salutation to Trivikrama, Vivasvat.
On the left side: *vāṃ aiṃ*, salutation to Vāmana, Indra.
On the left shoulder: *suṃ oṃ śrīdharāya pūṣṇe namaḥ*.
On the left side of the neck: *deṃ auṃ hṛṣīkeśāya parjanyāya namaḥ*.
On the back: *vāṃ aṃ padmanābhāya tvaṣṭre namaḥ*.
At the crown [of the head], one should say: "Oṃ, adoration to Viṣṇu Dāmodara.
Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the kirīṭa-mantra to be mentioned hereafter, one should place the twelve-syllable mantra upon the head. || 89 ||
And likewise, in the Nibandha: "The eight-syllabled [mantra] should be known as having the meaning of the eight prakṛtis;
through the combination of the four-fold selves, it is declared by the wise to be the distinguished twelve-syllabled [mantra]."
Therefore, those [syllables] beginning with the mantra-letters are conjoined with the twelve vowels.
Accompanied by the twelve Ādityas,
one should assign the twelve forms—
Keśava and the others— in sequence upon the body according to the procedure that will be described.
One should place Keśava on the forehead with the Dhātṛ-mantra, and Nārāyaṇa again on the belly;
Mādhava at the region of the throat with the Aryaman-mantra, and Govinda on the right side with the Varuṇa-mantra.
One should worship Viṣṇu with the syllable *aṃśu* on the shoulder, and Madhusūdana with *bhaga*.
On the neck is Trivikrama, joined with Vivasvat;
immediately following is Vāmana, situated on the left side, with Indra upon his shoulder.
With Pūṣan [he worships] the one named Śrīdhara on the neck, joined with Parjanya;
the one called Hṛṣīkeśa on the back, and after that, Padmanābha.
Afterwards, one should place Dāmodara on the back by Tvaṣṭṛ and Viṣṇu on the hump;
then, one should place the great twelve-syllable mantra upon the head.
Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-vinyāsa) with the Kirīṭa mantra.
And likewise in the Gautamiya:
"One should place the excellent twelve-syllable mantra in the aperture of Brahma (the crown of the head); Vāsudeva himself becomes manifest, pervaded by his splendor."
Having extracted the three measures (trimātrika), one should write "namo bhagavate vāsudevāya" in the dative case;
this mantra is a celestial wish-fulfilling tree.
By the mere consciousness of this, Vāsudeva is born.
Then one should recite this mantra:
"He whose body is the nectar of consciousness, possessing the brilliance of ten million suns, who resides upon the crown of the head— he is Vāsudeva, the entire form."
Just as pure water, when sprinkled, pervades that which is moistened, so too does [the mantra] pervade that which is infused with the clearly manifested syllables of the mantra.
And the fruit of this ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is as follows:
The placement of the cage of those forms has been declared by the Supreme Lord;
by performing this placement once, the practitioner of mantra becomes the unsurpassed form of Viṣṇu.
The placement of the cage of forms (*mūrtipañjaranyāsa*) is indeed manifold:
some say, "Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to Keśava together with Dhātṛ";
others say, "Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to Keśava and Dhātṛ."
"Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ together with Keśava"—thus [some] say on the other side;
that is not correct.
One should meditate upon Vāsudeva as a single syllable, devoid of the neuter gender,
consisting of a single vowel joined with the bindu, and ending in the dative case, beginning with Keśava.
Likewise, having spoken of Dhātṛ and the others, the Nyāsa with "namas" is declared;
thus, from the Nāradīya Tantra, they say: "Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ, the wind of the region. Then:
"Oṃ, [obeisance to Him] adorned with a crown, armlets, necklaces, makaras, and earrings..."

Salutation to Him who holds the conch, discus, mace, and lotus in His hands; whose chest is marked with the Śrīvatsa and adorned with the goddesses Śrī and Bhūmi; whose radiant rays consist of His own self-luminous light; and who possesses the splendor of a thousand suns.
Having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with this mantra and displayed the mudrās, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*).
And so it is stated in the *Prapañcasāra*: "The knower of mantras, having uttered the words 'kirīṭa' (crown), 'keyūra' (armlet), 'hāra' (necklace),
and 'kuṇḍala' (earring) at the end of the syllable *ma*, [should utter] the words 'śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-ādi' (conch, discus, mace, and so forth), and 'padma-hasta' (lotus in hand)."

Having spoken the words "O wearer of yellow garments," and having addressed the chest marked with the Śrīvatsa, one should then utter the phrase "together with Śrī and Bhūmi," and finally speak the word "the state consisting of one's own self-luminous light."

Having uttered "Dīpta" and "Karāya," followed by "to him whose splendor is like a thousand suns," there should be the mantra beginning with the *praṇava* (oṃ) ending at the heart; then follow the two mantras beginning with "Kirīṭa.
Having first performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, one should meditate upon the supreme Nārāyaṇa.
As for meditation:
[one should meditate on Him] who constantly bears a conch, a mace, a lotus, and a discus, shining like ten million rising suns, and whose two sides are graced by Indirā and Vasumatī.

I worship Him who wears a crown, armlets, necklaces, and earrings; who is clad in yellow garments and illuminated by the Kaustubha gem; who sustains the universe and bears upon His chest the shining mark of Śrīvatsa.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the ritual installation of the conch.
Regarding that, the *Gautamīya* states concerning the Vaiṣṇava vessel:
"O Brahmin-sage, a copper vessel is considered extremely dear to Viṣṇu."
In the same way, the conch is proclaimed to be the foremost among all vessels;
likewise, earthen, golden, and silver vessels are prescribed.
These five vessels for Hari are pure; one should not employ any other there.
Regarding the offering of *naivedya* there, [it is said]:
"In a vessel of gold, or a copper vessel, or a silver one, or on a lotus leaf," and so forth.
In the *Bhaktikalpadruma*:

A wise person should prepare an offering for Śrī Hari in a vessel made of gold, silver, bell-metal, copper, or even clay, or one made from the leaves of the *pālāśa* tree. And likewise, it is stated in the *Puraścaraṇacandrikā*:
In gold, silver, and so forth. || 97 ||

Then, after the general worship of the pedestal (sāmānyapīṭhapūjā), having performed the worship of the pedestal together with the powers (śaktis) such as Vimalā and so forth, and having meditated again, one should perform upon the visualized form (kalpitamūrti) the rites beginning with invocation (āvāhana) up to the offering of five handfuls of flowers (pañcapuṣpāñjali) by means of the root mantra (mūla).
One should begin the offering of the enclosures (*āvaraṇapūjā*).
It is as follows:
in the southeast corner, *oṃ kruddholkāya hṛdayāya namaḥ*.
To the great meteor in the southwest, for the head, svāhā! To the hero-meteor in the northwest, for the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ!
To the exceeding meteor in the northeast, for the armor, huṃ!
*Phaṭ* to the weapon-mantra consisting of a thousand meteors in all directions.
Then, in the filaments [of the lotus], starting from the east: *Oṃ namaḥ*, *Naṃ namaḥ*, *Moṃ namaḥ*, *Nāṃ namaḥ*, *Rāṃ namaḥ*, *Yaṃ namaḥ*, *Ṇāṃ namaḥ*, *Yaṃ namaḥ*.
Then, on the petals in the directions starting from the east: *oṃ vāsudevāya namaḥ*, *oṃ saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ*, *oṃ pradyumnāya namaḥ*, *oṃ aniruddhāya namaḥ*.
On the petals in the corners starting from the southeast: *oṃ śāntyai namaḥ*, and likewise for *śriyai*, *sarasvatyai*, and *ratyai*.

Then, at the tips of the eight petals in the directions starting from the east: *oṃ cakrāya namaḥ*; likewise for the conch, the mace, the lotus, the *kaustubha* gem, the pestle, the sword, and the forest garland.
Outside of that, at the front: *oṃ garuḍāya namaḥ*; to the right: *oṃ śaṅkhanidhaye*; to the left: *oṃ*.
To Padmanidhi; in the west, Oṃ Dhvajāya; in the southeast, Oṃ Vighnāya; in the southwest, Oṃ Āryāyai; in the northwest, Oṃ Durgāyai; in the northeast, Oṃ Senānyai.
*Namaḥ* (homage) everywhere.

Having worshipped Indra and the others, as well as the vajra and the other implements, outside of that, and having offered incense and lamps, one should present the food offering (naivedya). || 98ka ||
For example:
having brought the food offering for the deity, and having given water for the feet, the respectful offering (arghya), and water for sipping,
one should sprinkle the food offering with the mantra *phaṭ*, and protect it with the wheel mudrā (*cakramudrā*).
Having purified the mass of defects with the mantra *yaṃ*, having incinerated the defects with *raṃ*,
and having visualized it as filled with a stream of nectar from the left hand, made immortal by the syllable *vaṃ*,
one should recite the root mantra eight times.

Then, having rendered [the offering] nectarine by means of the *dhenumudrā* while reciting "Vam," and having worshipped the food offering with scents and flowers, one should offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) to the deity with the root mantra; then, with palms joined in reverence, one should pray to Hari.
Having visualized that "greatness shall flow forth from his mouth," one should offer water for the food offering (naivedya) while reciting the root mantra ending with *svāhā*.
Then, having recited the root mantra, [one says]: "This food offering (*naivedya*) is for [Name] Devatā; obeisance (*namaḥ*)."
Then, having set aside the *naivedya*, one should offer the food with the mantra: "Oṃ, I offer this oblation to you; may you enjoy it, O Hari.
Having thus presented the *naivedya*, one should give water to the deity [named] Amuka with the mantra: "This water is the spreading of ambrosia (*amṛtopastaraṇamasi*).
Then, displaying the *grāsamudrā* with the left hand, [one should proceed] with the right hand...
One should display the mudrās beginning with Prāṇa.
As follows: "Oṃ prāṇāya svāhā"—with this, one should touch the little finger and the ring finger with the thumb.
Saying "Oṃ apānāya svāhā," one should touch the ring finger and middle finger with the thumb.
Saying "Oṃ vyānāya svāhā," one should touch the middle finger and ring finger with the thumb.
Saying "Oṃ udānāya svāhā," one should touch the index, middle, and ring fingers with the thumb.
Saying "Oṃ samānāya svāhā," one should touch all the fingers with the thumb. || 99 ||

Then, touching the tips of the ring fingers with the two thumbs, one should display the *mudrās* for the food offering (*naivedya*) while reciting: "Ṭhrauṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Inner Self, Aniruddha; I offer this food.
Having recited the root mantra and saying, "I satisfy [the deity] Amuka-deva," one should perform this fourfold offering.

Having satiated [the deity] and offered water with the mantra "amṛtāpidhānam asi" for such-and-such deity, one should place that radiance within the mouth of the deity and then offer the water for sipping (ācamanīya) and so forth;
this is the sequence for the offering of food (naivedya) everywhere in the Vaiṣṇava tradition.
Then, one should complete the ritual up to the dismissal (visarjana) according to the sequence of the general procedure.
The preliminary practice (puraścaraṇa) for this consists of sixteen hundred thousand recitations (japa).
And so it is said:
With a concentrated mind, one should recite this mantra one hundred and eight times;
then, one should perform a fire sacrifice with lotuses soaked in honey, using a tenth part of that number.
Now, the mantras of Śrī Rāma:

Ananta, Agnyāsana, Saṃdu, and the seed-syllable (Bīja), followed by "Rāmāya" and the heart-mantra (Hṛt); this six-syllabled mantra is declared to be a wish-fulfilling jewel for those who worship it. (1)
The worship of this [deity] is as follows:
having performed the morning rites and so forth, up to the *pīṭhanyāsa* as prescribed for Vaiṣṇava practice, one should perform the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*.
For example: "Obeisance to Brahmā, the seer, on the head; obeisance to the Gāyatrī meter, on the mouth; obeisance to Śrī Rāma, the deity, on the heart. (2)
Then, the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*):
