Klīṃ! To the three eyes of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, the undiminished power, Vauṣaṭ!
Sauḥ! Anantaśakti Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, astrāya phaṭ!
Likewise, in the Navaratneśvara:
omniscience, eternal contentment, beginningless awakening, and sovereignty.
Śivā and the others say that the six limbs of Śiva and Śivā are unimpaired power and infinity;
having joined the name at the end of the seed-syllable, one should append the [six] classes to form the six-limbed [mantra]. (87)
Then follows the placement (nyāsa) of Vaśinī and the others;
that has been stated as a concise practice. Then follows the placement consisting of the nine wombs (navayoni).
And thus:
one should install the nine-yoni form of the youthful Mistress of Tripura.
The practical application, however, has been stated in the section on Bhairavī.
Again, having recited Bālā, one should contemplate [it] as a sphere;
again, having recited Bālā, one should contemplate a square. || 88 ||
Now, the placement of the seats (*pīṭha*) and the principles (*tattva*):
as follows;
having uttered the root *Vāgbhava*, [one places it] in the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*), in the abode of Kāmagiri, which has Mitrīśanātha as its essence.
"Salutation to the Śrīpādukā of the Goddess Rudrātmaśakti-Śrī-Kāmeśvarī" at the Ādhāra;
having uttered the second Kūṭa, [one should worship] at the Sūryacakra in the Jālandhara-pīṭha,
which has Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha as its essence.
"Salutation to the Śrī-pādukā of the goddess Śrī-Vajreśvarī, the power of the self of Viṣṇu," [this is] in the heart.

Having uttered the third *kūṭa*, "Salutation to the Śrī-pādukā of the goddess Śrī-Bhagamālinī, the power of the self of Brahmā, whose essence is Uḍḍīśanātha at the seat of Pūrṇagiri in the lunar wheel (*somacakra*)," [this is] on the forehead.

Having uttered the *trikūṭa*, [one should offer salutation] at the *brahmarandhra* to the *śrīpādukā* of the goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī— the power of the self of Brahman— residing as the essence of the venerable Caryānātha in the seat of Uḍḍīyāna within the wheel of the Supreme Brahman (*paraṃbrahmacakra*).
In the *Kalāmṛta*:
"Uttering the first seed-syllable of the root-mantra, one should join the seats that bestow accomplishment to the fire-wheel, and again to the abode of Kāmagiri."
Then, O Pārvatī, having uttered the word "Mitrīśā," one should worship the Śrīpādukā of Kāmeśvarī, who is the essence of the Lord (Nātha) and the power (Śakti) whose nature is Rudra,
while reciting the second seed-syllable followed by the word "namaḥ."
One should then join the station of Jālandhara to the Solar Wheel (Sūryacakra).
And upon the seat consisting of the Lord Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha, [one joins] the station of Vajreśvarī.
I worship the venerable sandals of the Goddess, the power whose essence is Viṣṇu.
O Pārvatī, having uttered the third word *namaḥ* as the seed-syllable (*bīja*),
one should join it with the word *pūrṇāgiri* in the lunar wheel (*somacakra*); then,
upon the seat (*pīṭha*) consisting of Uḍḍīśanātha, one places the word *bhagamālinī*.

O Pārvatī, having uttered the entire mantra beginning with "namaḥ" and ending with "devī brahmātmaśaktiśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi," [one should then recite] the state of the Supreme Brahman in the Cakra, followed by the state of Uḍḍīyāna.
Having joined the *pada* on the seat (*pīṭha*), then the *pada* consisting of Caryānātha;
at the end of the word "Mahātripura," then the *pada* "Sundarī";
then, at the end of the *devī-brahma-pada*, [one joins] "Śakti-śrīpādukā."
O Śivā, first is the sequence beginning with "I worship" (pūjayāmi) and ending with "salutation" (namaḥ).
And the locations are:
in the Mūlādhāra, the heart, the forehead, and the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra). (89)
Then follows the deposition of the principles (tattvanyāsa).
As follows: having uttered the Vāgbhava-kūṭa, [one says] "to her who pervades the principle of the self" (ātmatattvavyāpikāyai).
Salutation to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī at the Ādhāra.
Having uttered the second *kūṭa*, [one should say]: "Salutation to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the *vidyā-tattva*, at the heart."
Having uttered the third peak-syllable, [one offers] "Obeisance to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the Śiva-tattva," at the center of the eyebrows.
Having uttered the three peaks, [one offers] "Obeisance to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades all the tattvas."
In the aperture of Brahmā. || 89ka ||
Then follows the placement of the fifteen [syllables].
It is as follows:
at the *mūlādhāra*, in the heart, in the two eyes, in the two ears, and in the two nostrils.
One should place the syllables of the root mantra, ending with "namaḥ," individually upon the face, the two arms, the back, the pair of knees, and the navel. || 90 ||
Then follows the placement of the sixteen [syllables]:
according to the Nibandha,
one should contemplate the Pūrṇavidyā of red color in the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
The wise practitioner should rotate the Saubhāgyadaṇḍinī mudrā on the left shoulder;
he should place the Ripujihvāgrahā mudrā on the sole of the left foot;
and at the conclusion of the Vyāpaka mudrā, having cast the Yonimudrā into his mouth and offered salutation, [he should proceed].
Furthermore, one should place that rosary of sixteen syllables at the aperture of Brahma (the crown of the head), the wrist, and the forehead.
Now follows the ritual placement of withdrawal (saṃhāranyāsa):
Then, O Pārvatī, [one should worship] on the feet, the calves, the knees, the waist, the backs of the fingers,
the navel, both sides, as well as the breasts,
the shoulders, the hands, the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), the face, and the eyebrows.
Then, [he should apply them] successively to the region of the ears and to the two wrists.
Thus ends the ritual placement of withdrawal (saṃhāranyāsa). || 91 ||
Now, the sequence of placement: five [syllables] on the fingers of the hands, three in the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head), the mouth, and the heart;
one from the navel down to the feet.
One [segment] from the throat to the navel;
one from the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra) to the throat;
and five on the toes of the feet.
Thus concludes the placement of stability (sthitinyāsa). || 92 ||
Now, the Sṛṣṭinyāsa (the rite of placement in the order of creation):
[one places the mantras] at the aperture of Brahmā, the forehead, the eyes, the ears, the nose, the head, the lips, the lower teeth,
the upper teeth, the tongue, the chin, the back, all the limbs, the heart, the two breasts, and the belly.
And one should duly place sixteen syllables upon the liṅga.
Now, the placement of the *nāda* (*nādanyāsa*): salutation to the unmodified *nāda* on the head; salutation to the void *nāda* on the forehead;
salutation to the tactile *nāda* between the eyebrows; salutation to the *nāda*-of-*nāda* at the nose.

Salutation to Dhvanināda in the mouth; salutation to Bindunāda in the throat; salutation to Śaktināda in the heart; salutation to Jīvanāda in the navel; salutation to Akṣarātmakanāda in the mūlādhāra.
And so it is said in the Kulāmṛta:
"First is the unmodified sound (avikṛnnāda), then the sound of emptiness (śūnyanāda);
after that, the sound of touch (sparśanāda), the sound of resonance (nādanāda), and beyond that, the sound of vibration (dhvanināda)."
O Śivā, one should place *vindunāda*, *śaktināda*, *jīvanāda*,
and then *akṣarātmakanāda* ending with *namaḥ* in sequence upon the head,
the forehead, the space between the eyebrows, the nose, the mouth, and the throat.
The wise one should place the ninefold resonance (navanāda) upon the regions of the heart, the navel, and the root.
Now, the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*):
In the *Jñānārṇava*, it is said that the first placement is with Gaṇeśa, and the second is considered to be with the planets.
The third [type of] placement (nyāsa) is by means of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), the fourth by the yoginīs,
the fifth is by the zodiac signs (rāśis), and the sixth is said to be by the sacred seats (pīṭhas).
This sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa) has been proclaimed as invincible everywhere;
thus,
with the Yoginīs stationed upon his limbs, he is to be worshipped by all yogis.
In all the worlds, there is no one more worthy of worship than him, who is radiant with his father and mother;
he alone is the object of worship for everyone, for he himself is the Supreme Lord.
O Goddess Pārvatī, he who bows down to you without having performed the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) shall soon meet his death and fall into hell. (97)
The seer is Bṛhadāraṇyaka, the meter is Anuṣṭubh, the deity is Gaṇeśa; the application is for the rite of ritual placement (nyāsa) and for recitation (japa). || 98 ||
*Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ*, obeisance to Vighneśvara and Śrī—thus on the head.
*3 (Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ)* *āṃ*, obeisance to Vighnarāja and Hrī—thus on the mouth. *3 iṃ*, obeisance to Vināyaka and Tuṣṭi—thus on the right eye.
3 *Īṃ* obeisance to Śivottama and Śānti—thus on the left eye; *E* *Uṃ* obeisance to Vighna and Hṛtpuṣṭi—on the right ear; 3 *Ūṃ* obeisance to Vighnakartṛ and Sarasvatī—on the left ear.
3 Ṛṃ, obeisance to Vighnarāja and Rati on the right nostril; 3 Ṝṃ, obeisance to Gaṇanāyaka and Medhā on the left nostril; 3 Ḷṃ, obeisance to Ekadanta and Kānti on the right cheek.
3 ḶṂ, salutation to Dvidanta and Kāminī on the left cheek; 3 EṂ, salutation to Gajavaktra and Mohinī on the lip;
3 AIṂ, salutation to Nirañjana and Jaṭā on the lower lip.
3 Oṃ, obeisance to Kandarpa and Bhṛtīvrā on the upper teeth. 3 Auṃ, obeisance to Dīrghavaktra and Jvālinī on the lower teeth.
3 Aṃ, obeisance to Saṅkarṣaṇa and Nandā at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
3 AḤ: Salutation to Vṛṣadhvaja and Surasā on the face.
3 KAṂ: Salutation to Gaṇanātha and Kāmarūpiṇī on the right shoulder. 3 KHAṂ: Salutation to Gajendra and Śubhā on the right elbow.
3 Gaṃ, obeisance to Sūrpakarṇa and Jayinī at the wrists; 3 Ghaṃ, obeisance to Trinetra and Satyā at the bases of the fingers;
Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Lambodara and Vighneśī at the tips of the fingers.
3 Caṃ, salutation to the two who are the embodiments of great joy, on the left shoulder;
3 Chaṃ, salutation to the two who grant the desires of the four forms, on the left elbow;
3 Jaṃ, salutation to the two who are overwhelmed by the intoxication of Sadāśiva, at the wrist.
3 Jhaṃ, homage to Āmoda and Vikaṭā at the base of the fingers; 3 Ñaṃ, homage to Durmukha and Ghūrṇā at the tips of the fingers; 3 Ṭaṃ, homage to Sumukha and Bhūtinī below the right hip.
3 Ṭhaṃ, salutation to Pramoda and Bhūmi at the right knee; 3 Ḍaṃ, salutation to Ekapāda and Mati at the ankle;
3 Ḍhaṃ, salutation to Dvijihva and Ramā below the toes.
3 ṆAṂ, salutation to Śūra and Mānuṣa at the tips of the fingers;
3 TAṂ, salutation to Vīra and Makaradhvaja on the lower left hip;
3 THAṂ, salutation to Ṣaṇmukha and Vikarṇa at the knee.
3 *daṃ* to Varada and Bhṛkuṭi, *namas* to the secret place; 3 *dhaṃ* to Vāmadeva and Lajjā, *namaḥ* below the fingers;
3 *naṃ* to Vakratuṇḍa and Dīrghaghoṇā, *namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers.
3 Paṃ, obeisance to Dviraṇḍa and Dhanurdhara on the right side; 3 Phaṃ, obeisance to Senānī and Yāminī on the left side;
3 Baṃ, obeisance to Grāmaṇī and Rātri at the back.
3 Bhaṃ, Bhattacandrikābhyāṃ namaḥ on the two breasts;
3 Maṃ, Vimalaśaśiprabhābhyāṃ namaḥ on the belly; 3 Yaṃ, Mattavāhanalolābhyāṃ namaḥ on the heart.
3 *Raṃ*, salutation to Jaṭī and Capalākṣī on the right shoulder;
3 *Laṃ*, salutation to Muṇḍī and Ṛddhi on the hump; 3 *Vaṃ*, salutation to Khaḍgī and Durbhagā on the left shoulder.
3 *Śaṃ* to Vareṇya and Subhagā; *namaḥ* from the heart to the right hand.
3 *Ṣaṃ* to Vṛṣaketu and Śivā; *namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand.
3 *Saṃ* to Bhakṣyapriya and Durgā; *namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot.
3 *Haṃ*, salutation to Megha and Ānādakāminī, from the heart to the left foot;
3 *Laṃ*, salutation to Gajeśa and Kānyakubjā, from the heart to the abdomen; 3 *Kṣaṃ*, salutation to Gaṇeśa and Vighnahāriṇī, from the heart to the mouth.
And so it is stated in the Jñānārṇava: "Viśveśvara together with Śrī, Vighnarāja together with Hrī,
Vināyaka together with Tuṣṭi, and the supreme Śiva conjoined with Śānti."
Vighnahṛt is joined with Puṣṭi, and Vighnakartṛ is joined with Sarasvatī;
Vighnarāj is joined with Rati, and Medhā is joined with Gaṇanāyaka;
Ekadanta is joined with Kānti, and Dvidanta is joined with Kāminī.
Gajavaktra and Mohinī, Nirañjana and Jaṭaikata;
likewise Kandarpabhṛt and Tīvrā, as well as Dīrghavaktra, O beloved;
followed by Jvālinī, and then Nanda and Saṅkarṣaṇa.
Then Vṛṣadhvaja and Surasā were joined with Gaṇanātha; after them, Kāmarūpiṇikā and Gajendra with Śubhā;
then Sūrpakarṇa and Jayinī, and Trinetra joined with Satyā.
Lambodara, Vighneśī, Mahāmoda, Svarūpiṇī,
Caturmūrti, Kāmadā, followed by Sadāśivayutā;
then Madavihvalā by name, as well as Āmoda and Vikaṭā.
Durmukha, Ghūrṇā, Sumukha, Bhūtinī, Pramoda, Bhūmi, Ekapāda, Mati, Dvijihva joined with Ramā,
and Śūra joined with Mānuṣī.
O Daughter of the Mountain, thereafter Makaradhvaja was accompanied by Vīra.
Then Yanmukha, Vikarṇā, Varada, and Bhṛkuṭī; then Vāmadeva, Lajjā, and thereafter Vakratuṇḍa;
followed by Dīrghaghoṇā, together with Dviraṇḍaka and Dhanurdhara.
Senānī is joined with Yāminī; Grāmaṇī is conjoined with Rātri; Mata is associated with Candrikā; Vimala is with Śaśiprabhā;
Mattavāhana and Lola; and Jaṭī with Capalākṣiṇī.
Muṇḍī is endowed with supernatural power (ṛddhi), and Khaḍgī is subsequently joined by Durbhagā;
Vareṇya is with Subhagā, and likewise Vṛṣaketu is with Śivā;
Bhakṣyapriya is with Durgā, and Meghanāda is with Kāminī.
Gajeśa and Kānyakubjā, Gaṇeśa and Vighnahāriṇī—thus is the Gaṇeśa-nyāsa. || 99 ||
Now, the placement of the *grahas* (*grahanyāsa*):
3 (Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ) Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Āṃ; salutation to the two rays of the Sun in the heart.
3 Yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ soṃ, obeisance to Soma and Amara at the center of the eyebrows.
3 Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ aṃ, obeisance to Aṅgāraka and Rakta at the eyes.
3 Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ buṃ, obeisance to Budha and Jñānarūpa...
Above the heart:
3 Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ vṛṃ, obeisance to Vṛhaspati and Yaśasvinī at the throat.
3 taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ śuṃ, obeisance to Śukra and Āhlādinī at the throat;
3 paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ śaṃ, obeisance to Śanaiścara and Śakti at the navel.
3 Śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ rāṃ, salutations to Rāhu and Kṛṣṇa at the mouth.
3 Laṃ kṣaṃ keṃ, salutations to Ketu and Vāyu at the secret place.
And likewise in the Jñānārṇava:

One should place the Sun in the heart with the vowels; then the Moon with the *ya*-group. One should place Mars between the eyebrows with the *ka*-group, and Mercury in the three eyes with the *ca*-group.
Jupiter [is placed] in the heart with the *ṭa*-group.
O Goddess of gods, one should place Bha on the heart with the Ta-group, Bhṛgu on the throat with the Pa-group,
Śani at the navel, Rāhu in the mouth with the Śa-group,
and Ketu in the anus with the two La-s; thus, O fair-faced one, one should perform the ritual placement of the deities.
Now, the ritual placement of the constellations (*nakṣatrayāsa*):
(3 *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*) *Aṃ Āṃ*, salutation to Aśvinī on the forehead. (3 *Iṃ Īṃ*), salutation to Bharaṇī on the right eye.
3 uṃ ūṃ, salutation to Kṛttikā on the left eye; 3 ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ, salutation to Rohiṇī on the right ear;
3 eṃ, salutation to Mṛgaśirā on the left ear.
3 Aiṃ, obeisance to Ārdrā on the right nostril; 3 Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to Punarvasu on the left nostril;
3 Kaṃ, obeisance to Puṣyā on the throat.
3 Khaṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to Aśleṣā on the right shoulder; 3 Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Maghā on the left shoulder;
3 Caṃ, obeisance to Pūrvaphalgunī in the middle of the right arm.
3 chaṃ jaṃ, obeisance to Uttaraphalgunī, in the middle of the left arm; 3 jhaṃ ñaṃ, obeisance to Hastā, at the right wrist;
3 ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Citrā, at the left wrist.
3 Ḍaṃ, salutation to Svātī on the palm of the right hand; 3 Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ, salutation to Viśākhā on the palm of the left hand;
3 Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ, salutation to Anurādhā at the navel.
3 *Dhaṃ* to Jyeṣṭhā, salutation to the right hip region; 3 *Naṃ Paṃ Phaṃ* to Mūlā, salutation to the left hip region;
3 *Vaṃ* to Pūrvāṣāḍhā, salutation to the right thigh.
3 Bhaṃ, salutation to Uttarāṣāḍhā on the left thigh; 3 Maṃ, salutation to Śravaṇā on the right knee;
3 Yaṃ Raṃ, salutation to Dhaniṣṭhā on the left knee.
3 laṃ, obeisance to Śatabhiṣā on the right calf; 3 vaṃ śaṃ, obeisance to Pūrvabhādrapadā on the left calf;
3 ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ, obeisance to Uttarabhādrapadā on the right foot.
3. Laṃ kṣaṃ aṃ aḥ, obeisance to Revatī on the left foot. || 1 ||
Now, the Nyāsa of the Yoginīs:
(Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ) Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Ḍāṃ Ḍīṃ Duṃ Ḍaṃ Ma La Va Ra Yūṃ, to Ḍākinī, Māṃ.
Protect, protect! Salutation to the skin-self at the throat.

Kānta is joined with Kāminī; Bhrānta is indeed joined with Mohinī;

Ratipriya and Rāma, as well as Rātrinātha and Kubjikā;

Bhrānta joined with Kāmakalā, and Bhramāva with Asucañcalā.
Mohinī and Dīrghajihvā, Meṣaka and Mahāmati, as well as Mugdha and Lolākṣī, Mohavarddhanā and Bhṛṅginī, Mohaka and Capeṭā, and Manmatha accompanied by his mistress (Nāthā).
Mataṅga is joined with Mālinī; Bhṛṅgīśa is with Kalahasinī;
Viśvatomukha is joined with Gāyaka, and thereafter Gīti is with Gajanandikā.
Narttaka with Rañjinī, Meṣa endowed with Kānti,
Unmatta with Kalakaṇṭhā, Saṃvarttaka with Vṛkodarī,
Megha accompanied by Śyāmā, O Goddess, and Vimala with Śrīmatī, O Beloved.
O Goddess, one should place the Mātṛkās in their very locations within the Mātṛkā.
Now follows the placement (nyāsa) of the sixteen Nityās.
In the Jñānārṇava:
"The first Nityā Sundarī is Mahātripurasundarī."
Kāmeśvarī is proclaimed, as well as Bhagamālinī;
Nityaklinnā, Bheruṇḍā, and likewise Vahnivāsinī;
Vajreśvarī, Dūtī, Tvaritā, and Kulasundarī.
Nityā, Nīlapatākā, Vijayā, Sarvamaṅgalā,
Jvālāmālā, and Vicitrāntā— these fifteen are proclaimed.
Their mantras are found in the Jñānārṇava:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the unsurpassed Nityā-mantra:
one should utter the word *Bālāntara* at the end of the heart (*hṛt*), then the word *Kāmeśvarī*.
At the end of *icchākāmaphala*, one should utter the word *prade sarva*.
Then one should utter *sattvavaśam*, followed by *kari*, the station of the entire world (*sarvajagatpadam*).
At the end of the *kṣobhaṇa* [mantra], one should utter *kari* and inscribe three *huṃ* syllables.
Having inscribed the five arrows, one should [address] the young maiden with the *saṃhāra* [mantra].

O Śivā, this eternal Kāmeśvarī has been described here incidentally. One should write the Vāgbhava syllable followed by the word "bhaga," and then write "bhage bhagini. Then [one should write]: "bhagodari, bhagāṅge, bhagamāle, bhagāvahe."

In the secret place of the vulva, at the edge of the vulva, at the edge of the womb, and near the vulva; she who causes [semen] to fall at the very end, and then the one who brings power over the vulva;
thereafter, O lotus-eyed one, she whose form is the vulva should be drawn.
One should write "nityaklinne bhagaprānte svarūpe sarvamālikhet" (O eternally moist one, at the edge of the vulva, in your own form, write everything).
Then one should write "bhagāni me hyānayānte varade" (O giver of boons, bring the vulvas to me at the end).
Then "rete surete ca bhagaklinne klinnadrave" (In semen, O beautiful semen, in the moistened vulva, in the flowing moisture).

"O Mistress of the *bhaga*, moisten and dissolve all sentient beings! O Unfailing One, O Piercer of the *bhaga*, agitate and cause all sentient beings to tremble! O Mistress of the *bhaga*, one should utter the *vāgbhava* [syllable] preceded by *blūṃ jaṃ*."

*Bheṃ blūṃ moṃ heṃ blūṃ klinne*, and after that, *sarvāṇi ca bhagāny ante me vaśaṃ cānaya*. Then the feminine seed-syllable (*strībīja*) at the end of *hara*, which consists of the syllables of the Vedas.
Having written Bhuvaneśī, this is the Vidyā Bhagamālinī.

Having uttered the supreme seed-syllable (Parā-bīja), followed by "nityaklinne madadrave," and joined with the wife of Agni (Svāhā), this mantra is declared to be Nityaklinnā. First, having uttered the Praṇava (Oṃ).
Likewise, one should speak of a pair of goads.
In the middle of that, O Goddess, one should draw the syllable consisting of the letter *bha*.
One should draw the *ca*-group, omitting its last letter, situated within the fire.
Endowed with the fourteen vowels, and separately accompanied by the *bindu* and *nāda*,
this *vidyā* joined with the wife of fire (the *svāhā*) shall have Bheruṇḍā as its presiding deity.
Having written "parām" at the end of the fire-mantra (vahni), one should also write "vāsinyai namaḥ.
O Maheśānī, this eight-syllabled mantra has Vahnavāsinī as its deity.
[The next mantra consists of] the Praṇava, Bhuvaneśānī, and the syllable composed of "pha-re-m".
The Moon (S) with the Visarga (Ḥ) followed by *nityaklinne madadrave* and ending with the consort of Fire (Svāhā)—
this Vidyā bestows all sovereignty.
This fourteen-syllable Vidyā is likewise to be known as Vajreśvarī.
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Parā, one should add "Śivadūtī" with the case-ending "ṅe";
this mantra, O Goddess, ending with the heart (hṛdaya), is the Dūtī who bestows all prosperity.
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Oṃkāra, one should write "Parā" as the armor (kavaca).
Having written *khe-cā-cha-kṣam*, one should write the Śrī-bīja;
then the syllable *huṃ*, *kṣe*, *parā*, and the weapon-mantra (*astra*). This Vidyā is Tvaritā, who consists of all lion-thrones, and is like a young girl, the Beauty of the Kula.
One should likewise enclose Nityabhairavī with Bālā;
O Goddess of the gods, when the five arrows are [so arranged], Nityā becomes the Śakrākṣarī.
Or else:
This five-syllabled mantra, consisting of the seed-syllables of the arrows, is eternally the Aparā [form].
It consists of the Praṇava (Oṃ), Bhuvaneśvarī (Hrīṃ), and the syllable Pha-re-m;
the second part consists of the syllable Blūṃ, followed by Bhuvaneśī and the goad (Aṅkuśa).
Having extracted the word *nityā* and [the vocative] *madadrave*,
[one takes] the armor (*kavaca*), the goad (*aṅkuśa*), the *māyā* (hrīṃ), *nityā*, and *nīlapatākinī*.
Then [one takes] the final letter [of the alphabet] joined with *kāla* (the letter *ha*), and the letter *ra* endowed with the vowel of Indra (*e*).
O Goddess, this Vidyā marked with the *bindu* and the *nāda* becomes Vijayā.
Or else:
[the letter] at the end of *vā* (i.e., *pha*), conjoined with Kālāgni (the letter *ra*), Vāyu (the letter *ya*), and adorned with the vowel of Śakra (the letter *i*).
Joined with *nāda*, *bindu*, and *kalā*, this *vidyā* becomes *Vijayā*.
One should write the Moon (*candra*) conjoined with Varuṇa (*va*) and situated upon the *tāra* (the syllable *oṃ*).
Then, O Goddess, one should write *Sarvamaṅgalā* ending in the dative case (*-yai*).
O Goddess, this mantra ends with the heart [seed-syllable]; this Sarvamaṅgalā is eternal.
Having uttered twice "Tāraṃ hṛdbhagavati" (Oṃ Hrīṃ Bhagavati), one should then say "Jvālāmālinī devi" (O Goddess Jvālāmālinī) at the end of all, followed by "bhūtasaṃhārike" (O Destroyer of Beings).
Having inscribed the pair of words "jātavedasi" and "saṃlikhya," one should write the pair "jvalati" and "prajvalat," followed by three *huṃ* syllables.
This mantra is composed of the three fire-seeds (*vahnibīja*), the *kūrca* mantra, and is joined with *svāhā*.

This is the eternal Great Goddess Jvālāmālinikā, the supreme. She is adorned with the end of the *ka*-group, the end of the vowels, and the vowel of Indra (the nasal *ṃ*); she is the wondrous Supreme Sovereign, pervaded by the *bindu*, the *nāda*, and the *kalā*.
One should worship sequentially within all the vowels beginning with 'a';
O Supreme Goddess, one should worship the Śrīvidyā, the Mother of the Universe, in the vowel 'aḥ'.
O Lady with large lotus-like eyes, one should install the Vidyā according to the vowels.
One should place these [syllables] in the locations for the placement of the sixteen vowels. (7ka)
The mantra is as follows:
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ oṃ namaḥ kāmeśvari icchākāmaphalaprade sarvasattvavaśaṅkari sarvajagatkṣobhaṇakari huṃ.
huṃ huṃ drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ sauḥ klīṃ aiṃ, salutation to Kāmeśvarī-nityā-kalā (1).
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ aiṃ, O Bhaga, O Bhagā, O Bhaginī, O Bhagodari, O Bhagāṅgā!

O you who possess the vulva! O bringer of the vulva! O you whose secret place is the vulva! O vulva-source! O you who strike down the vulva! O you who bring all vulvas under control! O excellent semen! O excellent semen! O you who are moist with the vulva! O you who are a flowing liquid! Saturate! Cause to flow!

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ Hrīṃ Nityaklinne Madadrave Svāhā; salutation to the eternal digit Nityaklinnā (3).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Īṃ Oṃ Kroṃ Kroṃ Drauṃ Crauṃ Chrauṃ Jrauṃ Jhrauṃ Svāhā, salutation to Bheruṇḍānityākalā (4).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Uṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Vahnivāsinī; [this is] Vahnivāsinī.
Salutation to Nityākalā (5).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ūṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Phreṃ Saḥ, to the eternal, ever-moist, intoxicatingly flowing Vajreśvarī-Nityākalā, svāhā; salutation to her (6).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Śivadūtī; obeisance to the eternal digit of Dṛti.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṝṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Huṃ Khecha Chekṣa Strīṃ Hūṃ Kṣe Hrīṃ Phaṭ, obeisance to the eternal digit of Tvaritā. (8)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, salutation to Kulasundarī Nityākalā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḹṃ Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, Ha Sa Ka Ra Ḍaiṃ, Ha Sa Ka La Ra Ḍīṃ,
Ha Sa Ka La Ra Ḍauḥ, Drāṃ Drīṃ Klīṃ Blūṃ Saḥ Sauḥ Klīṃ Aiṃ.
Salutation to Vimalanityākalā.
Alternatively: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Drāṃ Drīṃ Klīṃ Blūṃ Saḥ, salutation to Vimalanityākalā (10).

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Eṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Phreṃ Blūṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Nitye Madadrave Huṃ Kroṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Nīlapatākinī, the digit of the eternal [Nityā] (11). Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Bhmrauṃ, obeisance to Vijayā, the digit of the eternal [Nityā].
Alternatively:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Bhmtryauṃ Vijaye, and so forth (12).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Svoṃ, obeisance to Sarvamaṅgalā.
Salutation to the eternal digit of all auspiciousness (13).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Auṃ Oṃ! Salutation, O Blessed One, O Goddess Jvālamālinī, O Goddess Jvālamālinī, O You who effect the destruction of all beings, O Jātavedas, you who are blazing, you who are blazing!
JVALA PRAJVALA PRAJVALA HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ RAṂ RAṂ RAṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ JVĀLĀMĀLINĪNITYĀKALĀYAI NAMAḤ (14).
AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ AṂ CAṂ KAUṂ VICITRĀNITYĀKALĀYAI NAMAḤ (15).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aḥ, having uttered the root mantra, [one says]: *namaḥ śrīmahātripurasundarīnityākalāyai* (16). Or else: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aḥ Oṃ, *namaḥ kāmeśvarīnityākalāyai*.
Thus one should perform the placement (nyāsa) of the sixteen Nityās.
At this time, the placement of emanation and maintenance (sṛṣṭisthitinyāsa) may also be performed.
This concludes the placement of the sixteen Nityās.
Now, the placement (nyāsa) of the manifest yoginīs:
at the *mūlādhāra*, *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ* [namaḥ] to the manifest yoginīs;
at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*, [3] *namaḥ* to the secret yoginīs.
At the navel: 3 obeisance to the most secret Yoginīs. At the heart: 3 obeisance to the Sampradāya Yoginīs.
At the throat: 3 obeisance to the Kulakaulinī Yoginīs.

At the center of the eyebrows (3): Homage to the Nigarva Yoginīs. In the resonance (nāda) (3): Homage to the Rahasya Yoginīs. At the end of the resonance (nādānta) (3): Homage to the Atirahasya Yoginīs.
At the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra): Oṃ 3, salutations to the Yoginīs of the supreme secret. || 8 ||
Now, the placement of the weapons (*āyudhanyāsa*):
*drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ śāṃ dhaṃ*, salutation to the bow of Kāmeśvara for the purpose of enchantment (*sammohana*).
*Yāṃ 5 drāṃ 5 thaṃ*, salutation to the bow of Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of enchantment;
these two [mantras] are on one's own lower left hand.
*Drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 jaṃ*, salutation to the arrows of Kāmeśvara for the sake of the Jambhalas.
Yāṃ 5 drāṃ 5 jaṃ: salutation to the Jambhalas and the arrows of Kāmeśvarī.
These two [mantras] are on the lower right hand.
Drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 āṃ: salutation to the noose of Kāmeśvara for the purpose of subjugation (vaśīkaraṇa).

*Drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 hrīṃ*, salutation to the noose of Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*); these two [mantras] are on the upper left hand. *Drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 kroṃ*, salutation to the goad of Kāmeśvara for the purpose of paralyzing all (*sarvastambhana*).
*Drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5*, salutation to the goad of Kāmeśvarī for the immobilization of all;
these two [syllables] are on the upper right.
Thus, having meditated upon Kāmakalā according to the sequence to be described, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*).
And so it is said in the Jñānārṇava:
"Having thus contemplated one's own body as consisting of the deity in the form of Kāmakalā, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the weapons of Śiva and Śivā."
And likewise: *drāṃ*, *drīṃ*, *klīṃ*, *blūṃ*, and *saḥ*—these are proclaimed as the arrows of Kāma;
*yāṃ*, *rāṃ*, *lāṃ*, *vāṃ*, and *śāṃ*—this is the pentad of arrows of Kāmeśvarī.
One should extract the letters beginning with *drā* followed by those beginning with *yā*, and from the word *saṃmohana*,
the dative singular form of *kāmeśvaradhanuḥ* ending in *ṅe* and ending in *namaḥ*. With this mantra, one should hold the bow in one's own left lower hand.
Above [the mantra] beginning with *yādidrādīni* and ending with *thaṃ ṅe*,
one should place the bow of Kāmeśvarī ending in *ṅe* and followed by *namaḥ* upon the hand below;
likewise, the practitioner should hold a sugarcane bow in the left hand of the Goddess.

The best of practitioners should install the Śiva-arrows made of flowers on his own lower right hand, beginning with *drā* and so forth for the Jambhalas near the word *kāmeśvara*, ending with *namaḥ* for the arrows.

The practitioner should place these syllables— *yā*, *dri*, *drā*, and so forth— followed by *jaṃ* for the Jambhalas, then from the word *Kāmeśvarī*, and then *bāṇebhyo namaḥ* (salutation to the arrows)— upon his own right lower hand;
thus the practitioner should assign the flowery arrows of the Goddess.

Furthermore, the syllables beginning with *drā* and ending with *yā*, accompanied by the nasal bindu (*m*), form the "mouth-circle" (*mukhavṛtta*). For the purpose of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), one should then place the word *kāmeśvara* followed by *pāśāya namaḥ* upon the upper left hand.
One should place [the seed-syllable] beginning with *yā* (yādidrādi), followed by *gagana* (ha), *vahni* (ra), the left eye (i),
and the bindu (m)— thus forming *yā~ hrīm*— for the purpose of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*). Then, saying "Kāmeśvarī" and "Pāśāya namaḥ," one should assign this to the hand on the upper left.
One should write *drā* and so forth, followed by *kroṃ*, then the phrase "for the immobilization of all" (*sarvastambhanāya*).
After the word *Kāmeśvara*, one should write "salutation to the goad" (*aṅkuśāya namaḥ*).
Then, one should place the Śaiva goad in the upper right hand.
One should write "Yādidrādīni kroṃ" for the purpose of paralyzing all [enemies], followed by the words "Kāmeśvarī" and above that, "Aṅkuśāya namaḥ.
Then, one should place the goad (aṅkuśa) in the upper right hand of the Goddess. 9ka.
Then, with the root mantra, one should perform the pervasive mudrā and display the nine mudrās.
Namely: Drāṃ, the All-Agitating; Drīṃ, the All-Enchanting; Klīṃ, the Attracting;
Blūṃ, the All-Penetrating; Saḥ, the All-Inebriating; Kroṃ, the Great Goad; Ha Sa.
Kha phreṃ, the Khecarī-mudrā; Hsauḥ, the Bīja-mudrā; Aiṃ, the Yoginī-mudrā. || 10 ||

Regarding the time for the ritual placement (nyāsa), it is stated in the *Yoginīhṛdaya*: "The application of these [mantras] is performed individually at the time of dawn, or during the time of worship, during the rite of fire-oblation (homa), or even at the time of recitation (japa)."
At the time of worship, the best of practitioners should perform either all [of these] together.
Then comes the meditation:
Then [one should meditate on] the Goddess, who resembles a lotus, blazing with the rays of the rising sun,
like the hibiscus flower, and comparable to the pomegranate blossom.
Resembling a ruby and appearing as red as saffron,
she was adorned with a shimmering crown-jewel and a network of tiny bells;
her sprout-like, curling locks were like a swarm of black bees.
The Supreme Goddess, whose lotus-like face has a mandala resembling the fresh glow of the rising sun;
whose soft forehead-band is slightly curved like the crescent moon;
and whose creeper-like eyebrows have the shape of Śiva’s bow.
Her eyes were swinging in the playful sport of bliss and joy;
she wore shimmering golden earrings resembling flickering rays of light;
and the full expanse of her beautiful cheeks surpassed the orb of the moon, which is filled with nectar.
Her nose was perfectly defined by the measuring lines of Viśvakarman’s craftsmanship;
her lips were red like copper, coral, or a bimba fruit, resembling nectar itself;
and she surpassed the ocean of the essence of sweetness with the sweetness of her smile.
She is adorned with a jaw-region endowed with incomparable qualities,
possesses a neck like a conch shell, and is the Great Goddess with arms as graceful as lotus stalks,
her lotus-like hands having the appearance of the petals of a red lotus.
The surface of the sky was overspread by the radiance of her red lotus-like nails;
she possessed lofty breasts adorned with strings of pearl necklaces,
and her waist was beautifully graced by the circle of the three folds.
Her navel was adorned like an eddy in the river of loveliness;
her hips were graced with a girdle fashioned from priceless gems;
and the line of hair upon her hips was like a supreme goad for the elephant of her rounded buttocks.
The sovereign lady, whose thighs were as delicate as the graceful pillars of a plantain tree;
whose knees were beautiful with the form of blossoming beauty;
and who was adorned with a pair of shanks resembling plantain stalks of loveliness.
Her pair of feet had hidden ankles, and her foreparts surpassed the tortoise;
they were adorned with slender, long toes and rows of clear nails,
while her lotus-feet were rubbed by the crest-jewels on the heads of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
She who smiles with a continuous stream of splendor resembling a hundred moons;
she whose form is like a ripe pomegranate, surpassing vermilion in its crimson hue;
she who is clothed in red garments and holds a noose and a goad raised in her hands.
Seated upon a red lotus, adorned with red ornaments,
four-armed and three-eyed, she holds five arrows and a bow;
her mouth is filled with betel leaf mixed with pieces of camphor.
Her body is crimson with the intense saffron of great musk;
she is richly arrayed in all the attire of amorous grace and adorned with every ornament;
she is the mother who generates joy for the world and the one who brings delight to the universe.
The Goddess who attracts the world, whose form is the cause of the universe,
who consists of all mantras, who is beautiful with every auspiciousness,
who is composed of all prosperity, the eternal Śivā who embodies all powers.
Having thus meditated upon the Self as having such a form, one should worship it with mental offerings.
For example:

having visualized the Goddess in the center of the heart-lotus, one should offer water for the feet (*pādya*) at the Goddess’s feet with the nectar from the thousand-petaled lotus situated in the vessel of *kuṇḍalī*.
Then, having offered the *arghya* to the mind,
one should offer water for rinsing the mouth (*ācamanīya*) with the supreme nectar flowing from a vessel shaped like a thousand-petaled lotus;
and one should offer fragrance by means of the twenty-four principles (*tattva*).
Non-violence, wisdom, patience, compassion, non-greed, non-delusion, lack of envy,
absence of deceit, absence of egoism, and freedom from passion and hatred— these ten are the [restraints of the] senses.
One should cause flowers to be offered.
Then one should present incense in the form of wind and a lamp in the form of fire.
Furthermore, [one should offer] clothing, a fly-whisk, the sun, a mirror, the moon, an umbrella, and a lotus.
One should offer a girdle, bliss, and a supreme necklace; a bell consisting of the sound of the unstruck (*anāhata*);
and then the ocean of the essence of nectar, a mountain of meat, and the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*).

Having offered the full vessel of milk-rice (pāyasa), one should gratify the Supreme Goddess with dances, songs, and instrumental music that arise from the erotic and other sentiments, accompanied by the rhythmic clapping of the hands of beings who are like dancers of the mind.
Having thus worshipped [the deity] non-differently, the recitation (japa) should be performed;
thereafter, one should begin the external worship, followed by the placement of the arghya vessel.
First is the general *arghya*; the procedure for that is as follows:
first, having fashioned a square with water on one's left, one should draw a circle within it.

Then, having worshipped that [mandala] with flowers, saying "Oṃ, obeisance to the mandala," one should place a vessel with its support there, worship it with the *bālā* [mantra], fill it with pure water, and [recite]: "Aiṃ, obeisance to the heart of the omniscient power, the illustrious Tripurasundarī."
Having worshipped the six limbs in this sequence and having recited the root mantra eight times over them, one should perform the installation of the special arghya offering. || 13ka ||
Regarding that vessel, another tantra states:
"The vessel may be made of gold, glass, or silver, or produced from pearl or skull; it may be made of viśvāmitra (amber), or this golden one which grants desires, or the beloved crystal one."

Copper bestows affection and produces the attainment of desired goals; that which arises from the auspicious coconut produces the perfection of manifest mantras; and the skull grants liberation, as does the pearl. (14)
In the *Navaratneśvara*:
"O Maheśānī, the vessel made of human bone should be known as the most excellent of the excellent;
the vessel produced from a coconut shell should be known as the next best in conception."

O lady of beautiful hips, the precious bowl (ratnapātra) should be known as either superior or middling; the bowl made of bael wood (bilva) or from the Brahma-tree (brahmavṛkṣa) is said to be of middling-superior quality, while the earthen one is declared to be of middling-inferior quality. (15)
For rites of subjugation and attraction, one should use a beautiful golden vessel;
for pacifying or nourishing rites, however, O Dear One, one should have it made of silver.
One should know that an iron vessel is used for killing and expulsion;
for acts of immobilization, a stone vessel; and for causing enmity, vessels made of iron or clay. (17)
O lady of virtuous vows, Viśvāmitra should be employed in all tasks;
however, in matters concerning the destruction of a lineage, a glass vessel is superior. (18)
One should know that for the rite of propitiating mantras, a vessel made of wood or leaves is appropriate;
however, a human skull vessel should be taken up, as it bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Goddess of the gods, upon seeing the vessel of honor (arghyapātra), Brahmā and the other deities,
as well as all the yoginīs, always dance with joy and bestow spiritual accomplishments (siddhi).
Navaratneśvara states the necessity of both the general and specific *arghya* offerings: "If one does not provide a single vessel [for the general *arghya*], even if Maheśvara is present in person,
the mantras turn away and calamities arise at every step."
In this world he shall be poor, and after death he shall go to the state of a beast.

Then, having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, a hexagon, and a square with the water of the general offering (sāmānyārghya) between oneself and the Śrīcakra, one should worship the center of the triangle with the root-vidyā, and worship [the corners] of the triangle with each of the individual kūṭas.
In the six-cornered [diagram], one should worship the six limbs by means of the root-mantra repeated twice, following the sequence of the corners beginning with the southeast (Agni).
Having placed the tripod there, [one should offer] "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Maṃ to the fire-mandala."
Having worshipped the support with the mantra "Obeisance to the support of the arghya vessel, whose self consists of the ten kalās," one should worship the ten kalās of fire there in a circular form.
It is as follows:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Yaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrā. Likewise: 3 Raṃ, to Nīlā;
3 Laṃ, to Kapilā.
3 Vaṃ to Visphuliṅginī; 3 Śaṃ to Jvālinī;
3 Yaṃ to Haimavatī.
3 Saṃ to Havyavāhinī; 3 Haṃ to Kavyavāhinī;
3 Laṃ to Rātri.

"3 KṢAṂ, obeisance to Saṅkarṣiṇī. Having thus worshipped, one should place the washed arghya vessel upon that [base], reciting the root mantra ending with the weapon-mantra (astra), and having written the mantra there as before.

Having worshipped [the vessel], and having worshipped it with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Aṃ, obeisance to the arghya-vessel which is the twelve-fold kalā-souled solar orb," one should worship the twelve kalās of the Sun in a circular form.
For example:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Bhaṃ, obeisance to Tapinī. Likewise: 3 Khaṃ Baṃ, obeisance to Tāpinī.
3 gaṃ phaṃ to Dhūmrā; 3 ghaṃ paṃ to Vibudhā;
3 ṅaṃ naṃ to Bodhinī.
3 CAṂ DHAṂ to Kalinī; 3 CHAṂ DAṂ to Śoṣiṇī;
3 JAṂ THAṂ to Vareṇyā.
3 Jhaṃ Taṃ to Ākarṣiṇī; 3 Ñaṃ Ṇaṃ to Māyā; 3 Ṭaṃ Ḍhaṃ to Vivasvatī.
3 Ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, [offering] to Hemaprabhā;
*namaḥ* everywhere.
Having thus worshipped, having filled [the vessel] with water and so forth using the root mantra, one should draw the yantra as before within the triangle.
One should contemplate three lines starting from the letter *a* in the center, as well as the letters *ha* and *la*.

Then, having worshipped as before, one should worship with the mantra: "sauḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ uṃ, obeisance to the nectar of the arghya vessel, which is the essence of the sixteen digits of the lunar orb (somamaṇḍala). [Then] of the Moon...
One should worship the sixteen digits (kalās) in a circular form as follows:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā.
Thus: 3 Āṃ to Madanā; 3 Iṃ to Tuṣṭi;
3 Īṃ to Puṣṭi.
3 uṃ to Prīti; 3 ūṃ to Rati; 3 ṛṃ to Śrī.
Ṛṃ to Kriyā; 3 Ḷṃ to Sudhā; 3 Ḹṃ to Rātri.
Eṃ, to Jyotsnā;
3 Aiṃ, to Haimavatī; 3 Oṃ, to Chāyā.
3 Oṃ to Pūrṇimā;
Aṃ to Vidyā;
3 Aḥ to Amāvasyā.
"Salutation everywhere.
Having thus worshipped and invoked the *tīrtha*, [one offers] "Salutation to the *haṃsātman* in the center.
Then: *ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ vaṣaṭ* to Ānandabhairava.
Having worshipped with "Ha Sa Kṣa Ma La Va Ra Yīṃ, vaṣaṭ to Sudhādevī," and having offered the fish-oblation while covering that water, having recited the root-mantra eight times,
having presented incense and lamps, and having displayed the nine mudrās, [one should contemplate] that which consists of Brahman.

Having poured a little of that water into another vessel, one should sprinkle oneself and the ritual materials with the root mantra, thereby making everything consist of Brahman. Until the completion of the worship, one should not move the *arghya* water.
Regarding the timing: the worship of the limb-deities of the goddess Sundarī occurs after the placement of the *arghya* vessel.
And so it is said:
Having sprinkled water upon himself and the sacrificial materials in due order,
the best of mantra-knowers should always contemplate that [reality] as consisting of consciousness with devotion;
from that, by the sequence of the four directions of the wheel, he should emanate the auspicious wheel and the sun.
Having meditated upon Hastimukha, Para-Smarahara, Gopāla, and likewise [the others],
and having invoked them, one should then dismiss them into one's own heart with various flowers, water for the feet (pādya), and other diverse substances, fragrant sweets, and fruits.

Then, on the great wheel (*mahācakra*): *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namo 'mṛtāmbhonidhaye*. Likewise: three times for the Jewel Island (*ratnadvīpa*); three times for the Great Garden of Various Trees (*nānāvṛkṣamahodyāna*).
3 to Santānavāṭikā; 3 to Kalpavṛkṣavāṭikā; 3 to Haricandanavāṭikā.
To the Mandāra grove, three; to the Pārijāta grove, three; to the Kadamba forest grove, three.
To the one with a wall of puṣparāga jewels; to the one with a wall of padmarāga jewels; to the one with a wall of gomedaka jewels.
To the sapphire jewel wall, three times; to the diamond jewel wall, three times; to the lapis lazuli jewel wall, three times.
To the one with a wall of pearl-jewels; to the one with a wall of coral-jewels; to the one with a wall of ruby-jewels.
To the Maṇikya-maṇḍapa, three; to the Sahasra-stambha-maṇḍapa, three; to the Amṛta-vāpikā, three.
3 to Ānandavāpikā; 3 to Vimarṣavāpikā; 3 to Bālātapoddhārā.
To Candrikodarā; to Mahāśṛṅgāraparikhā; to Mahāpadmāṭavī.
3. To the King of Houses made of wish-fulfilling gems;
3. To the eastern gate of the Eastern Tradition (Pūrvāmnāya); 3. To the southern gate of the Southern Tradition (Dakṣiṇāmnāya).
3. To the western door of the Western Tradition (paścimāmnāya). 3. To the northern door of the Northern Tradition (uttarāmnāya). 3. To the circle of the Jewel Island (ratnadvīpavalaya).
3. To the great lion throne; 3. To the single bedstead leg consisting of Brahmā; 3. To the single bedstead leg consisting of Viṣṇu.
To the single leg of the bed consisting of Rudra: 3. To the single leg of the bed consisting of Īśvara: 3. To the single plank of the bed consisting of Sadāśiva: 3.
3. To him whose body is like a swan; 3. To him whose great pillow is like a swan; 3. To him whose spread is of saffron-dyed cloth.
To Mahāvitānikā, three times; to Mahāyamanikā, three times. In all cases, one should perform worship with the word "namas" at the end.
Above that: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauḥ, obeisance to the great corpse-throne of Sadāśiva (Sadāśivamahāpretapadmāsana). || 22ka ||

Then, having meditated as before and having formed the *trikhaṇḍā* mudrā, one should bring [the deity] down onto the *mātṛkāyantra* at the peak above that, and invoke her into the conceived form within the *bindu*, saying: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauḥ! I conceive the form of Tripurasundarī."
Having uttered *hsraiṃ hasaklrīṃ hasrauṃ*, [one says]: *Oṃ, O Supreme Goddess, who dwells within the great lotus forest, whose form is the bliss of the causal source,
O Mother who acts for the welfare of all beings, come, come!*

Thus, having invoked the familiarization within the Vaindava-cakra and performed the rites beginning with the invocation and ending with the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*), one should display the mudrās such as the arrow, the bow, the noose, and the goad.
Then, having worshipped with the various offerings (*upacāra*) as appropriate, one should satisfy [the deity] three times. || 23 ||
In this regard, the procedure is as follows:

with water held in the Śrīpātra by the tip of the nail of the ring finger and thumb of the left hand, while flowers and unbroken rice grains are offered by the other hand, one should say: "I satiate Śrī Mahātripurasundarī."
One should satisfy the three [deities].
As it is stated in the *Svatantra*:
"O Pārvatī, by joining the thumb and the ring finger of the left hand..."
One should satisfy the beautiful goddess along with the oceans and their vehicles.
One should offer libations three times into the mouth of the goddess using the root mantra (mūlavidyā),
employing the union of the thumb and ring finger, lifted up by the nails as prescribed.
One should offer a drop of water from the *śrīpātra* to satisfy the Mistress of the Kula (*kulanāyikā*).
O Goddess, the thumb is Bhairava and the ring finger is Caṇḍikā, O Beloved;
with the right hand joined together, one should thus satisfy the Mistress of the Kula (*kuleśvarī*). (24)
The specific distinction is as follows:
one should offer libations with the thumb and ring finger for the rite of subjugation (vaśya),
and one should offer libations with the thumb and middle finger for the rite of pacification (śāntika).
O Dear One, one should perform the libation for malevolent rites by joining the index finger with the thumb;
for the rite of immobilization, one should perform the libation by joining the little finger with the thumb.

Then one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the intermediate directions— namely Agni, Īśāna, Asura, and Vāyu— and in the cardinal directions, either within the body of the Goddess or [elsewhere].
It is as follows:
Aiṃ, to the Heart of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the power of all-knowingness, salutation!
Klīṃ, to the Head of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the power of eternal contentment, Svāhā!
Sauḥ, to the Crest of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the power of primordial awakening, Vaṣaṭ!
Aiṃ, to the armor of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the independent power, Huṃ!
Klīṃ, to the three eyes of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the power of non-decline, Vauṣaṭ!
Sauḥ, to the weapon of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the infinite power, Phaṭ!
Then one should contemplate the Kāmakalā within one's own body.
And thus it is said:
"Having visualized the Bindu as the face, and below that, the two breasts."
One should contemplate that [triangle] below as being together with the *parārdha* and facing downwards.
Then, one should worship the *tithinityā*.
In the great triangle, by moving counter-clockwise, one worships the five beginning with *a* and the five beginning with *u*.
Having meditated upon the five [syllables] beginning with *ekāra*, one should worship the *visarga* in their center; rotating counter-clockwise,
one should worship from Kāmeśvarī to Vicitrā during the bright fortnight (*śuklapakṣa*), and from Jñānadakṣiṇāmūrti to Kāmeśvarī during the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapakṣa*).
Namely:
on the first lunar day (pratipad), having uttered the respective mantra—*akāre aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—one says:
"I worship the *śrīpāduka* of Kāmeśvarī Nityakalā; *namaḥ*."
In the form *evaṃ*, she is Bhagamālinī in the second [cakra];
in *i*, she is Nityaklinnā in the third;
and in *ī*, she is Bheruṇḍā in the fourth.
In the syllable *u*, on the fifth [day], is Vahnivāsinī;
in the syllable *ū*, on the sixth, is Mahāvidveśvarī;
in the syllable *ṛ*, on the seventh, is Śivadūtī.
In the letter *ṛ*, on the eighth day, [one worships] Tvaritā; in the letter *ḷ*, on the ninth day, Kulasundarī;
in the letter *ḹ*, on the tenth day, Nityā.
In the syllable *e*, on the eleventh day, [one worships] Nīlapatākā;
in the syllable *ai*, on the twelfth day, Vijayā;
in the syllable *o*, on the thirteenth day, Sarvamaṅgalā.
One should worship Jvālāmālinī with the syllable *auṃ* on the fourteenth day;
Vicitrā with the syllable *aṃ* on the full moon day;
and Tripurasundarī with the *visarga*.
In the dark fortnight, one should worship [the goddesses] beginning with Vicitrā and ending with Kāmeśvarī.

The mantra for worship is stated in another tantra: Having first uttered the word "Śrī," one should then utter the word "pādukā"; thereafter, one should say "I worship" (pūjayāmi) and "namas. In this manner, one should worship the deities of the limbs (aṅgadevatās).
Then, one should worship the lineage of Gurus in the middle of the triangle located in the center of the eastern [triangle].
O Parameśvarī, they are to be known as ending with the word "Ānandanātha.
O Goddess praised by heroes, the Gurus are said to be feminine in gender and ending with the suffix "-anvī."
Namely:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Paraprakāśānandanātha; obeisance!
Thus, three times: Paraśiva. Likewise: I worship the Śrīpādukā of Paraśaktyambā; obeisance. Thus, three times: Kauleśvara and Śuklādevī.
3. Pareśāna. 3. Kāmeśvaryambikā. These are the divine groups (divyaudha).
Bhoga, Krīḍa, Samaya, Veda, and Sahaja— these are the multitudes of Siddhas.
Gaganam, Viśvam, Vimalam, Madanam, Bhuvanam, Nīlam, Ātmānam, and Priyam— these are the multitudes of Mānavas.
Then [one worships] the Guru, the Paramaguru, the Parāparaguru, the Parameṣṭhiguru, or the Kevalaguru.
These are the gurus of the Kāmarāja-vidyā and of that which is composed of it.
Paraśiva, Ambā Kāmeśvarī, the Divine Current (divyaugha), the Great Current (mahaugha), Sarvānanda, Prajñādevī, and Prakāśa—
these are the Divine Currents (divyaughas) of Lopāmudrā, who is composed of them.
Divya, Citra, Kaivalya, Divyāmbā, and Mahodaya— these are the streams of the Siddhas.
They manifest the consciousness of the universal power, the blissful joy of the supreme lotus of the Lord, and the enchanting bliss of happiness.
"These are the multitudes of Mānavas"—
thus one should worship.
Then, as before, one should worship the three gurus or one.
Alternatively, one may worship the general lineage of gurus as follows: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ* homage to the gurus (*gurubhyo namaḥ*).
3. Homage to the sandals of the Guru. 3. Homage to the Supreme Gurus. 3. Homage to the sandals of the Supreme Gurus.
3. Salutation to the higher and lower gurus.
3. Salutation to the sandals of the higher and lower gurus. 3. Salutation to the supreme gurus.
3. Homage to the sandals of the supreme preceptor (parameṣṭhiguru). 3. Homage to the teachers (ācāryas).
3. Homage to the sandals of the teachers (ācāryapādukās).
In all cases, at the beginning, one should employ either two or three Āryās.
And so it is said in the Jñānārṇava:
"Indeed, according to the previous sequence, there is a pair of seed-syllables consisting of Māyā and Lakṣmī."
"O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, one should employ the triad as it has been taught.
Also, in the *Kalpasūtra*:
"In all cases, at the beginning, there is the employment of the *tritārī*."
And the *tritārī*:
Vāṅ, Māyā, and Kamalā—this is declared to be the *tritārī*. (26a)
Then, in the Sṛṣṭicakra beginning with Trailokyamohana: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hasrīṃ Shrīṃ Śrīṃ Kalahrīṃ, I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Unmanī of the Pūrvāmnāya; obeisance!
In the Wheel of Stability (sthiticakra): 3 Aiṃ Klinne Klīṃ Madadrave Kūle Hsauḥ. I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Bhoginī of the Southern Tradition (dakṣiṇāmnāya); obeisance!
Then, in the three wheels consisting of the nature of withdrawal (saṃhāra), beginning with Sarvasaubhāgyā: 3 Ha Sa Kha Phreṃ Hsauḥ.

Bhagavati amba ha sa kha phreṃ kubjike hsrāṃ hsrīṃ hsraṃ aghore ghore ghoramukhi cavrāṃ cavrīṃ cabrūṃ kili kili [in reverse order]— I worship the *śrīpādukā* of the goddess Kubjikā of the Western Tradition (*paścimāmnāya*), together with the five previously mentioned seed-syllables (*bīja*).
Homage!
To all the wheels (cakras) three times: *Ha Sa Kha Phreṃ*, O Great Caṇḍa-Yogeśvarī, Goddess Kālikā of the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya), I worship the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*).
In the *vaindava-cakra*: *hasaiṃ hasakalarīṃ hsauḥ*. [Worship] the Goddess Śrīpādukā, who bestows all *siddhis*, belonging to the *ūrdhvāmnāya*.
Then, one should worship the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) in the southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, and the center, as well as in the cardinal directions.
And so it is said in the Jñānārṇava:
"Then one should perform the selection of the limbs (aṅga) arising from the Śrīvidyā mantra;
the worship of the limbs is performed in the directions—namely, the southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, and the center."
Then, one should worship the eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇimā*, at the four gates starting from the west in the outer square. || 26ka ||
Regarding the rule for the directions starting with the west, it is stated in the *Guptārṇava*:
"When the practitioner of mantra worships Tripurā while facing a certain direction,
then the east is behind the Goddess and the west is in front of Tripurā."
And in the Viśuddheśvara [tantra]:
"If one should worship the wheel while facing north, then the Goddess is in the northern quarter;
the eastern quarter itself is [the front], without a doubt."
The south is declared to be behind the Goddess, and likewise the north is to her right;
that which is her left shall be the south—this is remembered as the rule everywhere.
O Queen of the Gods, the northeast is then the southeast; of this there is no doubt. (27)

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I worship] the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Aṇimā. Likewise, three times: [I worship] the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Laghimā; three times: [I worship] the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Mahimā.

3. [Worship] the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Sovereignty (Īśitvasiddhi). In the four corners starting from the northwest (Vāyavya), [worship] 3. the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Subjugation (Vaśitvasiddhi). 3. the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Irresistible Will (Prākāmyasiddhi).
3. Homage to the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Will (icchāsiddhi).
3. Homage to the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Enjoyment (bhuktisiddhi). Below: 3. Homage to the venerable feet of the Siddhi of Attainment (prāptisiddhi).
Above: 3 Sarvajñānasiddhi-śrīpāda-pūjita (I worship the venerable feet of Sarvajñānasiddhi).
At the four doors of the central square, beginning from the west: 3 Tāṃ Brahmāṇī-śrīpāda-pūjita (I worship the venerable feet of Brahmāṇī).
Thus: 3 īṃ Māheśvarī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | 3 ūṃ Kaumārī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | 3 ṝṃ Vaiṣṇavī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi |
In the four corners beginning with the northwest: 3 ḶṂ Vārāhī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | 3 AIṂ Indrāṇī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | 3 AUṂ Cāmuṇḍā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi |
3 Aḥ Mahālakṣmī-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi.
Within the inner square, at the four doors starting from the west: 3 Drāṃ Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī Mudrā-Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. 28. Likewise, 3 Drīṃ.
OṂ HRĪṂ SARVAVIDRĀVAṆĪMUDRĀŚRĪPĀDUKAṂ PŪJAYĀMI | 3 KLĪṂ SARVĀKARṢIṆĪMUDRĀŚRĪPĀDUKAṂ PŪJAYĀMI | 3 BLŪ SARVAVAŚAṄKARĪMUDRĀŚRĪPĀDUKAṂ PŪJAYĀMI |
In the four corners beginning with the northwest (vāyavya): 3 SAḤ [to] the venerable feet of Sarvonmādinīmudrā, I offer worship.
3 KROṂ [to] the venerable feet of Mahāṅkuśāmudrā, I offer worship. 3 HA SA KHA PHREṂ [to] the venerable feet of Khecarīmudrā, I offer worship.
Above: 3 hsauḥ, worship of the venerable Sabījamudrā (the mudrā with seed-syllables). Below: 3 aiṃ, worship of the venerable Yonimudrā (the womb-mudrā).
Above: 3 auṃ, worship of the venerable Trikhaṇḍāmudrā (the three-sectioned mudrā).
At the tip of the wheel, on the complete wheel: *Oṃ* three times, *namaḥ* to the Trailokyamohana-caturaśra-cakra.
*Oṃ* three times, *aṃ āṃ sauḥ*, *pūjā* to Tripurā-śrīpādukā.
To her right: *Oṃ* three times, *drāṃ*, *pūjā* to Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī-mudrā-śrīpādukā.
To the left of the Goddess: 3 AḤ, obeisance to the venerable Siddhis beginning with Aṇimā; 3, obeisance to the Cārvāka philosophy.
Here, in this four-cornered wheel (cakra) that fascinates the three worlds, presided over by the Mistress of the Wheel (Cakranāyikā) Tripurā, these [are worshipped].
"May Aṇimā and the other Prakaṭa-yoginīs, together with their mudrās, siddhis, weapons, vehicles, and retinues, being worshipped with all ritual offerings, be satisfied.
With these words, he should offer the arghya water to the Root Goddess. || 28ka ||
Then, having displayed the *drāmiti* mudrā which agitates all, [one recites]: *aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā | klīṃ vidyātattvāya svāhā*.
"Sauḥ, svāhā to the Śiva-tattva. Thus, one should offer libations three times with the arghya water. || 29 ||
Then, on the sixteen petals, beginning from the western petal and proceeding counter-clockwise:
3 AṂ Kāmākarṣiṇī Nityākalā Śrīpādukāṃ Pūjayāmi. 3 ĀṂ Buddhyākarṣiṇī Nityākalā Śrīpādukāṃ Pūjayāmi.
Thus, in all cases, the phrase "I worship the *nityakalā* Śrīpādukā" is to be employed.
And so it is said in the *Navaratneśvara*: "One should again worship these *nityakalās* in reverse order."
3 (Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ) Ahaṅkārākarṣiṇī; 3 Īṃ Śabdākarṣiṇī;
3 Uṃ Sparśākarṣiṇī.
3 Ūṃ Rūpākarṣiṇī | Ṛṃ Rasākarṣiṇī | 3 Ṝṃ Gandhākarṣiṇī |
3 ḷṃ Cittākarṣiṇī; 3 ḹṃ Dhairyākarṣiṇī;
3 eṃ Smṛtyākarṣiṇī.
3 Aiṃ, the Attractor of Names;
3 Oṃ, the Attractor of Seeds;
3 Auṃ, the Attractor of the Self.
3 Aṃ, the Attractor of Nectar;
3 Aḥ, the Attractor of the Body.
At the tip of the wheel: 3, to the sixteen-petaled wheel that fulfills all desires.

3 Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of Tripureśvarī, the Mistress of the Cakra; [this applies] everywhere at the end [of each name], [with the formula] "I worship the Śrīpādukā," preceded by Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. To her right: 3 Drīṃ, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of the Sarvavidrāviṇīmudrā.
On the left: 3 *Laghimāsiddhi-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Homage to the Buddhist philosophy (*Vauddhadarśana*).
Here, within the sixteen-petaled wheel that fulfills all desires, is Tripureśvarī.

These secret yoginīs, beginning with Kāmākarṣiṇī, who are presided over by the Mistress of the Wheel (Cakranāyikā) and are accompanied by their respective mudrās, one should offer to the Root Goddess. Having displayed the Sarvavidrāviṇī mudrā with the syllable *drīṃ*, one should say: *aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā*.
As before. || 30 ||
In the eight-petaled wheel (*aṣṭadala-cakra*), in the four petals starting from the east and proceeding counter-clockwise:
3 KAṂ 5, [worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgakusumā; 3 CAṂ 5, [worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgamekhalā.
3 Ṭaṃ 5, [I worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgamadanā; 3 Taṃ 5, [I worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgamadanāturā.
In the petals starting from the southeast (Agni), 3 Paṃ 5, [I worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgarekhā.

3 yaṃ 4, worship of the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgaveginī; 3 śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ, worship of the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgāṅkuśā; 3 laṃ kṣaṃ, worship of the venerable feet of the goddess Anaṅgamālinī.
At the tip of the wheel: *Oṃ* three times, *namaḥ* to the eight-petaled wheel that agitates all.
*Oṃ* three times, *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance and worship to the venerable feet of Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Wheel.
To her right: *Oṃ* three times, *klīṃ*, obeisance and worship to the venerable feet of the Sarvākarṣiṇī Mudrā.
On the left [petal], 3: *Mahimāsiddhiśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Homage to Jitendradarśana.
Here, in the eight-petaled wheel that agitates all (*sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇāṣṭadalacakra*).

"Obeisance to these most secret Yoginīs, beginning with Anaṅgakusumā, who are presided over by the Sovereign of the Wheel of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, together with their Śaktis," and so forth— one should offer this to the Root Goddess. Then, saying "klīm," one should display the Sarvākarṣiṇī Mudrā.
Aiṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva), and so forth, as before. || 31 ||
Beginning from the tip of the fourteen-spoked wheel and proceeding counter-clockwise from the west to the south, [one worships]: 3. *Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī* Śakti, Śrīpādukā, I worship;
3. *Sarvavidrāviṇī*.
3. The Attractor of All; 3. The Delighter of All; 3. The Enchanter of All.
3. Sarvastambhinī (the paralyzer of all); 3. Sarvajṛmbhaṇī (the one who causes all to yawn); 3. Sarvasattvavaśaṅkarī (the one who brings all beings under control).
3. Sarvarañjanī (The All-Enchanting One) | 3. Sarvonmādinī (The All-Intoxicating One) | 3. Sarvārthasādhinī (The Accomplisher of All Aims).
3. She who fulfills all prosperity; 3. She who consists of all mantras;
3. She who brings about the destruction of all suffering.

In all instances, the phrase "śaktiśrīpādukā" is to be employed. At the front of the wheel: *Oṃ* three times; *namaḥ* to the fourteen-spoked wheel that bestows all prosperity (*sarvasaubhāgyadāyakacaturdaśāracakra*).
*Haiṃ Ha Klīṃ Hsauḥ*, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Tripuravāsinī, the mistress of the wheel (*cakranāyikāśrīpādukā*), [and offer] libation (*pūjaya*).
To her right: 3 blūṃ, worship of the venerable feet of the Mudrā who brings all under control (Sarvavaśaṅkarī).
To her left: 3, worship of the venerable feet of the Siddhis such as sovereignty (Īśitva) and so forth.
Salutation to Sāṃkhya, Mīmāṃsā, and Nyāya philosophy.
Here, in this fourteen-spoked wheel that bestows all auspiciousness,

presided over by the Mistress of the Wheel, Tripuravāsinī— one should offer these powers, beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, who are the Yoginīs of the tradition along with their seals (mudrās), and so forth, to the Root Goddess.
Having displayed the *sarvavaśaṅkarī* mudrā with "blūṃ," [one recites] "aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā" and so forth, as before. || 32 ||
Beginning from the tip of the outer ten-spoked wheel and proceeding counter-clockwise from west to south:
[I] worship the Śrīpādukā of the Goddess who bestows all siddhis.
Thus, in all cases: *devīśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.
3. Bestower of all prosperity (*sarvasampatpradā*). 3. Maker of all dear (*sarvapriyaṅkarī*).
3. She who brings about all auspiciousness; 3. She who bestows all desires;
3. She who liberates from all suffering.
3. She who pacifies all death;
3. She who wards off all obstacles;
3. She who is beautiful in every limb.
3. Bestower of all auspiciousness.
Salutation to the outer ten-spoked wheel (*vahirdaśāracakra*) at the tip of the wheel, which accomplishes all aims (*sarvārthasādhaka*).
3. *Hasaiṃ Ha Sa Klīṃ Hsauḥ*. [Worship] the feet of the venerable Mistress of the *Tripurāśrīcakra* (*tripurāśrīcakranāyikāśrīpāda*). Pū.
To her right: 3 saḥ, worship of the venerable feet of Sarvonmādinīmudrā.
To her left: 3, worship of the venerable feet of the supernatural powers such as Vaśitva and so forth.
Salutation to Brāhmī, the science of medicine, and philosophy. || 33 ||
Then, in the outer ten-spoked wheel of the Sarvārthasādhaka,
presided over by Tripurā, the Mistress of the Śrīcakra— these goddesses who bestow all accomplishments,
the Kula-kaulinī Yoginīs together with their mudrās, and so forth— one should offer to the Root Goddess.
Then, having displayed the Sarvonmādinī mudrā, he offers [the oblation] as before with the mantra: "Aiṃ, svāhā to the Ātmatattva. || 33ka ||
Starting from the western spoke of the inner wheel (antardaśāracakra) and proceeding as far as the southern spoke, [one should worship] with: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvajñādevīśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.
In this same manner, everywhere [one should worship] with *devīśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.
3. She who consists of all powers;
3. She who bestows all sovereignty;
3. She who consists of all knowledge.
3. She who destroys all diseases; 3. She whose nature is the support of all; 3. She who removes all sins.
3 She who consists of all bliss; she whose very nature is all-protection; 3 she who bestows the fruits of all desires.
At the tip of the wheel: *Oṃ* three times, *namaḥ* to the inner ten-spoked wheel that effects all protection.
*Hrīṃ klīṃ blūṃ*, worship at the feet of the venerable Tripuramālinī, the mistress of the wheel.
To her right: *Oṃ* three times, *kroṃ*, worship at the feet of the venerable Mahāṅkuśa Mudrā.
On the left: 3 3 *Prākāmyasiddhi-Śrīpāda*, worshiped!
3 *Namaḥ* to Sauradarśana!
Here, in the *Sarvarakṣākara-antardaśāra-cakra*.

One should offer to the Root Goddess [the mantra] beginning with "These goddesses, Samrajñī and the others, who are the Nigarbha Yoginīs presided over by Tripuramālinī, the Mistress of the Cakra, together with their Śaktis," and so forth.
Then, displaying the Mahāṅkuśa Mudrā with *Kroṃ*, one says: *Aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā*.
As before. || 34 ||
Then, beginning from the tip of the eight-spoked wheel and proceeding from the west to the south:
3 AṂ 16 VAŚINĪVĀGDEVATĀŚRĪPĀDA PŪJITA. Likewise: 3 VĀGDEVATĀŚRĪPĀDA PŪJITA.
Thus for all [the letters]: 3 kaṃ 5 ka la hrīṃ Kāmeśvarī;
3 caṃ 5 na va līṃ Modinī;
3 ṭaṃ 5 ylūṃ Vimalā.
3 taṃ 5 ja ma rīṃ Aruṇā; 3 paṃ 5 ha sa la va yūṃ Jayinī;
3 yaṃ 4 jha ma ra yūṃ Sarveśvarī.
3 ŚAṂ ŚAṂ SAṂ HAṂ LAṂ KṢAMARĪ KAULINĪVĀGDEVATĀŚRĪPĀDAU PŪJAYĀMI | Obeisance to the eight-spoked wheel at the front of the cakra, which removes all diseases.
HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ SAUḤ TRIPURĀSIDDHĀNITYĀŚRĪPĀDAU PŪJAYĀMI |

To the right of this [seat]: 3 HA SA KHA PHREṂ, obeisance to the venerable feet of Khecarīmudrā (Khecarīmudrā-śrīpāda), [I] worship. To the left: obeisance to the venerable feet of Bhuktisiddha (Bhuktisiddha-śrīpāda), [I] worship. Obeisance to the Vaiṣṇava doctrine.

Here, in this eight-spoked wheel that removes all diseases and is presided over by Tripurāsiddhācakranāyikā, one should offer [the oblation] to the Root Goddess, saying: "These Yoginīs, beginning with Vaśinī, together with their attendants," and so forth.
Then, having displayed the Khecarīmudrā with "3 Ha Sa Kha Phreṃ," one says: "Aiṃ! Svāhā to the Ātmatattva."
As before. || 35 ||
Outside the triangle, starting from the front and proceeding counter-clockwise from west to south:
3 *drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ śāṃ*, obeisance to the arrows of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī that cause paralysis.
3 drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 dhaṃ thaṃ, obeisance to the bow of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of completely enchanting all. 3 drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 āṃ hrīṃ,
obeisance to the noose of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of subjugation.
3 drāṃ 5 yāṃ 5 kroṃ, obeisance to the goad of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī for the purpose of paralyzing all.
Then, having uttered the root *vāgbhava* mantra at the front, right, and left corners of the triangle, [one should worship] in the fire-chakra (*agnicakra*).
In the abode of Kāmagiri, which is of the nature of Mitreśanātha,
[I worship] the venerable feet of the goddess Kāmeśvarī, whose essence is Rudra-Śakti. Having uttered the Kāmarāja-mantra, [I worship] at the Sūryacakra in the Jālandhara-pīṭha.

Having uttered the Śakti-kūṭa, [one worships] the venerable feet of the goddess Vajreśvarī, whose nature is that of Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha and who is of the essence of Viṣṇu; [this is] at the seat of Pūrṇagiri in the Moon-chakra (somacakra). Having uttered the Śakti-kūṭa, [one worships] the venerable feet of the goddess Bhagamālinī, whose nature is that of Uḍḍīśanātha and who is of the essence of Brahmā; [this is] at the seat of Pūrṇagiri in the Moon-chakra.
At the tip of the wheel (3): *Namaḥ* to the first wheel, the bestower of all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradādyacakra*).
*Hsraiṃ Hsklrīṃ Hsrauḥ*, [I worship] the venerable feet of the eternal Mother Tripurāmbā (*tripurāmbānityāśrīpāda*). I worship.
To her right: 3 hsauḥ, worship of the venerable Bījamudrā (Bījamudrā-śrīpāda). To her left: 3, worship of the venerable Icchāsiddhi (Icchāsiddhi-śrīpāda).
3, obeisance to Śaktidarśana.
Here, in this first wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradā*), whose interior is adorned with arrows, bows, nooses, and goads,
and which is presided over by Tripurāmbā, the mistress of the wheel— these [goddesses] beginning with Kāmeśvarī,
who are the most secret yoginīs together with their retinues— one should offer [the oblation] to the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*).
Having displayed the seed-syllable and mudrā *hsauḥ*, [he offers] as before: *aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā*.
Then, having uttered the root mantra (*mūla*) in the *vaidvava* cakra, [he offers]: *śrīmahātripurasundarīnityāśrīpā pū0*.

Having thus worshipped three times, one should say at the tip of the wheel: "Obeisance to the Wheel of the Bindu consisting of All-Bliss (*sarvānandamayavaindavacakra*). Reciting the root mantra (*mūla*), one should worship: "Obeisance to the feet of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Wheel (*śrīmahātripurasundarīcakranāyikāśrīpāda*). To her right: "Obeisance to the feet of the venerable Yonimudrā (*aiṃ yonimudrāśrīpāda*)."
On the left: 3. *Prāptisiddhi-śrīpāda*, worshiped; 3. *Mokṣasiddhi-śrīpāda*, worshiped; 3. Salutation to Śaiva-darśana.
As it is stated in the Kuloḍḍīśa:
"Then, having recited the root mantra, one should worship Mahātripurasundarī,
who is the form of the deity, as the Mistress of the Wheel (Cakreśvarī) within the Bindu."
Or, as stated in the *Navaratneśvara*:
"The Buddhist, the Brāhma, the Saura, the Śaiva, and the Vaiṣṇava, and the Śākta should be known as the sixth; this is the wheel consisting of the six philosophical systems. (37)

In the Rudrayāmala it is also said: "The square is the Buddhist division; the sixteen-petalled lotus is the Brahma and Vaiṣṇava divisions; and the fourteen-sided figure is called the Śaiva and Saura divisions."
The eight-spoked and the twenty-spoked [circles] are declared to be the central Śākta [center]. In the locations thus described, the respective deity of that vision is to be worshipped.
Here, within the Bindu-cakra consisting of universal bliss, she whose nature is the Supreme Brahman resides.
[The mantra] presided over by the Mistress of the entire Cakra, who is the consciousness-form of Mahātripurasundarī, the Mistress of the higher and lower powers,
[and who possesses the qualities of] the Enchanter of the Three Worlds, the Fulfilled of All Desires, and the Agitator of All.
Bestower of all good fortune, accomplisher of all aims, creator of all protection, remover of all diseases, granter of all perfections, (consisting of all bliss),
the tradition of all the manifest, secret, and most secret [teachings] revealed by the Śrīcakra.

The venerable Tripurā— Tripureśī, Tripurasundarī, Tripuravāsinī, Tripurā, Śrītripuramālinī, and Tripurasiddhā— who is surrounded by the entire circle of Yoginīs, and who is the Kulakaulinī, the Nigarbha, the Secret, the Ultra-secret, and the Supreme-Non-Supreme Secret.
The Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī Nityā, the Mother of Tripura, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the leaders of all the *tattva*-cakras; the Sovereign of all cakras, the Sovereign of all mantras,
the Sovereign of all vidyās, the Sovereign of all pīṭhas, the Sovereign of all desires, and the Sovereign of all principles (*tattvas*).
The Sovereign Lady of all Heroes, the Enchantress of the Three Worlds, the Mother of the Origin of the Universe, who consists of all wheels—
together with the Mistress of those wheels, along with their retinues, powers, accomplishments, weapons, vehicles, and attendants, [I worship] Śrī Mahātripurasundarī with all ritual offerings.
"May they be worshipped and gratified with supreme and inferior service.
Thus, one should offer the special *arghya* water, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and flowers into the left hand of the principal goddess.
Then, having displayed the nine mudrās, one should perform the libation as before three times with the arghya water, reciting "aiṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā" and so forth. || 37ka ||

Then, having offered perfumes, flowers, *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), garlands, and so forth, and having uttered "Aiṃ" while ringing the bell, one should recite the root mantra: "Oṃ! The divine essence of the forest tree, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent."
"May this incense, which is to be smelled by all the gods, be accepted.
Thus one should offer the incense.
Then, having recited the root mantra: "Oṃ, the great lamp is well-illuminated, dispelling darkness on all sides."
"May this lamp, a light both internal and external, be accepted.
Thus one should offer the lamp.
Then, having recited the root mantra, one should say: "I offer the food offering (naivedya) to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī."
"Namaḥ. With these words, one should present the food offering (naivedya). Thereafter, one should perform the daily fire sacrifice (nityahoma).

It is as follows: having sprinkled [water] on the ground and recited the root mantra, [one offers]: *oṃ prāṇāya svāhā*, *oṃ apānāya svāhā*, *oṃ samānāya svāhā*, *oṃ udānāya svāhā*, *oṃ vyānāya svāhā*.
One should also offer six oblations with the six-limbed [mantra].
And thus it is said:
"Having sprinkled [water] around, one should then perform the daily fire-oblation (nityahoma) upon the ground."
O Goddess of Gods, one should offer five oblations in succession with the root mantra.
One should understand that the nature of these five oblations is the vital breaths: prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna.

Six oblations in the six limbs are declared to be this daily fire-sacrifice (*nityahoma*). Then, having drawn a triangle, a circle, and a square on one's left, and having worshipped it with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ,
obeisance to the all-pervading mandala," [one should offer] water filled with half-boiled rice.
One should place a vessel there;
reciting the mantra of the *kalā-varṇa* three times, one should then offer the *bali*:
"Oṃ hrīṃ, to all obstructors and to all spirits, hūṃ svāhā."

Having offered [the oblation] with the general *arghya* water, one should display the *tattva-mudrā*. Then, one should offer the *bali* to Vaṭuka and the others. Having drawn triangular and circular maṇḍalas in the northeast, northwest, southwest, and southeast corners, [one should place them] within those.
Vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka; yāṃ, obeisance to the Yoginīs;
gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati.
"KṢĀṂ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla.
Having thus worshipped with water for the feet and other offerings, and having placed vessels filled with ritual substances upon them, one should present the bali offering.
As it has been said:
"The mantra is declared to consist of the names of Vāmā and the others ending in the dative case (ṅe), followed by 'namaḥ'.
Having worshipped them with water for the feet and other offerings, one should present the bali offering with this [mantra]."
Likewise elsewhere as well:
"Come, come, O Devaputra Vaṭukanātha, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, with a flaming mouth! Destroy all obstacles; accept this bali-offering along with all ritual services."
One should offer the *bali* to Vaṭuka with the mantra "gṛhṇa svāhā" and display the *mudrā* by joining the left thumb and ring finger.

[The offering is made] upwards to the limit of the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*), or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the partless realm, or in the netherworld (*pātāla*).
Whether on the ground or in the air, in wind or water, or wherever they may abide—

in sacred fields (*kṣetra*), seats (*pīṭha*), and secondary seats (*upapīṭha*)— may those goddesses, who are worshipped by the lords of heroes (*vīrendra*), being pleased by incense, lamps, and the like, as well as by the ritual of auspicious offerings (*śubhabali*), always protect us.
One should offer the bali with the mantra: "YĀṂ YOGINĪBHYAḤ SVĀHĀ, SARVAYOGINĪBHYAḤ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ," using the thumb,
index finger, middle finger, and ring finger of the left hand in the shape of a yoni.

One should display the mudrās. With the mantra "KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ KṢAIṂ KṢAUṂ, O Kṣetrapāla dwelling in this field, accept, accept the bali-offering together with incense and other articles, svāhā," one should offer the bali to the Kṣetrapāla.
One should draw [the object] away.
Having straightened the index finger with the left thumb, one should display the mudrā.
*Gāṃ gīṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya*.
One should offer the oblation (bali) to Gaṇapati with the mantra "baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā.
One should display the mudrā by placing the middle finger against the thumb like a staff.
This same set of four offerings should also be performed for the Bhairavī-vidyā.
Or, at the very end, one should offer the bali-oblation to all beings.
Regarding the bali in the Tantra, it is said:
"He who worships Caṇḍikā without having first offered [the bali] to Vaṭuka and the others..."
His worship becomes fruitless and the Goddess's curse arises.
Therefore, having offered water for rinsing the mouth and other items to the Root Goddess, one should give fragrant betel-leaf;
thereafter, one should present the *ārātrika* lamp.
For example:
having drawn a wheel with saffron and other pigments upon a vessel made of bell-metal or similar material for a young girl,
one should place eight lamps filled with ghee and provided with wicks containing camphor within its eight "birth-paths" (yonis).
Having placed it in the center and established a great lamp upon the head fashioned from flour and other materials,
and having worshipped it with the mantra *śrīṃ hrīṃ glūṃ slūṃ mlūṃ plūṃ llūṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, one should lift that vessel up to the level of the head nine times.
