Followed by swans whose flight drew them far away by the sound of their tinkling anklets— as if they were personified messengers bearing commands—
and resembling two lotuses with upturned faces upon well-formed stalks, [the two] proceeded with the splendor of Śrīkaṇṭha’s consort.
He fashioned your two feet. || 16 ||

O Bhavānī, even though your two beautiful shanks are being gazed upon by the bull-bannered Lord Śiva— who, as if unsatiated in his desire to behold them, has plucked out his forehead eye and looks with eyes trembling with intense passion— [they remain untouched].
I bow down to you. || 17 ||
I remember your thighs, which surpassed the pride of an elephant’s trunk in their girth and suppleness, and which,
as if they were two pillars provided by the silk of your garment to support the weight of your hips.
By means of the middle one. || 18 ||
May your waist, its essence fully awakened by the age beyond childhood when the hips, thighs, and breasts shall expand simultaneously,
manifest before my heart— its form made evident by the play of the line of hair.
In the center. || 19 ||

O Goddess, your navel— which is filled with the waters of tears from the fear of the fire of Śiva’s eye— has never been entered by a sprout, as if it were offered by your fresh youth, O friend of Smara.
I might forget it. || 20 ||
Even the Lord [Śiva], though bearing ashes that proclaim his domestic life,
was reminded by those two breasts of the elephant— now risen from its bath, marked for a moment with foam and reddened with vermilion— as they resembled the mud and the *kāśmarī* fruit.
The two jars of Samada. || 21 ||
O Mother, those two arms of my enemy— beautiful with streams of radiant luster flowing from necks that surpass [the throat],
and which were indeed desired as long nooses for the embrace of the throat by the fish-bannered god (Kāma)— do not come within the path of my memory.
The two should leap across. || 22 ||

O Daughter of the Mountain King, contemplating your neck— neither too long, stealing the grace of fashioned conch shells, resplendent with various ornaments, and possessing enchanting qualities— I find no satiety.
Never at any time am I [that]. || 23 ||

O Mother, he who repeatedly remembers your face— with its long, wide eyes, a well-born forehead, the lines of his cheeks slightly blooming with a gentle smile, lips like the bimba fruit, and a high, long nose— is truly blessed.
Thus he was born. || 24 ||

O Goddess, for him who contemplates with his mind your mass of hair— which possesses the brilliance of the moon’s crescent and is indistinguishable from a swarm of bees hovering over abundant fragrant flowers— the ancient bond falls away of its own accord. (25)
That mortal here who, with a perpetually tender inner self, recites this hymn of the wise— which has been cooked with the skillful preparation of the Vedas—
attains a high station and prosperity.
For a long time, [he was the one] characterized by the glory of the crowns of kings bowing at his feet. || 26 ||
Thus ends the hymn to Bhuvaneśvarī.
Now follows the armor (kavaca) of Bhuvaneśvarī.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
O Lord of Gods, whatever vidyās have been revealed by Bhuvaneśvarī—all of them have been heard and mastered; now I desire to hear them once again.
O Mahādeva, please relate that supreme, pleasing armor named Trailokyamaṅgala which was previously mentioned. Īśvara said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall speak; attend with careful attention.
This armor, named Trailokyamaṅgala, is the very embodiment of mantra.
O Goddess, consisting of perfected vidyās and endowed with all sovereign powers,
by reciting and retaining it, a mortal shall become a possessor of sovereignty over the three worlds.

Śiva is the seer (ṛṣi) of this armor (kavaca), which is the auspiciousness of the three worlds; Virāṭ is the meter (chandas); the goddess Bhuvaneśvarī, the sustainer of the universe, is the deity (devatā);
and its application (viniyoga) is proclaimed to be for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. || 5 ||
May the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* protect my head; may Bhuvaneśī protect my forehead. May *aiṃ* protect my right eye, and may *hrīṃ* protect my left eye.
Śrīṃ—may Maheśvarī, ending with the three syllables, protect my right ear;
Aiṃ—may she always protect my left ear; may she protect my nose at all times. (2)
Hrīṃ, O Goddess, protect my face; Aiṃ, protect my tongue.
May she who is the enclosure of speech, consisting of three syllables and whose essence is supreme, protect my throat.
Śrīṃ may she protect my shoulders eternally; Hrīṃ may she protect my arms at all times; Klīṃ may Tripuṭeśānī, the bestower of sovereignty over the three cities, protect my hands. 4.
Āṃ protects the heart; Hrīṃ always protects my middle region;
Krauṃ protects my navel region—this is the three-syllabled Bhuvaneśvarī.
May Sarvabījā always protect my back; may Sarvavaśaṃkarī protect [me];
may Hrīṃ protect my private parts, and Namobhagavati protect my waist.
May Māheśvarī always protect the two thighs and the pair of knees;
may Annapūrṇā always protect [the navel], and Svāhā protect the two feet.
May this seventeen-syllable mantra protect the entire body of Annapūrṇā;
it consists of the syllables *tāra*, *māyā*, *ramā*, and *kāma*, followed by sixteen syllables.
May the Supreme Goddess, consisting of twenty syllables, residing in the head, protect me always;
she is the ten-syllabled mantra: *Tāraṃ durge yugaṃ rakṣaṇī svāhā*.
May Jayadurgā, dark as a rain cloud, protect me from all sides with joy;
she is preceded by the seed-syllable of Māyā and consists of ten syllables, and beyond her is another.
May Jayadurgā, who has the luster of refined gold, protect [me] in fire;
she is the supreme mantra consisting of eight syllables: *Tāraṃ* (Oṃ), *hrīṃ*, *duṃ*, *durgāyai*, and *namaḥ*.
Bearing the conch, discus, bow, and arrow, may she protect me on the right;
O crusher of Mahiṣa, Svāhā, the supreme one whose essence is gold and wealth! 12.
May she who destroyed the demon Mahiṣāsura protect [us] always in the southwest;
Māyā Padmāvatī Svāhā—this is proclaimed as the seven-syllabled mantra. || 13 ||
Padmāvatī, seated upon a lotus, may she always protect me in the west; O Supreme Goddess, with the noose and goad as your hands, come here, svāhā! || 14 ||
May she who consists of thirteen syllables, beginning with *Tārā* and mounted upon a horse, protect me in the fire:
*Sarasvati*, *Pañcasvare*, *Nityaklinne*, *Madadrave*. (15)
May the eight-syllabled *vasu* mantra, accompanied by *svāhā*, always protect me from above;
may the *tāra*, *māyā*, and *kavaca* mantras constantly protect the bride in the sky.
HŪṂ KṢEṂ HRĪṂ PHAṬ—may this Great Vidyā of twelve syllables, which bestows everything, protect me always in the northeast corner along with the eight serpents of Tvaritā. (17)
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ—may Bālā protect me constantly from the region of the head; may Bhairavī-Bālā, ending with the Bindu (Oṃ), protect me always on the ground. 18.
Thus has been told to you this meritorious [account], the supreme auspiciousness of the three worlds,
more essential than the essence itself, a merit that is the embodiment of the flood of great vidyās.
By the mere recitation of this, even Kubera becomes the lord of wealth instantly;
and by its retention and recitation, all the gods, beginning with Indra,
having become masters of all supernatural powers (siddhis), shall attain every sovereignty.
Having offered eight handfuls of flowers, one should recite [the mantra] once with the root mantra alone. || 20 ||
One shall obtain the fruit of worship performed for a year;
having established mutual affection, Kamalā remains steadfast in the home.
And the Goddess of Speech shall dwell in the mouth of that virtuous soul who bears this work named *Trailokyamaṅgala*; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. (22)
Having recited this supreme and meritorious armor (kavaca), even he who is the best among the virtuous shall become endowed with all sovereignty and a conqueror of the three worlds. || 23 ||
A man [should apply it] on the right arm and likewise a woman on the left arm;
she shall become possessed of many sons, and even a barren woman obtains a son. (24)
Weapons such as the Brahmāstra and others do not cut that person at all—[the one] who, without knowing this armor, worships the Mistress of the World (Bhuvaneśvarī). (25)
Having fallen into extreme poverty, he would soon meet his death.
Thus ends the *Bhuvaneśvarī-kavaca*, named *Trailokyamaṅgala*, from the *Śrī Rudrayāmala*, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord.
Now begins the *Annapūrṇā-stotra*.
Oṃ, salutations! O Goddess who bestows auspiciousness, salutations to you, the beloved of Śaṅkara!
Salutations to you, O Goddess who loves devotion; salutations be to you, O Annapūrṇā! || 1 ||
Salutations to you who have assumed a form through illusion; salutations to you, the beloved of Śaṅkara!
O Māheśvarī, salutations to you; O Annapūrṇā, let there be salutations to you. (2)
O Annapūrṇā, beloved wife of Havyavāha (Agni), O Hara-priyā; O you whose nature consists of the divisions of time such as Kalās and Kāṣṭhās, O Annapūrṇā, salutations be unto you! || 3 ||
O Great Goddess, who possesses the luster of a thousand rising suns, adorned with three eyes, and borne by the moon; O Annapūrṇā, salutations be unto you! || 4 ||
O Goddess dwelling in manifold garments, O sinless one who delights in the giving of food, O Annapūrṇā who brings joy through the dance of Śiva, salutations be unto you! || 5 ||
O Annapūrṇā, who dwells in the center of the six-petaled lotus, who consists of the six limbs of yoga, who is the very embodiment of Brahmāṇī and the other goddesses— salutations be to you!
O Goddess, bestower of universal sovereignty upon the seat of the crescent moon;
O Goddess Annapūrṇā, who brings joy to all—salutations be unto you! (7)
O Goddess who grants the desires of practitioners, O destroyer of the suffering of worldly existence, O Goddess bowed down by the weight of your breasts, O Annapūrṇā, salutations be unto you! || 8 ||
O Goddess whose lotus feet are worshipped by Indra and others, who assumes forms such as Rudra and bestows all prosperity— O Annapūrṇā, salutations be unto you!
Whoever recites this hymn with a concentrated mind at the time of worship, in his home prosperity becomes firmly established; of this there is no doubt. || 10 ||
Whoever recites this at dawn, preceded by the chanting of mantras,
shall possess an abundance of food that increases day by day.
It must never be given to anyone whatsoever, nor should it ever be disclosed.
Through disclosure, there is a loss of spiritual accomplishment; therefore, the wise person should guard it with great effort. (12)
Thus ends the *Annapūrṇā-stotra*. Now begins the *Annapūrṇā-kavaca*.
The Goddess said:
Whatever extremely rare vidyās were spoken by Annapūrṇā, all of them have been told out of compassion; they have been heard and mastered by me. (1)
Now I wish to hear that armor which was previously mentioned,
known as the "Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds," an armor that is the very embodiment of mantra.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall speak; attend with focused attention [to the armor named Trailokyamaṅgala, which bears the name of Brahmā].
The true nature of this Brahma-vidyā bestows great sovereignty;
by reciting and retaining it, a mortal becomes a possessor of sovereignty over the three worlds. || 3 ||
For this armor (*kavaca*) that protects the three worlds, Śiva is the seer (*ṛṣi*); the *virāṭ* meter is the meter; the goddess Annapūrṇā, the bestower of all accomplishments, is the deity;
and its application (*viniyoga*) is proclaimed to be for the sake of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation. || 4 ||
Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One, followed by the word "Māheśvarī. || 5 ||
Then "annapūrṇe tataḥ svāhā"—this seventeen-syllable mantra is Annapūrṇā, who is renowned throughout the three worlds; may she protect me. (6)
This seventeen-syllable mantra, beginning with the *praṇava* and preceded by *vimāyā*, protects [the practitioner] in all limbs;
it is filled with food and bestows jeweled jars and vessels of food.
May she who begins with the seed-syllable *Śrī* protect [the head]; likewise, she whose face consists of two nasal sounds (*m*) and the letter *R*;
may she who begins with the *Praṇava* (*Oṃ*) protect the eyebrows, and she preceded by the seed-syllable of speech (*Vāgbīja*, *Aiṃ*) protect the throat.
This [mantra] begins with the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma) and Maheśvarī is its heart;
it consists of Tāra (Oṃ), Śrīṃ, Hrīṃ, followed by the word "Namonta" and then the word "Bhagavatī."
May Māheśvarī, with the mantra "anna-pūrṇe svāhā," protect my feet;
may Māheśvarī, whose seed-syllable is the letter *m*, always protect my navel.
Tāra, Māyā, Ramā, and Kāma—these sixteen syllables, followed by the supreme [mantra] consisting of twenty syllables situated at the head, may she protect me always. 11.
May Ramā, Kāma, and Dhruva always protect my hands and feet;
and may she who consists of twenty syllables always protect my penis.
May the great vidyā Annapūrṇā protect [me]; may Hrīṃ protect the world; may Śrīṃ on the head, as well as Hrīṃ and Klīṃ, and Tripuṭā protect my anus. (13)
May the six limbs purified by the seed-syllable possessing the six long vowels sanctify me.
May Indra protect me in the east, and may Agni protect me in the southeast.
May Yama protect me in the south, and likewise Nirṛti in the southwest;
may Varuṇa protect me in the west, and may Pavana protect me in the northwest. || 15 ||
May Kubera protect me in the north, and may Śaṅkara protect me in the northeast;
may Brahmā and Ananta constantly protect me above and below, respectively.
"May the weapons, beginning with the vajra, protect [us] in the ten directions in due order.
Thus has been told to you this supreme, meritorious [teaching] for the protection of the three worlds. (17)
By holding and reciting which, the gods attained all sovereignty;
for by its retention and recitation, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra [attained their status]. (18)
In each and every kalpa, he separately creates and protects [the universe];
one should offer eight handfuls of flowers to the Goddess with the root mantra itself. || 19 ||
By reciting this armor-mantra (kavaca) and performing worship, one shall obtain the fruit thereof;
eloquence shall dwell in his mouth—this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. (20)
The preliminary rite (puraścaryā) for this mantra is prescribed as one hundred and eight recitations.
If one writes [the mantra] on birch bark, places it within a pill, and wears it encased in gold; || 21 ||
Whether on the neck or the right arm, he too is the best among the meritorious;
for when weapons such as the Brahmāstra reach his body, O Pārvatī,
they indeed become like garlands of flowers that grant happiness.
Thus ends the Armor of Annapūrṇā, from the Bhairava Tantra, in the dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī.
Now follows the Hymn to Tripuṭā:

One should meditate upon the Guru in the center of the lotus of the head— two-armed, holding a boon-granting gesture and a protection-gesture, serene, auspicious, and exceedingly gracious, seated with his own Śakti, possessing a radiant countenance, and whose very nature is light.
I meditate. || 1 ||
O Triśakti, those who recite your primordial seed-syllable— which is the Baka bird situated in fire, attended by the three forms, joined with the moon,
and possessing a golden luster— attain prosperity and good fortune.
Those men. || 2 ||

Then, having joined the sky, the wind, the friend, and the left eye [forming *nami*], and having visualized your own seed-syllable, which is the orb of the moon, the single face adored by the hosts of gods,
as your own glory (*śrī*);
They attain [it]. || 3 ||
Having meditated upon Viriñci situated on the earth, then the left eye, the Moon joined with the sound (Na), and the seed-syllable resembling the sun (Ra)—
by merely contemplating these, they delude the three worlds and through recitation attain lordship.
The lords of men. || 4 ||
Those who, having focused their minds on the beloved of the Enemy of Smara (Śiva), recite [the mantra] three times at the three junctions of the day while meditating upon Your body—
for them no enemy employs harsh speech; they become like Smara in the houses of women, and prosperity attends them.
Of them. || 5 ||
In his mouth resides Sarasvatī through compositions of prose and verse; indeed, the fierce gods do not harm him, but bow down to him.
His pair of feet is an ornament upon the heads of kings, and the supernatural powers (siddhis) rest in his hand.
They abandon those things that are difficult to grasp. || 6 ||
In a forest of *pārijāta* trees, upon the earth of golden luster, within a palace arrayed with jewels,
one should visualize an eight-petaled lotus on a radiant jewel lion-throne atop an altar.
Having reflected thoroughly. || 7 ||
Within the throbbing pericarp is a supreme pair of wombs; within them is she who possesses the luster of molten gold,
adorned with shimmering earrings, moon-faced, three-eyed, and possessing a neck marked by prominent folds like a conch shell.
She who causes the world to wander by means of her beautiful breasts.
With multitudes of arms radiant with great jewel-vajras, [he holds] a pair of excellent lotuses, a noose, and a bow;
a golden goad and flower-arrows.
Wearing ornaments of great jewels, she was slender-waisted and possessed beautiful hips.
Her lotus feet are shimmering with anklets, and she is adorned with a crown and other ornaments; she is gracious,
holding white yak-tail fans, a mirror, its case, and a casket filled with fine camphor.
By those who are upheld. || 10 ||
The creator of the three worlds, the remover of the world's afflictions, the agitator of the universe,
and the sustainer of the world; ever full of bliss, consisting of half the letter *ha*, and having the nature of the three dots (*bindu*).
I worship the one who possesses the three powers. || 11 ||

Having reflected for a long time upon her true nature, one should devoutly invoke Pūrṇā into the center of the yantra and worship her with self-arisen flowers and other offerings; thus, one shall attain the accomplishment of the four aims of human life.
Even a commoner. || 12 ||

Having likewise uttered the mantra into its own source, the king should worship Śrī and Śrīpati, Pārvatī and Īśvara, as well as Rati and Kāmadeva, together with their six limbs, and then worship Bhavānī in due order.
He would be so. || 13 ||
Having visualized the two treasures on both sides and worshipped them, one should then worship the queens and the world-protectors;
having worshipped their respective weapons at the tips of the petals, one attains the eight siddhis of Bhava.
Even a human being may obtain it. || 14 ||

You are the Earth, the ordainer and creator of the universe; you are also the Waters, Viṣṇu, and the protectress of the world. You are Fire, Rudra, and the agitator of the universe; you are endowed with sovereign power.
She is the wind-form of the world. || 15 ||

O Śivā, beloved of Śambhu, you are the primordial one; O refuge of the world, you eternally wander within the Brahma-aperture together with your consort. You are the sole merit accessible even without support; O Bhavānī, you are like the infinite sky.
Be gracious! 16.
Having cast everything into the midst of the ocean of existence, you render even the pride of the sages utterly diminished;
therefore, O Bhavānī, whose form is consciousness-bliss and whose nature is light, I do not know that [pride]— be gracious!
Even a person of dull intellect, by reciting with devotion a single hundred thousand times, attains poetic skill;
O Bhavānī, be gracious, for by contemplating Your own form within the three worlds, one obtains that which is difficult to attain. 18.
You are the foundational power (ādhāra-śakti), you are the form of that which is supported; you pervade the universe, and you are the form pervaded by the universe.
You alone are non-existence, whose nature transcends the qualities (guṇas); you alone are existence, O Bhavānī—be gracious!
You are the atom, you are the all-pervading, and you alone are the universe; what praise of yours could shine forth in this world?
Nevertheless, your qualities impel me to offer such praise to you, O Bhavānī.
Be gracious! || 20 ||
O Bhavānī, those men who recite this extremely secret hymn at the three junctions of the day, having chanted it within their lineage,
shall find nothing unattainable among the people of the three worlds; they shall attain your own true form.
Be gracious! || 21 ||
Thus ends the Tripuṭā Stotra. Now begins the Tripuṭā Kavaca.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
O Blessed One, knower of all dharmas, who has reached the further shore of the meaning of all scriptures,
whose form embodies the three powers, and who is the very essence of Lakṣmī— O Lord, please tell me that armor which has been revealed, known as the "Accomplisher of All Aims."
Īśvara said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the most wonderful armor (*kavaca*),
known as "The Accomplisher of All Aims," which is exceedingly rare throughout the three worlds.
O Goddess, it consists of all accomplishments and bestows all sovereignty;
by reciting and retaining it, a mortal shall become a partaker of the sovereignty of the three worlds.
Śiva is the seer (ṛṣi) of this armor-mantra which accomplishes all aims; the Virāṭ meter and the triple power (triśakti) are its meters; and the goddess Śrī, the sustainer of the world, is its deity.
Its application is proclaimed to be for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
May the Śrī-bīja protect my head; may she in the form of Lakṣmī protect my forehead. May Hrīṃ protect my right eye, and Sureśvarī my left eye.
May Klīm protect my right side, and likewise may Kāmeśvarī protect my left;
may Lakṣmī always protect my nose, and Keśava my face.
May Gaurī protect the tongue; may Maheśvara protect the throat;
may Rati protect the region of the shoulders; and may Makaradhvaja protect the two arms. || 7 ||
May Śaṅkhanidhi protect my hands, and likewise Padmanidhi my chest;
may Brāhmī always protect my belly, and may Maheśvarī protect my navel.
May Kaumārī protect my back, and may Vaiṣṇavī protect my private parts;
may Vārāhī protect my two thighs, and may Aindrī protect my two feet.
May Cāmuṇḍā protect his wife, and may Lakṣmī protect his sons.
May Indra always protect him in the east, and the deity Agni in the southeast.
May Yama always protect [her] in the south, and likewise Nirṛti in the southwest;
may Varuṇa protect [her] in the west, and the deity Vāyu in the northwest. (11)
May Soma always protect in the north, and may Īśvara protect in the northeast;
may Prajāpati protect above, and the deity Ananta protect below.
At the king’s gate, in the cremation ground, in the forest, and likewise in the wilderness; in water, on land, and in the sky, as well as amidst a multitude of enemies—
the Great Goddess Maheśvarī, whose essence consists of the three seed-syllables, is accompanied by these [mantras].
And may Triśakti, who is Mahālakṣmī, protect me always everywhere. || 14 ||
Thus, O Goddess, I have told you this most excellent essence of essences, the supreme armor named Sarvārthasādhana (the Accomplisher of All Aims), which is most wonderful. 15.
By reciting this, even Kubera, the lord of wealth, [attains his status] instantly;
and by retaining or reciting it, all the gods, beginning with Indra,
become masters of every accomplishment and shall obtain all sovereign powers.
One should offer eight handfuls of flowers while reciting the root mantra just once;
one shall thereby obtain the fruit of worship performed throughout an entire year.
Having established mutual affection, Lakṣmī remains steadfast in the home, and Vāṇī dwells within the mouth; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. (18)
The meritorious soul who wears this supreme and holy armor, known as the "Accomplisher of All Aims," shall become the best among the virtuous;
endowed with all sovereignty, he shall be a conqueror of the three worlds. || 19 ||
A man [should apply it] on the right arm and likewise a woman on the left arm;
having become possessed of many sons, even a barren woman obtains a son. (20)
Weapons such as the Brahmāstra and others do not cut through that body.
O Supreme Goddess, he who recites this [mantra] without knowing this armor shall encounter extreme poverty and soon meet his death. || 2 ||
Thus ends the armor (*kavaca*) named "The Accomplishment of All Aims" belonging to Triśakti in the Rudrayāmala.
Now follows the hymn of one hundred names (*śatanāmastotra*) of Durgā.
Īśvara said:
O lotus-faced one, I shall proclaim the hundred names; listen!
By the mere grace of this [recitation], the virtuous Durgā shall become pleased. (1)
Oṃ! Be true, be virtuous, be pleased, O Bhavānī, O liberator from worldly existence!
You are Āryā, Durgā, Jayā, the Primordial One, the three-eyed, and the wielder of the trident. || 2 ||
The bearer of the Pināka bow, the variegated one, she who possesses the moon-bell, the one of great austerity;
she who is mind, intellect, ego, and the form of consciousness; she who is the accumulated and the act of accumulating;
she who consists of all mantras, the true one, whose nature is the bliss of truth.
It is infinite, becoming, that which is to be realized, the capable, the incapable, and the eternal course. || 4 ||
She is the consort of Śambhu and the mother of the gods; she is ever intent on meditation and fond of jewels;
she is all-knowledge, the daughter of Dakṣa, and the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
Aparṇā, Ekavarṇā, Pāṭalā, and Pāṭalāvatī;
clad in silken garments, she is resplendent with tinkling anklets.
Immeasurably valiant, fierce, beautiful, and the beauty of the lineage;
she is Vanadurgā and Mataṅgī, worshipped by the sage Mataṅga. || 7 ||
Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Aindrī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, as well as Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, and Lakṣmī in human form. || 8 ||
Vimalā, Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, Satyā, Vākpradā, Bahulā, Bahulapremā, and Sarvavāhanavāhanā. (9)
She is the slayer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura,
the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and the annihilator of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
She is the destroyer of all asuras and the slayer of all dānavas;
she is the knowledge consisting of all scriptures and likewise the wielder of all weapons.
With many weapons in her hands and bearing various missiles,
she is a maiden, a single girl, a youth, a young woman, and an ascetic.
She is both immature and mature, the aged mother who bestows strength;
she is the Great Goddess with disheveled hair, of terrible form, and of great fruit.
She is a flame of fire with a fierce countenance, the Night of Doom, and an ascetic woman.
Nārāyaṇī, Bhadrakālī, Viṣṇumāyā, and Jalodarī. || 15 ||
Śivadūtī, Karālī, Anantā, Parameśvarī, Kātyāyanī, and Sāvitrī—the manifest expounder of Brahman. (16)
O Goddess Pārvatī, for one who constantly recites these one hundred and eight names of Durgā, there is nothing that remains unattainable within the three worlds. (17)
Wealth, grain, sons, a wife, a pair [of garments], and likewise an elephant, as well as the fourfold army—at the end, one shall obtain these and eternal liberation. (18)
Having worshipped the maiden and meditated upon the Goddess, the sovereign of the gods,
one should worship her with supreme devotion while reciting the Eightfold Hundred Names.
O Goddess, her success shall be achieved even by all the foremost of the gods;
kings shall become her servants, and she shall attain the glory of sovereignty. (20)

Having inscribed the yantra according to the prescribed rite using gorocanā, lac, and saffron— or with vermilion, camphor, and the three sweets— the knower of the ritual who always wears it becomes Śiva himself.
On the night of the new moon of the month of Bhādrapada, when the moon has entered the constellation Śatabhiṣaj,
one who writes and recites this hymn shall become a bestower of prosperity.
Thus ends the hymn of the names of Durgā in the Viśvasāra Tantra. Now follows the Śrī Durgā-kavaca.
The Lord said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim this armor (kavaca) which bestows all accomplishments;
by reciting and wearing it, a person is liberated from distress.
O Goddess, he who recites the Durgā-mantra without knowing the armor (kavaca) does not obtain its fruit; moreover, he shall go to hell. || 2 ||
O Goddess, this most secret armor (kavaca) is being told to you; it must be guarded with great effort—listen with full attention.
May the goddess Umā protect my head; may the wielder of the trident protect my forehead;
may Khecarī protect my eyes; and may Catvaravāsinī protect my ears.
May Sugandhā protect the nose; may Sarvasādhinī protect the face;
may Caṇḍikā protect the tongue, and likewise may Saubhadrikā protect the neck. || 5 ||
May Aśokavāsinī protect the mind; may Vajradhāriṇī protect the two arms;
may Mahāvāṇī protect the throat; and may Jaganmātā protect the two breasts. (6)
The heart is the goddess Lalitā, the belly is Siṃhavāhinī;
the hips are the goddess Bhagavatī, and the two thighs are Vindhyavāsinī.

O Goddess, you who possess great strength, with your two calves and feet resting upon the surface of the earth—you who exist thus, O Goddess whose very nature is the protection of the three worlds—protect me in all my limbs; O Durgā, Goddess, homage be to you! (8)
O Goddess, this armor-mantra bestows the fruit of great knowledge;
whoever recites it upon rising in the morning shall obtain the fruit of all sacred fords.
For one who places this armor upon the body, no obstacle shall arise anywhere;
he shall have no fear from spirits, ghosts, or demons.
In battle or in the royal court, he shall be victorious everywhere;
he receives honor everywhere on earth, like the son of a goddess. || 11 ||
Thus ends the Durgākavaca in the Kubjikā Tantra.
Now, the hymn to Mahiṣamardinī.
Bhairava said:
O Caṇḍī, who has crushed the fierce Asuras of wicked conduct, move within my heart; tear asunder [my enemies] at will!

May this swan of my mind, having reached the infinite ocean of the forest of the glorious lotus feet of the Peerless One, rejoice for a long time, free from the calamities of the core of the waves of intense, difficult-to-overcome malice. || 1 ||

O fierce one, having abandoned Nṛsiṃha— who has claws as expansive as the interior of the lovely Mount Sumeru, with fingers on his forepaws that are exceedingly powerful and capable of rending gold— the gods [sought refuge elsewhere].

O Mother, those who serve Your glorious feet—which are skilled at crushing the fetters of bound souls—are served by the enemies of elephants (lions); for what fear can there be from other foes for those who serve You? || 2 ||

O Caṇḍī, if even a single word or phrase concerning you should enter the range of one's hearing, that very reality, which follows the nature of the Supreme Spirit (Puruṣa), is sung of by Brahmā and the other gods.
Therefore, O Goddess, [I bow] to the glorious lotus-feet— shining as the sole abode of the essence of nectar for all deities— of you who...
Honor me today by being intent upon a yojana-long kiss. || 3 ||

Whether there be censure from men or not, whether it be better than the conduct of one's family path or not, let there be no fame for worshipping Keśava, Kauśika, or the Goddess; nor let me be near them.
O Mother, [let there be] only the place of service to Brahmā, Hara, Hari, Smara, the Enemy of Hutasana (Śiva), and the Enemy of Daityas (Viṣṇu).
May our mind always be intent upon the practice of meditating on the lotus feet of the Illustrious One. || 4 ||
If I am instructed in the sequential contemplation of His feet, then for me who has been so instructed, what rare or established ground could there be?
Therefore, O Goddess, [I seek] Your two lotus-feet, most abundantly graced with the weight of compassion.
May Kṣemaṅkarī, whose perfections are unimpaired within my heart, spread forth; may she be forgiven. || 5 ||
Even the Lord of Beings, embracing his own self, has fallen into madness; had that skillful Lord not expanded [his effort] in the protection of life,
[the world] would have been deprived of the moon and the essence of sandalwood by fate.
It has not been tasted by the fragrance of the single lotus that is the state of Lord Bhava, which is filled with the flowing honey of its core of bold eloquence.
Alas, alas! O Mother,

in one like me— whose inner self shines with the consecration of the essence of the bliss of Brahman, perfected through the utterances of the ocean of beginningless delusion— how can there be any hope?
May this overflowing torrent of the glorious aesthetic sentiment of devotion (bhakti-rasa), capable of overcoming the intense mental anguish of you hosts of gods, ever flow forth.

The triad of the deity consisting of the stainless bliss of consciousness— which spreads from the interior of the mass of rays flashing from His feet, dispelling the darkness that clings to millions of suns—
effects creation, extends preservation, and again dissolves the world.
May that splendor, like a mass of clouds as dark as freshly split collyrium, ever abide within our hearts. || 8 ||
She who constantly clings to the demon Tamas, whose head is filled with darkness spreading from within his mouth as he stumbles, runs, roars, and clearly manifests in the guise of a buffalo—
she is Durgā, the remover of misfortune, who terrifies the enemies within a hundred thousand leagues and protects from the fortress of fear.
May she who gladdens with victory, and who is skilled in rending the wives of the visible enemies of the gods, be triumphant.

In that ocean of many crooked, copper-hued arrows— arising from the swelling armies of Indra and other gods, who were short-statured yet exalted, with their fly-whisks and the hem of their shields dancing like a storm—
the wicked Asuras were being slaughtered with arrogance as their heads were tossed about by the spreading gale of the wind.
In which all birds were set ablaze by hunger and thirst due to being torn into pieces and fragments.
In the space between the horns of a wild buffalo, its head bent sideways in a state of frenzy as it delivers a violent blow with a shimmering, terrifying,
and death-dealing club, may [the Lord] be served by the Mothers, whose ears are adorned with golden ornaments set within eight-petaled lotuses.
One should remember her in the courtyard of the dawn, reeling with the joy of battle.
I bow to Śivā, who holds in her upper and lower hands— arranged clockwise and counter-clockwise— a discus, a conch, a flaying knife, a shield, an arrow, a bow, a trident,
and the gesture that dispels fear; she is dark-complexioned, with her mass of hair tied in a high topknot by a cluster of locks as thick as dark clouds.
Her terrifying mouth was radiant with the clashing of stumbling heroes, and she was formidable with her fierce, loud laughter. || 12 ||
Thus, O Goddess, those who meditate upon your sinless form— which is worshipped by Śakra and others— overcome difficulties and the like, and achieve the shaking of enemy cities,
sovereignty, victory over foes, and the wisdom of true purpose.
For those who perform such deeds as causing the freezing, melting, and killing of the mirror of the nectar of poetry, [the opposite] happens to them of its own accord. || 13 ||

O Goddess, if those who desire liberation and other blessings hear or recite this hymn— which is secretly taught as the practice of mantra-extraction and ritual service through the focused meditation on the pair of Your lotus feet— then [those desires] shall be swiftly attained for them.
O Mother of the worlds, they come into the hands [of your grace]; salutations to you, victory to you! || 14 ||
Thus ends the *Mahiṣamardinī-stotra*. Now follows the *Mahiṣamardinī-kavaca*.
Īśvara said:
Now, O Great Goddess, I shall declare the armor (kavaca) that grants all desires,
by obtaining the grace of which one becomes Sadāśiva himself.
Having first uttered the syllable *oṃ*, the practitioner of mantra should daily recite the armor (*kavaca*) for the sake of attaining the mantra and for the accomplishment of the mantra's phonemes.
For the armor-mantra (kavaca) of Mahiṣamardinī, the venerable Mahākāla is the seer (ṛṣi), the Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas),
the Primordial Power (Ādyāśakti) is the deity (devatā), and the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of life. || 3 ||
Klīṃ! May the goddess Kāminī, the bestower of desires, protect my head.
Ma! May the goddess Maheśvarī protect me in the pair of eyes. (4)
May the syllable *hīṃ* protect the face, and may Hiṅgulā, the leader of the Asuras, protect it;
may the syllable *ṣa* protect me, and may Śvetā and Aparājitā protect my tongue. (5)
May the goddess Mardinī, the leader of the gods, protect me with the syllable *ma*;
may the goddess Sāvitrī, the destroyer of time, protect me with the syllable *rḍi*.
May Nikāra protect me constantly in the heart, the two arms, the sides, the navel,
the penis, the anus, the throat, the two ears, the back, as well as the crest-lock,
the armor, the feet, the mouth, and the pair of shanks. || 7 ||
May she who is endowed with all powers protect me in every limb, Svāhā! May Kāmādyā protect me, Svāhā! May Mardinī protect my head in every limb, Svāhā!
May the ten-syllabled Mahāvidyā protect me in all my limbs;
may Mardinī protect me constantly, and may Mardinī always grant me refuge.

In a kingdom, as well as in a fortress, amidst the fears of lions, tigers, and the like, in a cremation ground, in a wilderness, in a stronghold, on a boat, or in the midst of fire—may Mardinī protect [me] constantly; may Mardinī always guard [me]. (10)
May the goddess Durgā protect me always; may Āryā protect me always. May Prabhā protect me, O Great Goddess; may Kanakā protect me at all times. (11)
May Kṛttikā protect me constantly; may Abhayā protect me at all times. May Prabhā protect me, and may Mahāmāyā protect me; may Māyā always protect me. (12)
May Prabhā protect me, O Great Goddess; may Vimalā protect me always.
May Nandinī protect me constantly; may Suprabhā protect me at all times. (13)
May Vijayā protect me everywhere; may the nine Śaktis protect the limbs of the Goddess. May the Śaktis protect me constantly, and may the Mudrās always protect me. (14)
May Jayā protect [me] always; may Sūkṣmā protect [me] at all times.
May the Yoginīs protect [me] constantly; may the Khecarīs protect [me] forever. (15)
May the ḍākinīs protect me constantly; may the siddhas always protect me.
May the Goddess Mahiṣamardinī protect me everywhere and at all times. 16.
Thus has this divine armor, which grants all desires, been recounted to you;
it must not be spoken of here or there, but must be guarded with great effort.
Kept secret in all tantras, it is proclaimed in the Viśvasāra:
everywhere this Vidyā is easily obtained, but this great armor (kavaca) is difficult to find. 18.

O Maheśvarī, one should not reveal this divine hymn or the armor (kavaca) difficult even for the gods to obtain to one who is deceitful, devoid of devotion, a slanderer, deficient in limbs, possessing extra limbs, cruel, or a speaker of falsehoods. (19)
O Maheśānī, that which was spoken by Śaṅkara must not be told here or there; having given it to those unworthy, the siddhis perish in due course.
The mantras turn away and depart after uttering a most terrible curse; misfortune shall befall him. Therefore, one should protect [the mantra] with great effort. (21)
O Maheśvarī, having written [the mantra] on birch bark with gorocanā and saffron during an auspicious conjunction, or likewise during the yoga of Brahmendra or Vaidhṛti; || 22 ||
Or during the asterism of Śravaṇā, Revatī, or Punarvasu, when the yoga is Siddhiyoga, Vava, or likewise Kaulava, or Vaṇija. || 23 ||
Indeed, during the conjunction with the three Uttaras as well as the three Pūrvas, or under Aśvinī or Rohiṇī, on the third or ninth lunar day; || 24 ||
On the eighth, the fourteenth, the sixth, or the fifth lunar day;
or on the new moon or the full moon—likewise at night in a remote wilderness.
In a solitary liṅga, in a cremation ground, in an empty house, or in a temple of Śiva—whether by the Guru, by Vaiṣṇavas, or even with self-arisen flowers—[one should worship]. (26)
Having drawn [the deity] with white or red flowers, sandalwood mixed with red [pigments],
and charcoal from a funeral pyre on a cloth, one should wear it; for him,
there shall be the accomplishment of all aims— so it was spoken by Śaṅkara.
Having worshipped the maiden and offered the hymn to the Goddess,
and having recited it, he should feed the most excellent Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas;
and for three days, he should indeed perform the narrative of Ākheṭaka.
Then one should wear this great protection, the armor that grants all desires.
For him there are no mental anxieties or physical ailments, nor is there ever any suffering, grief, or fear;
having seen him, even a debater becomes mute, and a king behaves like a servant.
He who, being self-controlled and pure, recites this for one month every day—
eating sacrificial food (haviṣya) by day and devoted to strength (śakti) at night—
should always chant it six thousand times daily.
In six months, or even in three months, one certainly becomes a sky-walker.
One without a son obtains a son; the poor man becomes wealthy;
the diseased becomes healthy and strong; and even a king may fall into servitude.
One should constantly recite this vidyā, especially within the womb of a menstruating woman;
the wise one who acts in this way is indeed Śrī Sadāśiva himself. (32)
Thus ends the *Mahiṣamardinī-kavaca* in the *Viśvasāra-tantra*.
Now begins the *Lakṣmī-stotra*. The Lord said:
O Goddess Kamalā, worshipped by the three worlds, beloved of Viṣṇu!
Just as you are immovable, O Kṛṣṇā, so may you be firm within me. (1)
The Sovereign, Kamalā, Cañcalā, Lakṣmī, Calā, Bhūti, Haripriyā, Padmā, Padmālayā, Sampat, Uccaiḥ, and Śrīpadmadhāriṇī. || 2 ||
Whoever, having fully worshipped Lakṣmī, recites these twelve names, for him prosperity shall become stable along with sons, wife, and other kin. (3)
Thus ends the Lakṣmī-stotra in the Viśvasāra-tantra. Now begins the Akṣmī-kavaca. The Lord said:
Now, O Maheśānī, I shall declare the armor (kavaca) that grants all desires;
by the mere knowledge of which one becomes Sadāśiva himself.
O Goddess of gods, a man need not perform worship for him; he should merely recite the mantra.
He shall become a son of Pārvatī, honored by all the scriptures. (2)
She who bestows wealth should always be served, especially by those seeking knowledge;
Kamalā, the beloved of Viṣṇu, should always be served by students of learning.

Of this armor (kavaca) of the four-syllabled consort of Viṣṇu, the Lord Śiva is the seer (ṛṣi), the Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), Vāgbhavī is the deity (devatā), Vāgbhava is the seed-syllable (bīja), Lajjā is the power (śakti), Ramā is the bolt (kīlaka), and the armor consists of the Kāma-bīja for my protection.
This is the application for the sake of attaining excellence in poetry, great scholarship, and the abundance of all supernatural powers (*siddhi*).
May the syllable *Aiṃ*, the Vāgbhavī who bestows all powers, protect my head.
May *Hrīṃ* protect the space between my eyes, and may Śāṅkarī protect the pair of my eyes. (4)
On the tongue, the perimeter of the mouth, the ears, the cheeks, the nostrils, the base of the lips, the rows of teeth, the root of the palate, and again on the jaw; || 5 ||
May Lakṣmī, the consort of Viṣṇu, whose form is the color of prosperity, protect me;
and may Pārvatī protect my two ears, my two arms, and my two breasts.
In the heart, at the wrists, in the neck, on both sides,
likewise in the region of the back, and in the private parts— on the left as well as on the right.
Furthermore, [one should place them] on the lap, the hips, the navel, the two shanks,
the two knee-circles, the pair of feet, and at the roots of the ankles and toes.

May the great goddess Kāmeśī, who is supreme elevation, protect [me] with her power of life-force (prāṇa-śakti), at the parting of the hair, on the head, and likewise in all limbs; Svadhā! May she protect! 9.
May Puṣṭi protect me; may Mahāmāyā, the most excellent one, protect me at all times.
May the Ṛṣi protect me always, O Goddess, you who are beloved by Śambhu everywhere. 10.
May Vāgbhavī protect me always; may the consort of Hara protect me;
may the great goddess Ramā protect me; and may Māyā herself, the self-sovereign, protect me.
May Lakṣmī, the illusion of Viṣṇu and queen of the gods, protect me in all my limbs;
may Vijayā protect me in my home, and Jayā always protect me.
May Śivadūtī protect me always; may Sundarī protect me at all times.
May Bhairavī protect me everywhere; may Bheruṇḍā protect me forever.
May Tvaritā protect me always; may Ugratārā protect me forever.
May Kālikā protect me constantly; may Kālarātri protect me forever. (14)
May Navadurgā protect me always; may Kāmākhyā protect me at all times;
may the Yoginīs protect me always; and may the Mudrās protect me forever. (15)
May the goddesses who abide in the wheel, along with the hosts of yoginīs, protect me always—in all places, in all undertakings, in all actions, and at all times. (16)
May the Goddess of gods, Lakṣmī, the bestower of all prosperity, protect me.
Thus has this divine armor been told to you for the sake of attaining all perfections.
O Maheśvarī, if one desires one's own welfare, this should not be spoken anywhere to one who is deceitful, devoid of devotion, or a reviler.
One should never show [the deity] to those with deficient limbs or those with redundant limbs;
nor should one show the divine hymn (stava), for by showing it, one becomes a destroyer of Śiva.
One should bestow this supreme armor upon one who is of noble birth, possessed of great aspiration, devoted to the worship of Durgā, a Vaiṣṇava, and pure.
One should bestow this armor, which is consistent with all tantras, upon one's own disciple who is peaceful, wealthy, and likewise possessed of knowledge; so it has been said. (21)
On a Saturday or a Tuesday, one should write the mantra, complete with all its wheels, using red sandalwood paste and barley-meal (yāvaka).
One should draw the divine armor with auspicious *svayambhū* flowers,
with one's own semen and the semen of the preceding [ancestors], combined with various fragrances.
With gorocanā, saffron, or red sandalwood,
on an auspicious lunar day, in a favorable yoga, or under the asterism Śravaṇā on a Sunday.
Under the asterisms of Aśvinī, Kṛttikā, Phalgunī, or Maghā;
during the conjunction of Pūrvabhādrapadā or Svātī; and on a Tuesday. (25)
One should write or recite the hymn in a temple during an auspicious conjunction (yoga),
especially during the Āyuṣmat, Prīti, and Brahman yogas.
During the Indrayoga, the Śubhayoga, and likewise the Śukrayoga;
during Kaulava, Bālava, and Vaṇija—O best of men! (27)
In an empty house, in a cremation ground, or especially in a secluded place,
having worshipped a young maiden, one should sacrifice to the eternal Goddess.
One should worship the Supreme Deity with fish, meat, vegetables, and cakes,
especially with ghee and other offerings, along with flowers and incense.
Having fed the Brāhmaṇas, one should worship the Supreme Goddess;
there, one should perform the narrative of Ākheṭaka for three days.
Then one should perform the great protection as proclaimed by Śaṅkara;
one obtains [powers such as] killing, inciting hatred, and so forth—of this there is no doubt. He shall become a son of Pārvatī, honored by all the scriptures. || 31 ||
The Guru is the god Hara himself, and his wife is the beloved of Hara;
for him who worships them as non-different, spiritual perfection is not far off.
That mortal who here constantly recites this with a moist inner soul perceives the specific fruit of the recitation as follows:
he becomes one whose station is elevated by prosperity.
May it be for a long time for those characterized by the fortune of the crowns of kings who bow at his feet. || 33 ||
Thus ends the Lakṣmī-kavaca in the Viśvasāra-tantra. Now follows the Sarasvatī-stotra.
Brahmā said:
O *Hrīṃ Hrīḥ*, you whose single seed-syllable is dear to the heart; you whose splendor is as clear as a lotus radiant with moonlight;

O auspicious one, favorable to the fortunate; you who are a forest-fire to the woods of evil intellect; you whose lotus feet are worshipped by the whole world; O Lotus, seated upon a lotus; you who bestow the joy of the minds of those who bow before you!
O Goddess, beloved of Hari, in whom the mass of ignorance has been utterly consumed, you who are the essence of the world! || 2 ||

Aiṃ Aiṃ Aiṃ! O you who are the essence of the splendor of the lotus-face born from the *kavala* [of the] desired mantra; O you who manifest as both form and formlessness; O you who consist of all qualities yet are devoid of qualities and free from modification;
O you who are neither gross nor subtle, whose object is unknown and whose true nature is not even known—[in you] the universe [rests].
In the midst of the universe, honored by the best of gods, you are partless and eternally pure.
Hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ! O you who are pleased by the recitation of mantras, who wear the moon as a crown, and who hold a *valvaja* grass brush in your hand;
O Mother, Mother, salutations to you! Burn away, burn away dullness and grant me excellent intelligence!
O Knowledge (*Vidyā*), sung in the Upanishads, recited by the Vedas, bestower of liberation, path to emancipation!
O Śāradā, wearer of white garlands, whose power transcends all paths, be the bestower of boons upon me! || 4 ||

Dhrīṃ dhrīṃ dhrīṃ! O you who are known as Dhāraṇā, to be celebrated by the names Dhṛti, Mati, and Nūti; eternal and yet non-eternal, both caused and uncaused; measured by the hosts of sages; both new and indeed ancient;
meritorious, possessing the power of merit; measured by Hari and Hara; pure in color, golden-hued, and the primordial Mother.
In the *mātrārddha-tattva*, in *matimatī*, in *matide*, and in the *mādhavaprīti-nāda*.

Hrīṃ kṣīṃ dhīṃ hrīṃ! O you whose very nature is *hrīṃ*, burn away my misfortune; O you who hold a book in your hand, whose mind is contented in form, whose face is smiling, O auspicious one, O science of paralyzing and crushing!
O you who flow with enchanting delusion, grant me good intellect, O eternal destroyer of darkness!
You are the song, the cow, speech, and Sarasvatī; you are the tongue of the bull among poets, the bestower of perfection, and the perfected lore.

Sauṃ Sauṃ Sauṃ! O Śakti-seed syllable, whose nature is the lotus-face of the Lotus-born (Brahmā), who manifests both form and formlessness, who consists of all qualities yet is beyond qualities and changeless;
who is neither gross nor subtle, whose majesty is unknown, and who is the reality of the knowledge to be recited—O Viśvā! [Salutations].
In the midst of the universe, measured by the hosts of gods, it is partless and eternally pure. || 7 ||
I praise you, I bow to you; take hold of my tongue and never forsake it. O Goddess, let not my intellect become perverse, nor my mind turn toward sin.
May I never experience suffering, even in times of adversity; may I have no agitation regarding the scriptures, debate, or the composition of poetry; and may my intellect never be dull. 8.

He who, bowed with devotion, praises her every day at dawn with these principal verses— whether he be eloquent like Bṛhaspati, possessed of desired wealth, a master of speech, or cleansed of all taint—
shall obtain his heart’s desires; and that Goddess shall protect him constantly, as if he were her own son.
His good fortune spreads throughout the world, and his poetry proceeds free from obstacles.
A man who observes celibacy, keeps vows, maintains silence, and abstains from meat on the thirteenth lunar day becomes a follower of Sarasvatī through recitation; he shall attain his desired objects.
On both fortnights, the wise man who, having meditated upon the goddess Sarasvatī, recites [this] twenty-one times for thirteen days without interruption; || 11 ||
One who [worships] the Goddess clad in white garments and adorned with white ornaments attains his desired fruit in this world; of this there is no doubt.
Thus Brahmā himself spoke this auspicious hymn of praise to Sarasvatī;
he who recites it daily with diligence bestows immortality.
Thus ends the hymn to Sarasvatī composed by Brahmā in the *Brahma Purāṇa*.
Now begins the hymn to Gaṇeśa:
The virtuous proclaim the syllable *Oṃ* as the first; it is that which the Vedas also extol.
I worship that elephant-faced one whose feet are bowed to by hosts of gods, who is adorned with the crescent moon as his crest-jewel,

and who is capable of quenching the forest fire of worldly existence for those intent on worshipping his lotus feet; I perpetually praise that Vighneśvara, who resembles a lotus and from whom streams of ichor flow incessantly.

Who could forget the son of the enemy of Ananga (Kārttikeya), who— his body anointed with fresh saffron, his form clinging to the mud of rut like a swarm of intoxicated bees— was warding them off with the flapping of his own ears?

Filled with devotion, they worship Gajānana, who, having brought the water of the Gaṅgā dwelling within the matted locks of Śambhu with his lotus-hand, worships Śiva from nearby with playful gestures.

Furthermore, while in the state of childhood, as he was washing the breasts of the Mountain King’s daughter with the spray from his trunk for his own sake, I worship that elephant-faced one with childlike innocence— those sprays which, released from the hollow of his trunk by you, were [caught] by the hand of the uplifted elephant-face.
In the courtyard of the sky, those stars wander, possessing a luster like pearls, with Time as their soul.
While the elephant-faced one was sporting in the ocean as the flood of water transgressed the shore,

the gods, reflecting upon the end of the eon, praised the Lord of Kailāsa with Vedic hymns. While the elephant-faced one, for whom a serpent serves as an upper garment, was sporting with hosts of divine youths—
Having abandoned their course through time for a moment within you, those two attained the state of being a ball and the moon.

I take refuge in Heramba, who is as tawny as the sun, the sole friend of the gods, the sages, and his devoted followers, who incessantly expounds the limitless meanings of all the Agamas through his five faces that laugh with joy.

My mind does not abandon that elephant-faced one, who out of compassion makes the earth blessed with his two exceedingly tender lotus-feet, and who is the causeless cause according to the words of the authoritative sages.

I worship that son of the Moon-crested Lord, a mass of bliss, whom he propitiated through austerities; he who, in former times, having drawn the Purāṇa with the tip of his tusk, offered it to the son of Satyavatī.

Worship the primordial Lord of Obstacles, who is the abode of the Vedas and the object of all praises; who is a playful incarnation of the Supreme Self; and who is indivisible, being either of the nature of a serpent or of the nature of a man.
Holding a noose and a goad, with his tusk broken, he carries his desired objects in his hands;
with streams of broad spray resembling pearls released from the hollows of his trunk, he sprinkles his own body.
I worship the two Śivas. || 13 ||

I constantly worship that son of Śambhu, whom those who know the Vedas call Brahman— the one who is many yet one, the elephant with a single tusk, the embodiment of consciousness, and the primordial seed of the universe—
his eyes restless as he gazes upon the lotus-face of his own beloved seated on his lap.
I worship Him, who deludes the entire universe, whose lotus-face is blooming with the splendor of intoxication.
O Gajānana, for those who, having first propitiated you, study all the scriptures,
there is nothing further to be learned from them; if there were, then everything [else] would be as if unreal.

I take refuge in Him who is golden-hued, the Lord of the universe, the ancient Seer situated within the solar orb, the elephant-faced one into whom the virtuous enter through the yoga of that [final] time. 17.
I worship that Person, the essence of bliss, who dwells within the heart and is celebrated in the Vedanta;
by whose splendor the darkness of obstacles for people is utterly dissolved. I worship Gajanana.
May He, who out of childishness desired to pull off the crescent moon from Śambhu’s mass of matted hair with His own trunk— mistaking it for a fruit— and who, having broken His tusk,
now offers coconuts, plantains, and other fruits to strike down the bolts of obstacles, bestow prosperity upon us.
May I always worship the Lord, whose face is like a rutting elephant, who manifests his power, and who is ever-desired. || 20 ||

Those who duly praise the primordial one with this hymn—the one whose face is like that of the king of elephants, whom he is worshipped by means of numerous sacrifices and manifold austerities—become repositories of all prosperity. 21.
Thus ends the Gaṇeśastavarāja. Now follows the Haridrāgaṇeśakavaca.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O beloved, I shall declare the armor (kavaca) that bestows all accomplishments;
by reciting it and causing others to recite it, a man is liberated from every peril.
O Goddess, if one recites the mantra of Gaṇeśa without knowing his armor-mantra (kavaca),
success will not arise for him even in hundreds of crores of kalpas.
Oṃ! May Āmoda protect the head, and Pramoda the top of the crest-lock;
may Sammoda protect the pair of eyebrows, and Gaṇādhipa the space between the eyebrows. || 3 ||
May Gaṇākrīḍa protect my pair of eyes, and Gaṇanāyaka, accompanied by Gaṇakrīḍā, protect my nose and face for the attainment of all perfections. May he protect [me] for the sake of all success. (4)
May Sumukha protect the tongue; may Durmukha always protect the neck;
may Vighneśa protect the heart, and may Vighnanāśa protect the chest.
May the Leader of the Gaṇas protect my pair of arms;
may the Creator of Obstacles protect my belly, and the Creator of Obstacles protect my genitals.
May Gajavaktra protect my waist; may Ekadanta protect my hips; and may Lambodara always protect my private parts. || 7 ||
May he who has a serpent for his sacred thread protect me with his pair of feet;
may the reciter always protect me, and may the Lord of the Gaṇas protect my knees and shanks.
May the yellow-hued Gaṇanāyaka protect me always in every limb;
O Maheśvarī, whoever should recite this daily concerning Gaṇeśa— || 9 ||
This armor, known as "The All-Accomplishing," destroys all obstacles;
it directly bestows all perfections and liberates one from all sins. (10)
It directly bestows all prosperity, it is the direct liberation from all sins;
it directly bestows all prosperity and brings about the destruction of all enemies.
Afflictions by planets, fever, disease, and whatever other [troubles] such as those caused by Guhyakas and the like,
go to destruction at that very moment simply through recitation and retention.
O Goddess, O Great Mistress, this armor, honored by the gods and which bestows wealth and grain, is equal to that of Gaṇeśa; there is nothing else like it in the three worlds. (13)
O Great Goddess, what is the use of other worthless talk on this earth, wherein one's life is merely spent? (14)
Thus ends the *Haridrāgaṇeśakavaca* in the *Viśvasāra-tantra*. Now begins the *Śrīsūryakavaca*.
The venerable Sūrya said:
O Sāmba, O Sāmba, O mighty-armed one, hear from me this auspicious armor, the most wonderful armor known as the "Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds. (1)
Knowing which, the knower of mantras certainly attains the fruit;
and by wearing which, Mahādeva became the lord of the Gaṇas. || 2 ||
Through recitation and retention, Viṣṇu is the eternal protector of all;
likewise, Indra and all the others shall attain complete sovereignty.
For the Kavaca, Brahmā is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi), the Anuṣṭubh is said to be the meter (chandas),
and the deity here is Śrī Sūrya, who is saluted by all the gods.
The application of the Vinaya has been proclaimed for the sake of health, fame, and liberation.
May the Praṇava protect my head; may the syllable Ghṛṇi protect my forehead.
May Sūrya protect the pair of eyes, and Āditya the pair of ears;
may the eight-syllabled great mantra grant the fruit of all desired objects. (6)
May the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* protect my mouth; may Bhuvaneśvarī protect my heart;
and may the moon-seed-syllable (*saṃ*) joined with the visarga protect the region of my private parts.
This three-syllabled great mantra is concealed in all the tantras:
Śiva joined with Fire and adorned with the left eye and the bindu. (8)
The single-syllable great mantra of the glorious Sun is proclaimed;
it is known as the wish-fulfilling gem for desires, a mantra more secret than the secret. || 9 ||
"May the supreme Manu protect [me] always from the head down to the feet.
Thus has this divine [mantra], difficult to find in the three worlds, been told to you. (10)
It bestows prosperity and constant luster, increases wealth and health, pacifies diseases such as leprosy, and destroys even great maladies. (11)
Whoever recites this daily at the three junctions of the day shall become free from disease and endowed with strength.
What need is there for much speaking here? Whatever resides in one's mind [shall be attained]. (12)
All of that indeed comes to pass by wearing this armor;
[so too do] the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas.
Brahma-rākṣasas and vetālas are not even capable of looking [at him];
they flee from afar at the mere mention of his name. 14.
Having inscribed it upon birch bark with yellow pigment, agallochum, and saffron, especially on a Sunday, at the sun's transit (saṃkrānti), or on the seventh lunar day; || 15 ||
The best of practitioners should wear it; he shall become a conqueror of the three worlds.
Having placed it within three metals, he should wear it on his right arm. (16)
Whether on the crest-lock or on the neck, he too is undoubtedly the Sun;
thus, O Sāmba, has this [mantra] named Trailokyamaṅgala been told to you.
This armor, difficult to obtain in the world, has been revealed out of affection for you.
Without knowing this divine armor, whoever should recite the supreme Sūrya-mantra will not attain success even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Thus ends the *Sūryakavaca*, named *Trailokyamaṅgala*, from the *Brahmayāmala*.
Now begins the *Śrīviṣṇustava*:
Oṃ! Having taken up all the Vedas and the oceans, and having slain the exceedingly fierce enemy Śaṅkha...

Worship today that primordial Viṣṇu, who in the past gave [the Vedas] to the Grandfather (Brahmā); when the great ocean was churned by the gods and asuras using Vāsuki and Mandara for the sake of divine nectar,
I remember him as the Tortoise who became the support for the earth as it was tossed about by a mighty force.

I take refuge in that Primordial Boar (Ādikola), who, with a mind capable of shattering the suffering of his devotees, raised up the earth from between the pillars as Nṛsiṃha; he by whom the earth— with the ocean for its girdle, the rivers for its upper garment, and Mount Meru for the weight of its crown— was lifted up upon the tip of his tusk.
I do not forget him who tore asunder the enemy of the gods with the tips of his sharpened claws;
whose single foot, adorned by the four oceans, was too vast for the earth to serve as a deposit—
him, the all-pervading Trivikrama, the sole peerless one among the gods, I bow down.
I bow to that foremost of heroes, Rāma, who, having slain kings twenty-one times over, performed a libation of blood with the strength of his staff-like arms; he who,
having taken birth in the lineage of the Raghus, constructed a bridge across the depths of the ocean.
I bow with devotion to that Lord of Sītā who bound the Lord of Laṅkā;
who, having dragged all the asuras out with his plow, reduced them to powder with blows from his mace;
and who, having encountered the powerful Kṛṣṇa, displayed even greater strength—I worship him with devotion.
To Balabhadra Rāma. || 8 ||

I bow down to that Buddha, the fundamental source, who of old, intending to enable the gods to conquer the asuras, composed a treatise of unfailing efficacy, adorned with the marks and attire of Śrīvara.

At the end of the aeon, he who, terrifying in his splendor, consumed with his own brilliance that horse which was of the nature of Viṣṇu, and who in a mere twinkling of an eye joined himself with all his own deities— we worship him as he holds the conch,
the excellent discus, the beautiful mace, and the lotus in his four hands.
I praise Viṣṇu in my heart—him who is mounted upon Garuḍa, marked with the Śrīvatsa, the primordial source of the universe, and dark as a Tamāla tree. 11.

I repeatedly remember the primordial one, who resembles a rain cloud, whose face is beautified by an inner smile, whose lotus-eyes are fully blossomed, and who reclines within the ocean of milk upon the preeminent Śeṣa— the source of the Vedas. One should gratify the Lord of the World, who is identical with the universe, with this hymn of praise.
For the attainment of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, [one should worship] the Supreme Person.
Thus ends the *Śrīviṣṇustava*. Now begins the *Śrīrāmastotra*. Śrī Hanumān said:
I bow to that fierce one who was the king even of the animals assembled together, such as those headed by Sugrīva. || 1 ||
I bow to that hero who, on the shore of the ocean, granted supreme refuge to Vibhīṣaṇa, who had sought him for protection just once.
I bow to that Great Viṣṇu, who is the great one, the honored, the all-pervading, the nectar of compassion of the great ocean, and by whom Jaṭāyu was praised. || 3 ||
I bow to that blazing one, by whose splendor the fires and other elements are nourished and burn, and who shines forth as independent.
I bow to that Sarvatomukha, by whom, through his sport, the warriors of the lord of the Rākṣasas were shown [to destruction] from every direction in battle. || 5 ||
I bow to that Nṛsiṃha, who, like a lion preeminent among creatures, destroys those who have attained human form as well as those among men.
I bow to that terrifying [form] from which the wind, the sun, fire, and Indra, along with Death himself, are afraid; it strikes terror into the wicked.
I bow to that Blessed One, who, through his own innate generosity, always bestows auspiciousness upon others without regard for their worthiness. (8)
I bow to that Death of Death, who slays even death for his own servants and grants all desired objects; there are many illustrative examples of this. (9)
I bow down to that Lord of all the gods, who is worthy of being saluted by even the Supreme Person when he bows at his lotus feet. || 10 ||
Having surrendered my very self as a servant, I worship Rāma—the scion of Raghu—along with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, every single day. (11)
The servants of Yama are eternally the servants of the illustrious Rāmabhadra;
the quarters of the sky are composed of Śiva for him, and the supernatural powers (siddhis) are his maidservants.
Whoever recites daily this hymn, which is the essence of the king of mantras, as proclaimed by Hanumān, shall possess devotion toward Rāma. (13)
Thus ends the Śrī Rāma Stotra, consisting of the King of Mantras, from the Śrī Hanumat Kalpa. Now begins the hymn named the Rāmāṣṭaśataka.
Vedavyāsa said:
Listen, O son of Gaṅgā, I shall proclaim the meritorious hundred-and-eight names of Rāma of wondrous deeds, which destroy even the greatest sins.
There exists nothing more secret than this in the three worlds. (1)
On the delightful peak of Kailāsa, adorned with various jewels, Śaṅkara—
having become single-mindedly disciplined and having propitiated Viṣṇu with devotion—
sat down and then spoke to Pārvatī as he was about to eat. || 2 ||
"O Pārvatī, O you who are adored by the world, come with me to eat.
To him, the goddess Pārvatī replied after reciting the *Nāmasahasraka*:
"Then I shall eat, O God; let it be eaten by you first, O Lord. (3)
Then the Supreme Lord, laughing, said to her:
"O Pārvatī, you are blessed; you have performed meritorious deeds; you are a devotee of Viṣṇu."
O Goddess, devotion to Viṣṇu is indeed difficult to attain without good fortune;
yet, O Pārvatī, as I listen to these names beginning with the letter 'Ra,' [I feel such fortune].
The mind attains clarity through the recollection of Rāma’s name;
for yogis delight in the infinite, true bliss that is the conscious Self.
Thus, by the word "Rāma," the Supreme Brahman is denoted. (6)
"O Rāma, O Rāma! I delight in the delightful Rāma.
Among the thousand names [of the Lord], O lady of beautiful countenance, the name 'Rāma' stands supreme.
Having uttered 'Rāma,' O Great Goddess, enjoy yourself now together with me. (7)
Then, having uttered the name "Rāma" and having eaten together with him, Pārvatī,
the great goddess, remained seated there after eating along with her husband.
With a mind overflowing with affection, he questioned Śrī Mahādeva:
"O Rāma, you have spoken of the name [of the Lord] which is equal to the Thousand Names;
if there are other names as well for the enemy of Rāvaṇa,"
"O Lord of Gods, let it be told to me; my delight therein is supreme."
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall declare the names of Rāmacandra;
whatever words there may be, whether worldly or Vedic, O Pārvatī.
The names of Rāmabhadra exceed one thousand.
Among those, indeed, the one hundred and eight names are the most preeminent;
the fruit of each single name of Viṣṇu is superior to that of all the Vedas.
Among thousands of such names, O Pārvatī, the name of Rāma is considered supreme.
For one who chants all the Vedas and all the mantras, the merit obtained through the name of Rāma alone is ten million times greater than that. 12.

Now, for this hymn of one hundred and eight names of Śrī Rāma: the seer is Īśvara, the meter is Anuṣṭubh, the deity is Śrī Rāmacandra, and the application is in recitation for the sake of pleasing Śrī Rāmacandra. 13.
Oṃ, Śrī Rāma, Rāmabhadra, Rāmacandra, the Eternal One.
The lotus-eyed, illustrious lord of kings, the foremost of the Raghus. || 14 ||
The beloved of Jānakī, the victorious, the friend of Citrāṅgada, Janārdana, the one dear to Viśvāmitra, the self-controlled, and the one intent on protecting those who seek refuge. || 15 ||
The subduer of Bālin, eloquent, truthful in speech, and of true valor;
one whose vows are truth, who is the fruit of his own observances, and who is always the refuge of Hanūmat. (16)
The son of Kauśalyā, the destroyer of Khara, the one skilled in the slaying of Virādha, the protector of Vibhīṣaṇa, and the remover of the heads of the ten-necked Rāvaṇa. || 17 ||
The breaker of the seven palm trees, the shatterer of Hara’s bow, the fire that consumed the great pride of Jamadagni’s son, and the slayer of Tāḍakā. || 18 ||
He is the essence of the Vedānta, the immeasurable Self, the physician for worldly existence, and the medicine;
he is the destroyer of the three-headed Dūṣaṇa, the triple-formed one, the possessor of the three qualities, and the triple Veda.
Trivikrama, the soul of the three worlds, renowned for his meritorious conduct;
the protector of the three worlds, the wielder of the bow, and the performer of merit in the Daṇḍa forest. || 10 ||
He is the purifier of Ahalyā, devoted to his father, the bestower of boons, one who has conquered his senses, conquered his anger, conquered his greed, and the teacher of the world. (21)
He is the leader of the hosts of bears and monkeys, the refuge of Citrakūṭa, the bestower of protection and boons upon Jayanta, and the one served by the son of Sumitrā.
He is the supreme lord of all the gods, the one who restores life to dead children,
the slayer of Māyāmārīca, the possessor of great enjoyments, and the one with mighty arms.
Praised by all the gods, gentle, devoted to Brahman, and extolled by sages;
he is the great yogi, most magnanimous, and the bestower of the desired kingdom upon Sugrīva.
He is the sacred ford that yields fruit superior to all merit, the destroyer of all sins;
he is the primal person, the great person, and likewise the supreme person.
Rāghava is the source of merit, the essence of compassion, the ancient one, and the Supreme Person; he has a smiling face, speaks with moderation, and speaks with fullness.
Profound with infinite virtues, preeminent in the qualities of the wise and noble,
he whose conduct was that of an illusory human was worshipped by Mahādeva.
The builder of the bridge, the conqueror of the lord of waters, Hari who consists of all sacred fords;
he of dark limbs, the beautiful one, the hero, clad in yellow garments, and the wielder of the bow.
He is the Lord of all sacrifices, the sacrifice itself, free from old age and death; he is the installer of the Śiva-liṅga, liberated from the entire multitude of sins. || 29 ||
He is the Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
He is the supreme light, the supreme abode, the ultimate limit, and higher than the highest.
Pareśa, Parāga, Pāra, Sarvadevātmaka, Śiva—these are the one hundred and eight auspicious names of Nāma. (31)
O Goddess, this which is more secret than the secret has been proclaimed out of affection for you.
Whoever should read or even hear it with a mind endowed with devotion,
he is liberated from all sins arising from hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Waters turn into dry land, enemies become friends, kings fall into servitude, and fires attain gentleness. (33)
All beings become favorable, and even fickle fortunes attain stability;
the planets become gracious, while calamities come to an end. (34)
O Daughter of the Mountain, for a person who recites [this] with a spirit of devotion,
whoever should recite it with supreme devotion, the three worlds shall be under his control;
whatever he desires in his heart, he attains that through this chanting.
Whoever recites the one hundred and eight names of Rāmacandra shall not be tainted by sin, even if he is of base birth, through that very knowledge. (36)
The fruit that is obtained through all the Vedas, sacred fords, acts of charity, and ascetic penances is attained ten million times over by means of this hymn. (37)
Reciting it at all auspicious times, one attains infinity;
for thousands of crores of kalpas and hundreds of crores of kalpas,
one obtains residence in Vaikuṇṭha, together with ten ancestors and ten descendants.
Those men who praise Rāma— who is dark like a blade of dūrvā grass, lotus-eyed, and clad in yellow garments— with divine names, are no longer subject to the cycle of worldly existence.
Salutations to Rāma, to Rāmabhadra, to Rāmacandra, the creator; to the Lord of the Raghus, the Protector, the husband of Sītā. || 40 ||
O Great Goddess, by chanting this mantra day and night, one becomes liberated from all sins and attains union with Viṣṇu. || 41 ||
Thus, O son of Gaṅgā, this majesty of Rāmacandra, which is in accordance with the Vedas, has been told to you, since you are indeed the best among the Vaiṣṇavas. 42.
We pay homage to Maheśāna, the breaker of Hara’s bow;
to the Joy of Janakī’s heart, the Sandalwood tree, the Delight of the Raghus. 43.
Thus ends the Śrī Rāmacandra Stavarāja in the Padyapurāṇa, within the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara.
Now follows the Śrī Rāma Kavaca.
Having meditated upon Rāma, who is dark as a blue lotus, with lotus-like eyes,
accompanied by Jānakī and Lakṣmaṇa, adorned with a crown of matted hair,
holding a sword, a quiver, a bow, and arrows in his hands, and the destroyer of night-stalkers.
The unborn and all-pervading Lord, who has manifested by his own divine play to protect the world.
The wise person should recite the Rāmarakṣā, which destroys sins and grants all desires.

Of this Śrī Rāma-kavaca, Budha Kauśika is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Śrī Rāmacandra is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of pleasing Śrī Rāmacandra during recitation. || 3 ||
Oṃ! May Rāghava protect my head; may the son of Daśaratha protect my forehead; may the descendant of Kauśalyā protect my eyes; and may the beloved of Viśvāmitra protect my ears. 4.
May the protector of sacrifices protect my nose; may he who is affectionate toward the son of Sumitrā protect my face;
may the treasury of knowledge protect my tongue; and may he who is saluted by Bharata protect my throat. || 5 ||
May he who possesses divine weapons protect my shoulders; may he who broke the bow of Bhaga protect my arms;
may the Lord of Sītā protect my hands; and may the conqueror of Paraśurāma protect my heart.
May the bearer of the headless trunk (Kabandha) protect the chest; may he who is praised by the gods protect the breasts;
may the Lord of the Kula protect the sides; and may the joy of the Ikṣvākus protect the belly. || 7 ||
May the destroyer of Khara protect my waist; may he who has Jāmbavān as his refuge protect my navel;
may the master of his senses protect my private parts; and may the best of the Raghus protect my back.
May the Lord of Sugrīva protect my waist; may the Master Hanumān protect my thighs;
and may the best of the Raghus, the destroyer of the race of Rākṣasas, protect my hips.
May he who made the knees bend protect the shanks; may the destroyer of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa protect the feet;
may the glorious Vibhīṣaṇa protect the two feet; and may Rāma protect the entire body.
Whosoever, being virtuous, recites this protection accompanied by the power of Rāma, shall become long-lived, happy, possessed of sons, victorious, and disciplined. (11)
Those who move through the netherworld, the earth, and the sky, and those who wander in disguise,
are not even able to look upon one protected by the names of Rāma.
By remembering [the Lord] as "Rāma," "Rāmabhadra," or "Rāmacandra," a person is not tainted by sins and attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 13 ||
For one who holds in their hand that which is protected by the name of Rāma—the sole mantra for conquering the world—all spiritual perfections (siddhis) remain within the palm of their hand. 14.
Whoever, having written this vidyā on birch bark smeared with fragrant sandalwood paste, wears it, shall obtain his desired fruit. || 15 ||
The woman who is barren like a crow, or she whose children have died, shall become one with many offspring and living children; of this there is no doubt. (16)
Whoever recites this armor of Rāma, known as the Vajrapañjara, shall have his commands unimpeded everywhere and obtain victory and auspiciousness. || 17 ||
Just as he had been instructed in his dream by Hari, the wise Kauśika wrote down this Rāmarakṣā upon waking in the morning. (18)
May both those heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa—archers with girded swords, wearing the side-locks of youth, and auspicious—protect me on the road. (19)
Young, endowed with beauty, delicate yet possessed of great strength,
with large eyes like white lotuses, they were clothed in bark garments and black antelope skins.
Subsisting on fruits and roots, self-controlled, ascetic, and practicing celibacy—these two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are the sons of Daśaratha. (21)
The two best of all archers, the refuge of all beings and the destroyers of the race of Rākṣasas— may those two foremost of the Raghus protect you.
May Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, with their bows strung and ready, touching the arrows, and accompanied by quivers containing inexhaustible shafts, always go before me on the path for my protection.
